articleTitle: A 2-Bit Dual-Polarization Reconfigurable Intelligent Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarization reconfigurable metasurface (DP-RIM) at 5G mid-band frequency of 3.3-3.8 GHz is described. The square meta-cell is deliberately designed in a symmetrical form with respect to principal axes, hence the RIM can be tuned independently using voltage-controlled varactor didoes. Whereas a dual 2-bit phase-coding method is used for a DC voltage of 0~10V, the equivalent cell-size is reduced and thus the reflection phases are changed in 4 levels. The proposed DP-RIM provides a new approach to wireless communications that can overcome the obstacles faced by the current 5G mid-band systems.

articleTitle: 274-GHz Substrate-Integrated-Waveguide Fed Rotman-Lens Multibeam Antenna Integrated in Multi-Layer Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multibeam antenna fed by a substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) Rotman-lens beam-forming network (BFN) was designed at 274 GHz. A Rotman lens and microstrip comb-line antennas are placed in the different layers within a single 7-layer substrate to reduce the 2D size to 11 mm × 10.5 mm. The simulated radiation patterns show that the proposed antenna achieves beam scanning over 80 degrees.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of QUBO Model for Radio Propagation Analysis with Quantum Annealing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: At present, QUBO model for radio propagation analysis has been proposed. The model is applicable to quantum annealing computer, so it can find radio propagation paths faster than conventional ray-tracing method. Here, the model consists of objective function and constraint conditions, and their balance is adjusted by the weight coefficients. This mean that the performance of the model depends on the setting of the weight coefficients. In this paper, suitable weight coefficients are examined.

articleTitle: Total Radiated Power Measurements of a mmWave Phased Array in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper explores the use of reverberation chambers for TRP measurements of beamformed radiation by phased arrays at mmWave frequencies. First, the received power was verified by the one-sample K-S GoF test to follow the exponential probability distribution. Different numbers of samples and stirrers’ positions were considered. Second, we showed that the effective number of independent samples is different depending on the number of samples and stirrers’ positions. Third, the beamforming TRP estimates are presented for all beams, analyzing the statistical significance of the observed differences with a selection of samplings.

articleTitle: Relationship between Reflector Size and Reflection Coefficient for 300 GHz Indoor Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the size of flat metal reflectors required for indoor wireless communications operating in the 300 GHz band. The dependence of the path length between the transmitter and receiver on the relationship between the reflector width and reflection coefficient was evaluated by simulation and measurement. The influence of the incident angle on the reflection area was also evaluated.

articleTitle: Composite Right/Left Handed Leaky Wave Antenna Using Complementary Omega Shape on Half Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) by using complementary omega slots to provide HMSIW Composite right/left handed (CRLH) Leaky wave antenna (LWA) is presented. Omega shaped slots provide the series capacitance required for the CRLH transmission line, whereas the vias on one side of the proposed structure provides the shunt inductance. The unit cell configuration has been analyzed and an array of eight-unit cells is used for presenting HMSIW CRLH LWA exhibiting continuous beam scanning from the angle -30 to 20 between the frequency range of 14.5 - 19 GHz.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband MIMO Antenna Array for mm-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes couple of ports MIMO antenna for the mm-Wave frequency for a 5G communication system. Each unit element of the recommended design measures 8 by 8 millimeters with a 0.8mm thickness and is implanted over the Roger RT/duroid 5870 substrate material. The suggested design's simple geometrical shape, small size, ultra-wideband, and high gain make it a potential choice for future wireless femtocell devices. The unit element was also used to produce a couple of port MIMO antennae for MIMO applications. A variety of performance metrics of the recommended MIMO antenna were also looked at using the electromagnetic simulation tool-based HFSS software package to show the potential of the proposed study.

articleTitle: New Equivalent Circuit of Rectangular Dumbbell-Shaped Defected Ground Structure with Ideal Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new equivalent circuit of a rectangular Dumbbell-shaped Defected Ground Structure (DGS) in parallel with a resistor. The design consists of a resistor (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf>) soldered in parallel with the DGS unit in the ground plane. The parameters of the proposed circuit are derived by applying the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf> into ideal transformer circuit has parallel resistance (R), inductance(L), and capacitance (C) as the properties. The result shows the greater accuracy of circuit to EM simulation if compared with other similar work. To confirm the validity of equivalent circuit, various simulation results from EM simulation are done to shows excellent agreement of the DGS unit in parallel with R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</inf> with corresponding to the proposed equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: Endfire Circularly Polarized Antenna for CubeSat/SmallSat applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents the design of a Circularly Polarized (CP) end-fire antenna at 8 GHz. Complementary magnetic and electric dipoles are used to generate the CP. A phase shifting line connects both the dipoles which provides the necessary phase shift to get proper CP. Taper section of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feed is used to excite the dipoles. The antenna has a broad beam width in the elevation plane and can find applications in small satellite TT&C application.

articleTitle: SIW Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna Using High-Order Radiation Modes for Broadband Applications in X Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents a compact SIW cavity-backed slot antenna design for X-band communication. The single-layer structure includes a rectangular radiating slot on the top layer and utilizes grounded coplanar waveguide feeding. By matching TE13 and TE32 mode impedances, the antenna achieves enhanced operating bandwidth and high gain. With an impedance bandwidth of 0.721 GHz (11.119 GHz to 11.84 GHz), resonance dips occur at 11.229 GHz (TE13) and 11.744 GHz (TE32), providing gains of 10.4 dBi and 8.11 dBi, respectively. The proposed design shows promise for its simplicity, broadband capability, and high gain in X-band applications.

articleTitle: Open Source Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for the Frequency Range of 5 GHz WiFi
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have been identified as a potential ingredient to enhance the performance of contemporary wireless communication and sensing systems. Yet, most of the existing devices are either costly or not available for reproduction. To close this gap, a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for the frequency range of 5 GHz WiFi is presented in this work. We describe the designed unit cell, which is optimized for the full frequency range of 5.15 to 5.875 GHz. Standard FR4 substrate is used for cost optimization. The measured reflection coefficient of a rectangular RIS prototype with 256 elements is used for RF performance evaluation. Fabrication data and firmware source code are made open source, which makes RIS more available in real measurement setups.

articleTitle: Broadband Waveguide Transitions and Loss Measurement Technique of Planar Transmission Lines in Millimeter-Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A transmission loss measurement technique of planar transmission lines is proposed in this work. The planar transmission line under test is terminated by broadband waveguide transitions at both ends. A waveguide jig is used to connect to standard waveguides. A probe station is not necessary to connect to a vector network analyzer. Developed various broadband planar-line-to-waveguide transitions for transmission line variation were summarized. The way to measure the transmission loss was introduced. Measurement in 300 GHz band was demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: Low-profile Multi-beam Lens Antenna with Corrugation to Suppress Surface Reflection of High-permittivity Material in 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile multi-beam lens antenna with corrugation formed on the lens surface to suppress the surface reflection due to the high-permittivity material. Low profile is achieved by the design of low focal-to-diameter (F/D) ratio and high permittivity material. Reflection on the lens surface is reduced by 1-dimensional corrugation for easy manufacturing. Multi-beam performance was obtained by feeding from horns arranged one-dimensionally as primary radiators. The gain improved by larger than 1.2 dB for multi-beam covering over a 30-degree angular range at 270 GHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Quad-polarization L-band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-cost L-band antenna with reconfigurable quad-polarization is presented. The antenna consists of four identical radiating elements. Each element comprises two stacked rectangular patches to achieve more than 10% bandwidth. Through proper phasing of the four elements, the antenna can realize two orthogonal linear polarizations and two circular polarizations. To demonstrate the concept, an antenna is realized using FR-4 substrate. The measured 10-dB input return loss bandwidth is 11%. And the measured 3-dB gain bandwidth is from 1.21 GHz to 1.36 GHz, with a maximum gain of 8.8 dBi for both linear polarization and circular polarization.

articleTitle: A Metamaterial-based Dual-band ±45° Phase Shifter for 5G Lower Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band ±45° phase shifting line miniaturized using metamaterial interdigital capacitor (IDC) is presented in this work. The branch of the conventional transmission line (TL) is replaced with a T-section TL using ABCD matrix analysis having –45° phase shift at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and +45° phase shift at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The proposed structure is compact and designed on the Rogers RT/Duroid substrate. The design achieved wide frequency ratio centered at sub-6 GHz 5G frequency bands of 0.7 GHz and 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Single-point feeding electrification of a circularly polarized MACKEY composed of three grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a model of a single point feeding of a circular braided wave MACKEY consisting of three grids was investigated. This model enables the simplification of the feeding circuit by consolidating the two excitation elements inside the substrate into a single excitation element.

articleTitle: A VHF-Band Printed Reconfigurable Dipole Antenna Based on Bistable Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a bistable material based on glass fiber reinforced resin matrix composites (GFRP) is used as the dielectric substrate of a printed dipole antenna to realize pattern reconfigurable characteristics. The proposed reconfigurable dipole antenna is symmetrical and can work at 100MHz. Its shape can be turned from straight into a circular conformal form. The antenna pattern can be reconfigured from the conventional "8" shape to an ellipse, forming approximate spherical shape radiation. Simulation results show that the antenna patterns can be reconfigured while remaining the resonance frequency unchanged, and the direction chart can be reconstructed. The proposed antenna can be applied to portable mobile communication terminals at the VHF frequency band.

articleTitle: High Gain Asymmetrical Branching Stub 1-D Combline Leaky Wave Antenna With Improved Backward To Forward Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Novel technique is presented eliminating the open stop band (OSB), which enables the antenna to scan through the broadside. The method is to introduce asymmetry in the structure. To introduce asymmetry in the 1-D combline periodic leaky wave antenna (PLWA): a rectangular stub is connected to another rectangular stub rotated at an angle θ° this structure is further connected to a microstrip fed line. The proposed 1-D PLWA shows OSB elimination, improvement in gain, and beam scanning. The proposed 1-D PLWA can achieve 16.2dbi peak gain and have a scanning range from -51° to +19°, bandwidth 6.1GHz -10.8GHz, its dimensions are 8.25λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×1.5λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Estimation Formula of UAV-BS Density for Required LOS Coverage in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The line-of-sight (LOS) probability in an urban environment assuming unmanned aerial vehicle base stations (UAV-BSs) is studied. We establish an estimation formula to calculate the minimum density of UAV-BSs required to achieve a certain LOS probability over an area.

articleTitle: Design of Cosecant Squared Pattern with Leaky Wave Antenna using Dielectric Image Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Leaky wave antenna radiating cosecant-squared pattern is proposed in this paper. We show that the directivity of a leaky wave antenna with dielectric image lines can be easily changed by the shift of the first metal strip for the grating waveguide to obtain a cosecant-squared pattern.

articleTitle: Development of Multi-Polarization Triangular Microstrip Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multi-polarization capability is proposed to deal with the depolarization issue in the propagation channel. The reconfiguration capability is expected to maintain the polarization matching between the received wave orientation and the antenna polarization. The proposed antenna array, which is designed to operate at the frequency of 3.5 GHz, consists of four triangular microstrip elements arranged circularly in an angular distance of 90°. The progressive phase difference and switching mechanism are applied to reconfigure the polarization of the antenna array. Simulation and measurement are carried out to investigate the performance of the proposed method and configuration. The results show that the proposed antenna array can produce two linear and two circular polarizations.

articleTitle: A Compact UHF RFID Tag Antenna for Soil Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: UHF RFID technology is currently being chosen to replace the existing soil monitoring system for smart agriculture. However, when attached to backing objects, the current RFID tag typically has a large footprint and a short read distance. Therefore, this paper introduces a compact tag antenna design comprising a slotted radiating patch connected to a ground plane via an inductive stub. The tag antenna is mounted on loamy soil for soil monitoring purposes. The proposed tag has a small size of only 48.2×48.2 mm, a power transmission coefficient of 0.99, and a longer theoretical read range of 9m.

articleTitle: Comparison Study of Ring Resonator Shape for Multiband IRS Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a performance comparison study between two shapes of ring resonators for intelligent reflector surface (IRS) application. The ring resonator shapes used for a multiband reflector are circular and hexagonal shape. Utilizing a multiring resonator design, a multiband reflector is simulated by using CST Software, and the RO5880 substrate is used as the dielectric substrate for both ring shapes. The simulated result is shown in S-parameters and a reflection phase graph to present the reflector performance of each shape. Based on the simulated results, the circular shape has a slightly better performance, wider bandwidth, and reflected power percentage compared to the hexagonal shape.

articleTitle: Double Layer Fractal FSSs for 5G Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As the global popularity of fifth-generation (5G) telecommunication systems increases, so does the need for electromagnetic (EM) shielding rises. For such requirements, frequency selective surfaces (FSS) arise as a possible solution. This paper presents a fractal frequency selective surface (FSS) design for sub 6 GHz 5G bands that provide tri-bands on 1.5 GHz, 3.5 GHz, and 5.5 GHz frequencies. The second-order Sierpinski gasket fractal is taken as the unit cell FSS element. The simulated results of the proposed FSSs design are capable of getting wider bandwidths and minimum attenuation at these three-stop band 5G signals for electromagnetic (EM) shielding applications.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Transmitarray With Linear-To-Linear Polarization Conversion Function
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a three-layered transmitarray with linear-to-linear polarization conversion operating in 5G N257 band. The potential application of transmitarray is served as an amplify-and-forward repeater with polarization conversion dealing with polarization mismatch and high path loss. The simulated results show that the TAA possesses a high gain of 30.1 dBi, satisfactory polarization conversion with cross polarization discrimination (XPD) of 26.6 dB, and the gain bandwidth almost covering the N257 frequency range.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing-Based Global Optimization for Multipole RF Cavity Filter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents a simulated annealing optimization technique for tuning a RF cavity filter. In this study, Two types of 5th-order Chebyshev bandpass filter have been considered: one with a frequency range of 0.84 to 1.07 GHz and another with a frequency range of 0.72 to 0.95 GHz. The result shows that the optimized S-parameter pattern matching the desired bandpass and satisfied the target passband of -15dB less. The objective function is minimized during the iteration, confirming the effectiveness of the simulated annealing optimization algorithm for tuning RF filters and enabling filter designs that meet the system requirements. The proposed technique can find the optimal filter characteristics in the frequency domain using S-parameter and allows for global optimization search. The validity of the proposed method was confirmed through computer simulation.

articleTitle: Design Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna Array for D-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) based antenna design working at a frequency of the D-band. The single-element antenna design has a matching bandwidth of 11.75% and a gain of 3.036 dBi. Antenna array configurations of 2, 4, and 8 elements are evaluated in terms of gain and bandwidth. The simulation results showed that the 2-element array configuration had a matching bandwidth of 13.41% with an antenna gain of 7.04 dBi. The 4-element array configuration had a matching bandwidth of 13.01% with an antenna gain of 9.31 dBi. Finally, the 8-element array configuration had a matching bandwidth of 13.23% with an antenna gain of 11.6 dBi. From the results obtained, increasing the number of elements of the antenna will increase the gain and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna Composed of Double-Shell Halo Antenna and Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents, compact wideband orthogonal polarized omnidirectional antenna. The proposed antenna is the combination of a Halo antenna with double-shell structure and a dipole antenna. The antenna characteristics are clarified by the simulation. To improve the directivity deviation between both polarizations, this antenna is loaded with two short elements on the opposite side of the aperture of the Halo antenna and parasitic element so as not to contact each other. As a result of the simulation, the characteristics of the proposed antenna are that the relative bandwidth is 9.0%, and the antenna height and diameter are 0.46λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 0.14λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> the wavelength of the center operational frequency), respectively.

articleTitle: Characterizing Rail Sweep with Radar Target Identification Using Matrix Pencil Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the radar target identification system for investigation of the characteristics of defective rail. The BS100A rails with various sweep angles are modeled by using CST microwave studio. A Gaussian pulse is transmitted to the defected rail to measure the time-domain response. A matrix pencil method (MPM) is used to extract poles including the damping factor and natural frequency from the late-time portion of the time-domain response. An estimation of the sweep angles of the defective rail using the 2nd-order polynomial curve fitting is analyzed. From these simulation results, the extracted poles can characterize subsoil with different electrical properties. From the simulation results, the extracted poles can characterize defective rails with different sweep angles. The final results confirm the superiority of the proposed system over the conventional one using visual inspection.

articleTitle: Broadband GCPW-to-Waveguide Transition in Multi-Layer Dielectric Substrate with Double Patch and Corrugation Structures in 275 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW)-to-waveguide transition in a multi-layer dielectric substrate covering the 250-290 GHz band was developed in this study. This transition consists of a GCPW line inserted from the broad wall of the waveguide that excites a double rectangular stacked patch located at the waveguide center. The corrugation structures are applied at the edges of the aperture on the middle layer. Broadband operation is achieved by using a double patch, corrugation structures, and a cavity formed by the via-hole arrangement surrounding apertures patterned in a multi-layer substrate. The transition geometries are optimized by electromagnetic simulation using a finite element method. The bandwidth of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> below -10 dB of the proposed transition was 49.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Planar Beam-Tilt Array for Primary Radiators of CubeSat-Onboard Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A primary radiator for cube-satellite (CubeSat) onboard reflectarray antenna is designed. To avoid blocking by the primary radiator, a planar beam-tilt array is designed and composed of an eight-element slot array antenna on a printed circuit board. The dimensions of the radiating elements, element spacing and excitation phase are adjusted and a desired radiation patterns are obtained.

articleTitle: Array Layouts for Regularized Zero Forcing Massive MIMO: Sum Rate vs. Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: First, we show that an array antenna thinned for maximum ergodic sum rate in regularized zero forcing massive MIMO single-cell systems comes with an increased average peak sidelobe level (PSLL). Then, we propose a new hybrid-beamforming-based array layout that achieves PSLLs comparable with a conventional half-wavelength-spaced full-digital-array, while using as few RF chains as the thinned array.

articleTitle: Estimation of undersea localization using electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We consider using electromagnetic waves in seawater suitable for use in shallow water areas because the loss due to seawater is significant, and communication is faster than acoustic waves, although at short distances. Then, we are investigating an underwater position estimation system using electromagnetic waves. The location of divers and AUVs is essential in a broader range of scenarios. This paper presents the underwater position estimation principle and actual estimation results to show the technique's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Multi-Dimension Feature Learning of Radar Echoes for HFSWR Maritime Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The dynamically changing ionospheric condition seriously limits the detection performance of High-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR). In order to identify the covered targets, we separately extract the feature information from phase and time-frequency dimension of different echo components. Then, different dimension features are applied for training the corresponding deep learning networks. When the label results of a radar echo from different trained models are the same, final result of this echo is obtained, in addition, when they are different, this echo information will be added into the training dataset for the next training. Finally, we will find the covered targets under the F-layer specular reflection ionosphere clutter.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of Reconfigurable Array Using Effective Media Properties of Unit-Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of an effective medium-based approach to analyse antenna simulations with reconfigurable metasurfaces or other periodic structures. It is shown that the effective properties of unit cells are unusable above resonance. Hence, it is proposed to use unit cells with a higher resonance frequency than the required operating frequency. Antenna simulations with a reconfigurable metasurface and with effective media are found to be in good agreement, and the latter is found to be faster.

articleTitle: Scanning Spot Beam Reflectarray Antenna with Dual-Polarization Stacked Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The multi-beam method, which covers a service area with multiple beams, is applied to reflectarray antennas. By controlling the beam direction according to polarization and frequency, a desired area can be covered even with a small number of mirrors. In this paper, a new element shape suitable for scanning spot beams is proposed to improve the gain reduction that occurred in a previous study. The validity of the proposed element was verified using electromagnetic field analysis of a reflectarray antenna with the proposed element.

articleTitle: An Overview on Nature Inspired Planar Broadband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an overview on planar broadband antennas whose radiator has nature-inspired geometry. The natural leaves and flower petals have curved boundaries and multiple segments. These features of nature-inspired geometries are advantageous to get closely spaced multiple resonances hence broadband characteristics when arranged in specific antenna configuration and optimized properly. A case study on recently developed flower- and leaf-shaped planar monopole antennas for broad frequency range is given in this paper. In addition, some of the nature-inspired antennas are analyzed through surface current distribution which helps to understand the fundamental relation of operating frequency and active element of antenna.

articleTitle: Multi-sector Yagi-Uda Antenna for 28GHz Indoor Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 12-sector antenna is presented for 28GHz indoor base station, consisting of printed Yagi-Uda antennas fed through integrated coplanar balun. Two branches for MIMO antenna are provided by arranging alternately Yagi-Uda antenna for both vertical and horizontal polarization in every 30º above the ground plane. The design of an antenna element and a balun is described and a prototype multi-sector antenna is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Applications of Measured Antennas as Field Sources in Numerical Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The utilization of measured antennas as field sources in numerical simulations is a well-established method for investigating performances of deployed antennas on large platforms. This approach is particularly valuable in situations were conducting a measurement or a full-wave simulation of both the antenna and platform is either impractical or unattainable. A prime example of such a scenario is the placement of antennas on satellites and vehicles. In these cases, the antennas are often provided by a third party, making it unlikely that the necessary mechanical and electronic characteristics required to create a comprehensive full-wave model are available.To enable the study of antenna placement on complex platforms using standard Computational Electromagnetic (CEM) tools, the antenna can be effectively characterized by a Huygens box derived from an equivalent current expansion of the measured antenna. In this paper, we will outline the derivation of the Huygens box representation from antenna measurements and demonstrate how the source representation can be employed in the full-wave simulation of both the antenna and the platform. The technique will be illustrated and supported by practical examples based on measured data, with particular attention to an array antenna.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of Wave Propagation in Sandstone Cave
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Effective communication in caves is crucial for rescuers during accidents or disasters. Previous studies have investigated wave propagation in tunnels and limestone caves. This paper presents an experimental study of wave propagation in a sandstone cave at Wat Tham Patihan Cave in Thailand, covering the MF to UHF bands in both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios. The study aims to investigate the behavior of waves while traveling in the sandstone cave. The study found that in LOS, the path loss decreases with higher frequencies, contrary to the propagation theory in free space. Since waves traveling in a cave behave like they are in a dielectric-walled waveguide. In NLOS, the path loss in the L-Bend range at low frequencies was lower than that at high frequencies due to the ability to reflect, diffract, and encounter obstructions. In contrast, at 350 kHz, a high attenuation is caused by the skin effect when the wave travels through the arc, penetrating the cave wall. The study results will aid in developing communication systems and antennas for use in caves.

articleTitle: Low-Sidelobe Series-Fed Microstrip Antenna Array of 32×4 for K-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a K-Band series-fed microstrip antenna array with 32×4 elements, having a measured beam-width of 20°×3°. Both the E-plane and H-plane are section-wise impedance-matched for power distribution in the series-fed structures. The desired amplitude distribution and sidelobe levels for E and H plane of less than −30 dB and −20 dB respectively. The designed antenna structure has a good impedance matching in the required band of 24.0 GHz to 24.3 GHz. The max realised gain of 27 dBi in the bore-sight direction has been measured in the far field antenna setup. The proposed antenna offers a low profile, low side-lobes level, and highly directivity, making it valuable for portable radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: Beam-scanning Performance of 2×2 Shaped Lens Array Antenna in 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we developed a high-gain 2 x 2 phased lens array antenna with a combination of mechanical and electrical beam scanning. The square-bottom plano-convex (Sq-PC) planar lens array provides higher aperture efficiency compared to the conventional circular lens array. The combination of plano-convex (PC) lens shape and square-bottom lens extension helps to maintain higher gain during beam scanning than concave-convex (CC) lens shape. The proposed scanning lens phased array achieved boresight gain with 34.8 dBi and high-gain beam scanning ≥ 31.5 dBi towards 24° at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Double Square Loop Single Layer Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) for Wideband Absorption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research presents a planar rectangular microwave absorber with double square loops in relation to a frequency selective surface (FSS). The suggested absorber is extremely effective, small in size, and contributes to widespread absorption outside of the x-band. A single layer substrate (RT5880) with a single layer (FSS) featuring double square loops is used to design the suggested structure. The suggested design’s working absorption bandwidth ranges from 10.21-40.5GHz, or 30.32GHz.

articleTitle: Planar Four-Port Dipole MIMO Antenna for 5G NR 257/258/261 Frequency Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband planar dipole antenna that is extended as a 4-port MIMO antenna having linked ground planes is proposed for fifth-generation (5G) NR band applications. The broadband is attained by feeding the proposed dipole antenna through a Balun that serves the purpose of ensuring impedance matching across a wide range of frequencies. The |S11|<-10 dB of single antenna spans from 27.93% (23.62-31.29 GHz). Even with the linked ground, the MIMO antenna displayed decent isolation with Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) < 0.02. The antenna has great potential owing to the low profile, omnidirectional radiation pattern, satisfactory MIMO performance, and covers the majority of the 5G NR 257/258/261 frequency bands.

articleTitle: Dual-Wideband – Linearly and Circularly Polarized C-Band Antenna for VSAT Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: C-Band VSAT is one of telecommunication infrastructure that is suitable for a tropical archipelago country because it has wide range and more resistant towards rain attenuation. This paper proposed a C-Band horn antenna design as feeder for VSAT antenna with characteristic dual polarization – linear and circular, and dual wideband. The antenna design combines and modifies conical and corrugated horn with septum perturbation. The proposed antenna has achieved a working frequency downlink at 3.7 to 4.2 GHz and uplink at 5.925 to 6.425 GHz. The antenna beamwidth varies from 22.3 until 38.4 degree and can achieve a gain of 18.30 dB.

articleTitle: A Planar Monopulse-Beam Steering Antenna With Wide Field-of-View for Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna design for electronically steering monopulse beams at wide angles. Unlike conventional monopulse antennas, the proposed one employs the inner two antennas to steer a deep null, while other antennas are used to produce a directive beam. The modification offers high efficiency and wide-angle monopulse scanning without ambiguities, which is suitable for indoor localization. The proposed antenna has the reflection coefficients of Σ and Δ ports better than −10 dB in 22% fractional bandwidth. The Σ and Δ patterns have a beam width and sharp angular resolution of 25° and 1° at 4.9 GHz, respectively, offering accurate direction-finding.

articleTitle: Low Profile Dual-Band Base Station Antenna Array Decoupled by Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, by using electromagnetic transparent antenna (ETA) and artificial magnetic conductor (AMC), the cross-band coupling and in-band coupling between low-band (LB) antenna and high-band (HB) antennas are significantly reduced. The profile of the LB antenna can be reduced by making use of the in-phase reflection characteristic of AMC. As for HB antennas, AMC can work as antenna decoupling surface (ADS). Due to the electromagnetic transparency of LB antenna, the HB radiation patterns are restored. With VSWR better than 1.5, the co-polarized and cross-polarized in-band couplings are reduced by about 8 dB and 9dB respectively.

articleTitle: A Design of Microstrip Antenna With Ellipse Metasurface for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A design of a microstrip antenna with an ellipse metasurface is presented in this paper. The antenna construction comprises two layers of substrate. A square radiating with corner truncation on the bottom layer and an ellipse metasurface on the top layer. The ellipse metasurface is rotating 45 degrees by the y-axis. The simulated result of impedance bandwidth is 410 MHz. Meanwhile, the simulated result of gain is 8 dBic at 3.5 GHz. Based on the simulation results, the antenna design could be employed for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of Center Radiation Slot for Radial Line Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To enhance the degree of freedom for radiation pattern of radial line slot antenna (RLSA), we propose attaching a center radiation slot. In this study, we developed a procedure for attaching a center radiation slot to the RLSA. We created two types of center slots: ring-shaped and cross-shaped. Both exhibited good characteristics in terms of the rotation mode, coupling, and reflection of the radial line in wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Metamaterial Inspired 1×4 Linear Antenna Array With Beam-Forming Network For 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of a linear 1×4 antenna array using metamaterials (MTM) for 5G applications. The array consists of four single-element MTM-UWB antennas fed by a beamforming network (BFN) based on an MTM-inspired Butler matrix (BM). The proposed design was simulated using CST Microwave Studio and operates within the frequency range of 2.8GHz-4.05GHz (1.25 GHz) with a return-loss of less than -10dB. By exciting different input ports of the BM, the main beam of the antenna array can be steered in four different directions: -165°, -40°, +40°, and +165°. The results demonstrate that the proposed design is well-suited for 5G applications.

articleTitle: α-β Filter With Optimal Filtering Noise Suppression Ratio Under Constant Prediction Steady State Error
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design method for an α-β tracking filter that optimizes the filtering noise reduction ratio required for display while maintaining the predictive steady state error required for radar tracking. This filter gain equation is derived, and theoretically verified that the proposed method provides the smaller noise reduction compared with the conventional method, while maintain the same predictive steady state error.

articleTitle: Reflection Coefficient Variation based on the Configuration of Integrated Antenna and Reflecting Surface at 3.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work offers a low profile, and enhanced microstrip patch antenna for 5G and Wi-Max applications. The proposed design is based on a patch antenna embedded with reflective surface metamaterial consisting of an array of 5 × 5 elements. The simulated and measured of S11 has been observed to determine its performance. The advancement of Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) evolution known as Reflective Surface (RS) metamaterial has been adopted to integrate with the patch antenna. This design has a small size of 107 mm × 107 mm. Furthermore, it has been integrated with the microstrip patch antenna under two different configurations which provides a variation performance antenna in terms of reflection coefficient for both configuration 1 and configuration 2, at the operating frequency of 3.5 GHz. For configuration 1, no significant changes have been observed. While in configuration 2, the resonant frequency of the patch antenna has been shifted up and down with the best S11 is -40dB at 3.4 GHz

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Ferrite and Amorphous Shielding Materials for NFC Tag Antenna on Metal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper compares ferrite and amorphous sheets as shielding materials for NFC tag antennas on metal surfaces. The presence of metal surface poses challenges to NFC communication, impacting the reading of the tag. Effective shielding materials are necessary to mitigate these challenges. Experimental evaluations are conducted to assess the performance of the NFC tag antenna in terms of signal strength, inductance, and reading range in the presence of ferrite and amorphous materials. The results demonstrate significant enhancements in signal strength when utilizing ferrite material compared to amorphous material. However, amorphous materials offer the advantage of lower thickness, enabling broader application possibilities.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of A Dual-Band Microstrip Antenna with Tunable Frequency Characteristics Based on Varactor Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental evaluation of a dual-band microstrip antenna which has tunable frequency characteristics. The tunable characteristics of the proposed antenna offer the advantage to tune the operating frequency at the desired one without altering geometry or dimensions of the antenna. To achieve a dual-band microstrip antenna with these characteristics, four varactor diodes are involved into the design to influence the resonant frequency of antenna. Prototype of the proposed microstrip antenna is then realized for experimental evaluation. The measurement results demonstrate that the prototype resonates within the frequency range of 0.83 GHz to 1.2 GHz when the DC voltage across the varactor diodes is increased from 0 V to 12 V.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Various Geometries on Tri-Band Antenna Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)

authors.preferredName: Mohd Adzimnuddin Bin Mohd Nor Azami

abstract: A triband antenna that has difference geometry is studied for wireless communication. The study of the transitional structure is studied by maintaining the other design parameter. The simulation of the triband antenna can generate the frequency at 1.73 GHz, 2.33 GHz and 2.74 GHz and have a frequency gap by 400 MHz. Most of the radiation pattern is in bi-directional. The simulated gain is 1.49 dB, 1.25 dB and 0.91 dB respectively.

articleTitle: Diffraction from Impedance Wedge: Case Study Nonphysical Pole Suppression from Maliuzhinets Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a study on the non-physical poles of the Maliuzhinets (MZ) solution for diffraction from an impedance wedge under oblique incident conditions. The objective of this study is to simplify the MZ solution by suppressing these non-physical poles. The findings reveal that the accuracy of the MZ solution, without one or two nonphysical poles, is highly satisfactory. However, it is worth noting that the accuracy is significantly compromised, particularly in the case of cross-polarization, when the O-face of a right-angle wedge is a Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC).

articleTitle: A Study on Spreading Reflectarray Antenna for Eliminating Blind Spots in Millimeter-Wave Band Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose the use of a spreading reflectarray to eliminate blind spots in millimeter-wave band communications. The reflectarray consists of patch elements arranged alternately at half-wavelength intervals, with reflection phases in opposite phases, effectively satisfying the end-fire condition. Through a two-dimensional simulation using a 20-element linear array, we demonstrate that 60 GHz signals can propagate successfully even when obstructed by a screen.

articleTitle: Compact Slotted Heptagonal UWB Textile-Based SNG Metamaterial for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact slotted heptagonal Ultrawideband (UWB) textile-based SNG (Single-Negative) metamaterial unit cell with truncated ground plane for breast cancer detection is presented in this paper. The overall dimensions of 30x30x3.34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, covering a bandwidth of range between 1 and 15 GHz is obtained. MNZ (Mu-Near-Zero) and ENG (Epsilon-Negative) characteristics exhibited by the proposed MTM provides an effective platform for breast cancer detection.

articleTitle: Development of RF coils for low-field portable MRI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To realize a comprehensive community care system in a super-aging society, regular acquisition of medical imaging information is desirable in the community and home environment for preventive and preliminary diagnosis. MRI is suitable in community medicine because of the high soft tissue contrast and no exposure to radiation. MRI using permanent magnet arrays (PMA) has recently been considered an appropriate modality. PMA has a nonlinear magnetic field gradient, and its static field strength is weaker than conventional MRI. Therefore, the RF coil used in PMA-based MRI must have broadband characteristics and low resistance. In this study, we adopted a cylindrical structure for the RF coil, and the optimal combination of parameters was obtained by analyzing several models with different shapes. We fabricated and measured RF coils using these parameters and investigated fabrication feasibility and error factors.

articleTitle: Tensile Damage Assessment on Carbon Fiber Reinforced Laminate for 45 ° and 90 ° Layout Orientation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Damage assessment is an important criteria to determine properties and characteristic for any material. The diversity of fiber orientation and production method are among the source of uncertainty in the behavior of carbon fiber composite product. The effort to study the effect of carbon fiber layout orientation on layout orientation of 45 ° and 90 ° to the tensional force was investigated in this study. The specimen was fabricated using single vacuum bagging method from the carbon fiber reinforced prepreg to produce carbon fiber reinforcement laminate (CFRL). The damage assessment using scanning electron microscope (SEM) to investigate closely the fiber and matrix fracture after breakage to find the correlation with the acoustic emission (AE) failure features.

articleTitle: Bow-tie-Shaped Rotated Yagi Antenna with Dual Circular Polarization for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a bow-tie-shaped rotated stacked Yagi antenna with dual-circular polarization (CP). The proposed antenna consists of four elements with different angle: a director, a reflector, and two orthogonal driven elements, and all antenna elements are designed in a bow-tie-shape. The two driven elements connected with LC balun. Each stacked element, except for the two driven elements, is equally rotated at an angle of 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup> based on the driven elements, resulting in the proposed antenna having dual-circular polarizations. A driven element located at the top of substrate forms right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), while the other forms left-hand circular polarization (LHCP). The antenna size is 0.39λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.39λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.27λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 2.45 GHz. The simulated -10dB bandwidth, 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and maximum gain of RHCP and LHCP are 6.2% / 5.3% and 3.1% / 2.6%, and 4.6 dBic / 4.4 dBic, respectively.

articleTitle: Fabrication and measurement of an antenna radiating polarization parallel to a substrate in a direction perpendicular to a side surface of the substrate for millimeter-wave radar board
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a reflector-backed dipole antenna embedded in a substrate for 79 GHz band radar application. The antenna radiates in a direction perpendicular to a side surface of the substrate with polarization parallel to a substrate main surface. From a viewpoint of manufacturing cost, radar boards are often composites of low-loss substrates for high-frequency bands and general-purpose substrates such as flame-retardant type 4 (FR-4). The asymmetric structure of the composite substrate in the thickness direction deteriorates the radiation pattern in the plane parallel to the thickness direction. By removing the FR-4 substrate below the antenna, the degradation of the radiation pattern is mitigated. In this paper, the design and the measured results of the proposed antenna are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Improvement of Line Availability of 300-GHz-band Wireless Fronthaul Links during Local Downpour by Switching Routing in Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigated the improvement of the connection ratio between RAUs and central station during a local downpour for 300 GHz band wireless fronthaul link by switching routing in mesh network. When we set one central station in mesh network, the connection ratio between the RAUs and the central station during the local downpour was 40 %. In case of two central station in mesh network, we clustered RAUs and the clusters with the second and third highest number of RAUs are selected. By setting the RAUs with highest betweeness centrality and cut points for each selected cluster as the central station, the connection ratio between RAUs and the central stations could be improved to 77.2 % during the local downpour.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized High Gain 4-Port MIMO Antenna Configuration for mm-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a small 4-Port Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna system. DGS structures are utilized along with the main radiators to achieve the desired performance. Through simulation, we demonstrate that the proposed design achieves operating impedance bandwidth of 3.49GHz, spanning from 27GHz to 30.49GHz, while maintaining a minimum port isolation of -18dB at 28GHz. Within this functional bandwidth, the antenna attains a peak gain of 7.01dBi at 27GHz and 28GHz, making it suitable for handheld 5Gmm-wave applications.

articleTitle: A Metalized Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Millimeter Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultra-wide band, circularly polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) fed by a coaxial probe has been designed here for millimeter wave 5G frequency band applications. The DRA has achieved a wide bandwidth from 25.20 GHz to 48.20 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 23 GHz. The polarization bandwidth of 0.37 GHz and 0.46 GHz is achieved within the frequency band of 46.88 GHz to 47.25 GHz and 48.4 GHz to 48.86 GHz respectively. The frequency resonance occurs at frequencies 25.62 GHz, 29.14 GHz, 32.88 GHz, 39.96 GHz, and 45.08 GHz with an average gain of 6 dBi uniformly over the defined frequency band. The wide impedance bandwidth is generated by using a circular metallic patch over the surface of the DRA. The DRA designed here is right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) and is excited with mode TEx21. The coaxial probe feed is used to excite the DRA at the desired resonating frequency of 26 GHz under its characteristic’s mode. The wide impedance bandwidth with circular polarization characteristics makes this antenna more suitable for millimeter wave frequency bands which covers all the frequency bands of 5G at millimeter wave in the band 30 GHz and band 40 GHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Fractal CDRA for Enhanced Mobile Broadband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel Fractal Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna (F-CDRA) is designed and investigated for enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) applications. Semicylindrical portions are etched and added in an iterative manner to broaden the DRA length. The proposed F-CDRA comprises a fractal DRA, a tapered feedline, and a Defective Ground structure (DGS). This feed line with DGS results in the super wideband behavior of the DRA. The proposed DRA provides an impedance bandwidth of 28.1 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 160% and has a gain of 6.86 dBi. It also offers a radiation efficiency of 98.6% and has omnidirectional radiation characteristics which makes it a perfect fit for eMBB applications including 5G millimeter waves.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Metasurfaces for 5G-and-beyond Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces the latest designed electromagnetic metasurfaces at the Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) for 5G-and-beyond networks. Various technologies and metasurfaces at different frequency ranges were developed to solve the drawbacks related to metasurfaces such as the limited bandwidth and Non-line-of-sight (NLoS) coverage issues.

articleTitle: A Simple Approach for Equivalent Circuits of Microstrip Bend and Tee Discontinuity Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a simple approach to find the equivalent circuits of microstrip bend and Tee discontinuity elements which are widely used in microwave circuits. In order to find the equivalent circuit elements, S-parameters obtained through electromagnetic (EM) simulation and simple network analysis theory are adopted instead of conventional difficult electromagnetic equations and/or numerical methods. The EM simulated S-parameters of bend and Tee elements are converted into Z-parameters. Simple network analysis theories are applied to the Z-parameters for finding the equivalent circuit elements. The calculated S-parameters of the extracted equivalent circuits are in good agreement with EM simulation. In addition, the measured S-parameters, which agree well with simulation, are presented to verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Transmission-Reflection-Array Using Magnetoelectric Dipole Elements in X-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, a reconfigurable transmission-reflection-array (TRA) operating in X-band is investigated, which combines the functionalities of the reconfigurable transmittarray and reflectarray. A receiver-transmitter structure with magneto-electric (ME) dipoles integrated with two PIN diodes is designed as the wideband TRA element. Due to the separated direct-current (DC) path that can independently control the states of two diodes with the bias voltage from a field-programmable gate array (FPGA), elements achieve the 1-dB insertion loss bandwidth covering the X-band and 1-bit phase resolution both of the transmitted and reflected waves. Then, a reconfigurable TRA with 16*16 elements is designed to verify its beamforming ability. The simulated results show that the proposed TRA enables manipulation of the reflected and transmitted wave-front, allowing for full-space control of the EM wave-front.

articleTitle: Human Body Blockage Effects on Personal Exposimeter Device in 4G/5G Frequency Bands for Epidemiological Research on Children’s Health
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Due to the spread of smartphones and other wireless devices, and the decline in the age of starting to use these devices, children are increasingly exposed to RF-EMF. Therefore, it is required to conduct epidemiological research about the effect on children’s health and RF exposure in the general environment. In this study, we precisely estimate the effects of human body blockage on personal exposure assessment tools in frequency bands, including 5G, using the FDTD method to investigate the dosimetry protocol for epidemiologic research.

articleTitle: Broadband measurement of insertion loss of FCCL directly metallized on modified Polyimide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper proposes a broadband design and measurement of insertion loss (IL) based on direct metallized polyimide for Flexible Copper-Clad Laminate (FCCL), a crucial foundational material for a variety of applications such as mobile devices, wearable electronics, and point-of-biosensors. We designed a grounded coplanar waveguide transmission line as our measurement fixture with a transition line at the two end port connector in order to reduce impedance mismatch. This model was implemented in an HFSS simulator. A multiline through-reflect-line (TRL) calibration and de-embedding technique were applied to obtain accurate pure response S-parameters of the device under test (DUT). The results obtained from both techniques showed a high degree of agreement with each other in the frequency range from 0.1 to 67 GHz.

articleTitle: Impact of Radio Wave Frequency on Heartbeat Radar Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of radio frequency on the performance of heartbeat radar. Especially, the heartrate accuracy over the various radio frequencies, i.e., from 2 GHz to 40 GHz, was experimentally tested under the equal condition. Experimental results revealed that the heartbeat detection performance does not have obvious frequency dependency over the tested frequency band.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition of Millimeter-wave Radar Based on DRCNet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The use of radar for human activity recognition has the characteristics of not being affected by external factors such as illumination and protecting user privacy, and millimeter wave radar as an important sensor has been widely used in attitude recognition. Based on this, a Doppler and Range decision-level Convergence Network model (DRCNet) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the common human activity data is collected by millimeter wave radar, the doppler-time plot and range-time plot are obtained by preprocessing the original data. Then the convolutional neural network is built according to the characteristics of the generated human activity data set, and finally the final recognition result is output by decision-level convergence. The experimental results show that the recognition accuracy of DRCNet is improved compared with other models. The collected human activity can be effectively identified, and the recognition accuracy reaches 93.00%.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Quasi-Isotropic Antenna Based on Split Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An electrically small antenna (ESA), which is based on split ring resonators (SRRs), with quasi-isotropic coverage is developed and investigated. This quasi-isotropic antenna is comprised of two orthogonally arranged SRRs and a circular holding tray to support the antenna structure. Each SRR possesses a quasi-isotropic radiation characteristic for the whole space with a gain variation about 3 dB. This feature is attributed to the equivalent electric and magnetic dipoles for the SRR. The isotropic radiation pattern is achieved by the combination of them. Through the combination of the two linearly polarized SRR, the final antenna could realize the circularly polarized characteristic in the maximum radiation direction. This proposed antenna exhibits an electrically small size (0.19 × 0.15 × 0.15 λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, ka = 0.89), and a radiation efficiency higher than 90% with a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 1.6% at the center frequency of 748.5 MHz. Additionally, the simulated realized gain differences of the quasi-isotropic ESA is 2.77 dB, which reveals that the antenna has a consistent quasi-isotropic coverage of the whole space.

articleTitle: Miniaturized CPW Fed Open End Ring Slot Antenna for Broadband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized open-end ring slot antenna is designed for broadband applications. The antenna is fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) line. This configuration has 82.8% impedance bandwidth (IMBW) (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ -10 dB) from 2.92 to 7.05 GHz. The designed prototype is uni-planar with a small size of 0.27λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.29λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency in free space). The antenna has a peak gain of 3 dBi.

articleTitle: Analytical Derivation of Reactance Time Function Generating Multiplexed Antenna Patterns for Two-element ESPAR Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we derive a time-based reactance function to generate an antenna pattern consisting of two different patterns for a two-element Electronically Steerable Passive Array Radiator (ESPAR) antenna. The patterns can construct two distinct patterns to exploit space diversity with a single connecting cable to receivers, resulting in reduced antenna space compared to conventional array antennas.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of a SFCW Software- Defined Radar System for Target Detection: Varying Distances Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental analysis of a stepped-frequency continuous wave (SFCW) software-defined radar (SDR) system. The system utilizes a USRP N210 with WBX daughterboard, a standard gain horn antenna, a waveguide antenna, and a personal computer. Operating with a bandwidth of 560 MHz, a frequency step size of 20 MHz, and 28 steps, the system's performance is evaluated through range profile analysis. Experimental trials involve transmitting SFCW signals and collecting corresponding echoes for target responses at distances of 0.7 meters, 0.9 meters, and 1.25 meters. The analysis of the range profile reveals distinct target signatures, demonstrating the system's effectiveness for target detection at varying distances.

articleTitle: Parasitic Beam Steering Antenna loaded with Shorting Vias
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a beam steering patch antenna with two parasitic elements loaded with shorting vias. The proposed antenna consists of a circular driven patch and two circular parasitic elements placed adjacent to the driven patch (upper left and below right). The mutual coupling effect between both driven and parasitic has managed to steer the beam. The parasitic elements electrically shorten the ground plane through shorting vias. ON state condition indicates the activation of the parasitic elements which required a shorting vias connected to the ground plane and vice versa. Based on the ON/OFF state of the shorting vias loaded parasitic elements, the proposed antenna able to steer the main beam to different directions to -7°, 0°, 5° and 12° at the resonant frequency of 3.5 GHz with maximum gain of 7.73 dBi.

articleTitle: Dual Band CPW Pentagonal Island with Modified Sierpinski Gasket Structure at 3.5 GHz and 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a dual-band pentagonal island antenna is proposed for WiMAX 3.5 GHz and WLAN 5.8 GHz applications. Firstly, the basic CPW pentagonal island antenna, Antenna A, is constructed on a 1.6 mm thick FR-4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.3 and a copper thickness of 0.035 mm. This antenna contains a pentagonal island with five mini structures of pentagonal island. Then, for Antenna B, a modification is made to the shading made of the Sierpinski gasket structure in the mini structure of the pentagonal island. For simulation Antenna B, it shows the simulation performance of 3.52 GHz and 5.93 GHz with return loss of - 24.84 dB and – 27.94 dB. For the measurement result of Antenna B at desired frequencies of WiMAX 3.5 GHz and WLAN 5.8 GHz, it shows a good performance of – 17.25 dB and – 19.35 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Broadband End-Fire Antenna Based on Double-Sided Ridge Gap Waveguide for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed an end-fire antenna based on the double-sided ridge waveguide with wide impedance bandwidth and high gain performances. The antenna is designed by extending the double-sided ridge gap waveguide (DS-RGWG) structure with I-shaped radiation aperture, which has the advantage of wideband and high gain. The I-shaped aperture is designed by etching the gap between ridge and pins. The stepped transmission structure is designed from DS-RGWG to the radiation aperture with broad band performances. The 1×4 antenna array is fed by the low loss air-filled DS-RGWG power divider to verify the performance of antenna element. The simulated results indicate that the antenna array can achieve broad impedance bandwidth of 46% from 25.1 to 40 GHz with realized gain above 12 dBi. The whole antenna array has high symmetry structure which is easy to fabrication, and it is a promising candidate for millimeter-wave (mmW) communications.

articleTitle: Measurement System and Methodology for RIS-Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a simple measurement methodology and system that enables a comprehensive RF performance test of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) board prior to its final usage. The complete RF switching functionality of each element on the surface can be verified, and any faulty RIS elements can be detected. Unlike far field measurements, this evaluation takes place in the nearfield of the RIS, directly above the board's surface.

articleTitle: Metasurface Based Linear to Linear or Linear to Circular Multiband Multi Polarisation Converter for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents an ultrathin reflective type multi-polarisation converter of periodicity 0.177λ0 where λ0 is the free space wavelength for X, Ku, K and Ka band applications. The metasurface unit cell of the proposed triple broadband PC consists of diagonally oriented slotted semicircular metallic ring resonators and shows triband linear to linear polarisation conversion at 10.94-15, 17.80-18.48 and 27.08-30.09 GHz with polarisation conversion ratio > 95 %. The same linear converter also shows pentaband linear to circular polarisation conversion at 10.05, 15.7, 17.25, 19.55 and 25.95 GHz. The designed linear to circular converters can be used for X and Ku-band downlink (10.7-12.5 GHz), K-band downlink (19.5-21.5 GHz) and K and Ka-band uplink (25.5-27.5 and 29.5-31 GHz) satellite communications and can also be integrated with multiple input multiple output antenna (MIMO) for simultaneous RCS and mutual coupling reduction.

articleTitle: Multilayer S/X-Band Array Antenna for Shipborne Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multilayer S- and X-bands array antenna for shipborne radar applications. The proposed antenna consists of the three parts such as the multilayered radiators, transmit receiver modules (TRMs), and an interface layer. S- and X-band elements of the multilayered radiators are designed in a mutual complementary form to reduce the blockage effect by the upper S-band elements. For the electric beam steering, each element of the multilayered radiator should be individually connected to the TRMs. Then, the durability of the antenna is improved by employing the interface layer between the radiators and the TRMs. The maximum array gains with the 16 unit-cells in the S- and X-bands are observed to be 14.6 dBi and 26.6 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Crossed Dipole Antenna with a Wide Axial Ratio Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A technique for miniaturizing a crossed-polarized dipole antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of a pair of dipole antennas and a halved dipole antenna. Two arms in the dipole antenna are arranged perpendicular to each other, producing two resonant frequencies. Tuning the arms’ length changes the frequency ratio for the axial ratio below 3 dB, leading to a wide axial ratio bandwidth of over 50%.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Slotted Waveguide Antenna at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article proposed a low-profile dual circularly polarized leaky wave antenna designed for W band applications. The unit element of this antenna comprises of a unique combination of longitudinal and transverse slots, that are positioned on the broad wall of the waveguide. The precise arrangement of slot offset positions and lengths results in the generation of circular polarization (CP). The presented design facilitates the realization of dual CP by simply switching the antenna's ports. The presented antenna operates from 82 GHz to 86 GHz frequency band, and exhibits a maximum gain of 19.58 dBi. Its all-metallic structure, easy fabrication process, and robust structure make it a highly promising choice for W band space applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Reconfigurable Dual-Band Antenna for Efficient IoT based LoRa Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact reconfigurable dual-band monopole antenna for Long-Range (LoRa) IoT applications. It incorporates a PIN diode for seamless switching between 433 MHz and 868 MHz frequencies. With dimensions of 80 × 80 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, it is ideal for space-constrained applications. The antenna achieves a 2 dBi peak gain and exhibits a signal transmission efficiency exceeding 90%. It addresses the demand for a reconfigurable antenna solution in Europe and Asia’s LoRa bands, thereby enhancing the capabilities of LoRa IoT systems with flexible frequency operation.

articleTitle: Effect of Gap between Arm and Torso and Clothing on Human Body Shadowing at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We assessed the human body shadowing at 300 GHz using a human body phantom and terahertz hemispheric scanner. Measurements were taken at chest and belly levels to change the gap between arm and torso. When the gap between the torso and arm was 20 mm, the shadowing loss was approximately 5 dB higher than when the gap between the torso and arm was 45 mm. At chest height, the shadowing loss with down coat was approximately 5 dB lower than that without clothing. The measurement of the direction-of-arrival (DOA) of radio signals in the 300 GHz band shows that the clothing spreads the DOA of diffracted waves at human body in the elevation direction.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Koch fractal antenna for UHF Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ultra-high frequency can capture the electromagnetic waves that are generated due to partial discharge. In wireless communication the technology has been over-rising day by day due to this there is an introduction of compact multiband antenna. In this paper we will discuss about the Koch fractal antenna. Fractal antennas are the antennas which have self-similar properties. There are used to increase the effective length and perimeter of a material. A Koch fractal antenna has been developed for multiband application. Fractal antennas are systematic in comparison to the conventional antenna. The principle of Koch fractal antenna is its self-similar properties that make the antenna to work in multiband operation. Miniaturing of antenna can be obtained by space filling property of fractals. As the iterations of Koch fractal antenna increases, the resonate frequency also increases. The maximum range of Koch fractal antenna is 2-30GHz.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Circularly-Polarized Microstrip Antenna with Simple Two-Branch Switchable Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study proposes a new concept of a microstrip antenna with circular polarization (CP) reconfigurable function. The proposed CP switchable antenna consists of a corner-truncated single patch element and a simple two-branch switchable feed network. Each branch is connected to a PIN diode. CP switching between the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) and right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) can be achieved by applying positive and negative switching voltage, respectively. In the measurement, the 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 4.3% and 4.4% are achieved for LHCP and RHCP, respectively. The axial ratio is lower than 3 dB, and around 6.5-dBic antenna gain is achieved for both LHCP and RHCP. The proposed concept and performance are evaluated by simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Chamfered UWB Monopole Textile Antenna With Truncated Ground Plane for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A bandwidth enhancement of chamfered square Ultrawideband (UWB) monopole textile antenna with truncated ground plane for breast cancer detection is presented in this paper. The overall dimensions of 28.5 x 28.5 x 3.34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, covering a super bandwidth of range between 2.23 and 18.24 GHz is obtained. A total impedance bandwidth (<-10 dB) of 16.01 GHz is achieved with a total efficiency of 93.54% and realized gain of 12.95 dBi at 9.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Semi-Circle Ring Antenna For 5G UAV Application
