publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a microstrip antenna configuration for 5G technology (3.4 - 3.8 GHz), particularly designed for UAV applications. The proposed design features a circular ring with a semi-circle ring, connected to a 50 Ω SMA connector. The substrate material employed is RO4003 with a dielectric constant of 3.38 and a thickness of 1.5 mm. Simulation using CST software demonstrates that the antenna resonates effectively at 3.8 GHz, showcasing a reflection coefficient of - 39.96 dB. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits a gain of 3.43 dBi and a generous bandwidth of 1.53 GHz, making it suitable for 5G UAV applications.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Balun with Bandpass Responses and Wide Stopband
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized balanced-to-unbalanced transformer (balun) with bandpass responses. Two miniaturized K-inverters with filtering components are applied to substitute for the λ/4 transmission (λ is the wavelength in vacuum) line of the conventional balun structure, which can reduce the size and have good out-of-band suppression performance. The relevant theoretical analysis and specific steps of method realization are listed. To illustrate, a filtering balun operating at 400 MHz, which is widely used in mobile communication, is implemented. Bandwidth and insertion loss is 15.63 % and 1.2 dB, respectively. In the passband, the two outputs have identical amplitudes, and exhibit a phase difference of 180 degrees. The circuit size is 0.051 λ × 0.033 λ, which is compact.

articleTitle: A Simple and Low-Cost Integratable MIMO Antenna for 5G Sub-6GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a simple and low-cost MIMO antenna without any decoupling structure has been presented. The proposed antenna fully covers Australian commercial 5G band that is designated for 3.5 – 3.7 GHz. This band offers high speed wireless connectivity and supports 5G communications that inherently have low latency and high data rates. It is designed using FR-4 low-cost substrate with thickness of 0.8mm. Moreover, it exhibits good radiation characteristics in terms of radiation patterns and gain. The shape and compactness of antenna allow its easy integration to 5G enabled devices and IoT applications.

articleTitle: Design of 60 GHz SIW Six-Port for Phase Differences Detection in Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a six-port using a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW). Six-port detects the phase difference between two signals effectively. Meanwhile, SIW is a synthetic rectangular waveguide with low cost and low transmission loss. The characterization results show that the proposed design gave good results at the operating frequency of 60 GHz and is suitable for detecting phase differences in radar systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Height Estimation of Forward Targets Using Automobile mmW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The main objective of our research is to construct a collision prevention system by Automotive Millimeter-Wave (mmW) radar to achieve highly accurate sensing of the environment in front of a vehicle. Current Automotive radar systems are specialized for horizontal detection and have a problem of false detection in the elevation direction. We show that height estimation can be achieved with a conventional radar by using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). However, since the forward target is located in the end-fire direction in this SAR observation, the effect of positioning error becomes large. Therefore, we propose a method that can estimate the height of the target and vehicle velocity. The concept of SAR and the validity of the proposed method are evaluated experimentally.

articleTitle: Cognitive manipulation of Wireless Channel Matrix using Software-driven Electromagnetic Skins for mmWave and sub-THz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electromagnetic skins (EMSs) can be employed to manipulate the wireless channel matrix, improving the signal-to-noise ratio at the millimeter-wave and sub-THz frequency spectrum. A line-of-sight channel can be achieved through the use of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, passive reflectarrays, and frequency-selective surfaces for scattering mitigation. These beamforming surfaces are integrated with cognitive radios, which exploit field diagnosis and deep learning for acquiring channel state information. These software-driven EMSs are expected to be a cost-effective solution for future smart electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: Leaky Wave Antenna with Non-Radiative Dielectric Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a leaky wave antenna (LWA) with non-radiative dielectric superstrate (NRDS) is proposed. The proposed antenna is having a dielectric superstrate and an asymmetric, half-filled dielectric spacers forming a quasi-cutoff region in the unfilled region. A high gain, unidirectional tilted beam with wide-angle characteristics is demonstrated using numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Gain Improvement of Reflector Antennas Using Novel Partially Reflective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the antenna gain improvement of conventional reflector antennas using novel partially reflective surfaces (PRS). The conventional circular open-ended feed horn with 20×20×4 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> flat ground plane and the antenna gain of 11.6 dBi at 9.5 GHz is modified to improve the antenna gain. The PRS cross-slot together with the rectangular slot structures are combined and embedded in the rectangular conducting patch unit cells to increase the antenna gain. Moreover, the conventional center-fed parabolic reflector antenna size of 20×20×18.2 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with 23.8 dBi gain is employed as the reference antenna. It is found that the proposed antenna length (20×20×5.65 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) is shorter than the conventional center-fed parabolic reflector antenna by 3.64 times while an improved antenna gain of 25 dBi is achieved. Moreover, in the case of a conventional circular open-ended feed horn with a flat ground plane, the antenna gain is increased from 11.6 dBi to 25 dBi.

articleTitle: Estimation of Excitation Position of Platform Excitation Antenna Using Short Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Miniaturization of antennas leads to a decrease in radiation efficiency and bandwidth. To overcome this problem, the excitation of the platform has been proposed to make the platform function as a radiator of the antenna. This paper proposes the evaluation method to evaluate the amount of excitation of the platform to improve efficiency of the small antenna. By using a low-efficiency dipole antenna with the size of 1/600 wavelength, the radiation efficiency of the whole system including the platform is evaluated.

articleTitle: Textile Characterisation for Wearable Antenna Application using Transmission Line Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the conductivity measurement and analysis technique for the conductive textile on low loss and lossy substrates using transmission line measurement. This method is proposed to determine the accurate conductivity properties of the samples based on the transmission parameters, S21 of a two-port transmission line. The experiments were performed on conductive samples; pure copper as a reference and a conductive textile called Shieldit Super. Three samples were fabricated; Copper Pure on Rogers RO5880 as a reference sample, Shieldit Super on R05880 as sample 2 and Shieldit Super on felt fabric as sample 3. Operating at 1.575 GHz, simulation and measurement were carried out to analyse the properties of these three samples. The result shows a close agreement of the measured S21 for the three samples to the simulated value. Result is plotted to observe the conductivity behaviour for all samples and found correlates with the theoretical equation showing the lower the transmission loss, the higher the conductivity, resulting in higher antenna gain performance. Furthermore, a close match is demonstrated for the conductivity results for all fabricated samples to the expected conductivity. Hence, applying the correct technique to measure the material conductivity is imperative, especially for high-frequency applications like antennas.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulations of Undersea Propagations for Various Sea Depth at 100 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Applications of radio waves for underwater communication are currently growing. Utilization of the lateral wave is considered promising. In this paper, electromagnetic simulation data are obtained in different seadepth at 100 MHz. Normal-mode helical antenna is employed for transmit antennas. The seadepth are changed from the seasurface to 50 cm depth. Visual 2D electric field distributions of the seasurface antenna indicate the lateral wave propagation situation. At 20 cm and 50 cm depth, the propagation attenuation becomes the same as the theoretical value based on the sea conductivity.

articleTitle: Classical Electrodynamics Predictions for LUXE and E-320 Experiments with 17 GeV electrons and TW Laser Collision
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The experiments LUXE at DESY Germany and E-320 at SLAC USA, are aimed to test strong-field QED for 15 +- 3 GeV electrons and TW laser pulses. In concrete both experiments will demonstrate the dominance of nonperturbative physics by which is expected a huge amount of emitted photons. Although one would expect that classical electrodynamics will fail for strong-field conditions, the purpose of this paper is to demonstrate the inverse of it. In fact, here it is presented a theoretical as well as computational methodology based at the theory of Hartemann-Kerman known as classical nonlinear Compton scattering that yields various energy spectra by which one can anticipate the transition from the lowest nonlinearity until scenarios for bunching emission of photons, fact that to some extent will validate the classical electrodynamics, as to make predictions for prospective experiments.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband, Dual-Linearly Polarized Tightly Coupled Dipole Array With Composite Wide-Angle Scanning Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present an ultra-wideband (UWB) dual-linearly polarized tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) with composite impedance matching superstrate for wide-angle scanning. The proposed design provides a superior performance of 10.6:1 bandwidth (1.8–19.1 GHz) with active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 3 when scanning up to ±45° in both E and H planes, which is mainly due to use of double-layer composite frequency selective surface (FSS) impedance matching superstrate that contains two types of unit cells. Besides, the array achieves average efficiency of 80% by removing the resistive FSS layer between dipole and ground plane in conventional designs. The overall profile is 0.68λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">middle</inf>, which makes the antenna suitable for the application of satellite communications.

articleTitle: A Metasurface Design Method for Beam-forming Based on Impedance Sheet Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a metasurface design method for antenna beam-forming. Based on tangential electromagnetic fields on both sides of the metasurface, the equivalent model of the metasurface—impedance sheet model(ISM) is calculated. Accordingly, the metasurface structure is designed. The given examples illustrate that ISM and metasurface can transform antenna pattern into target field pattern and realize beam-forming.

articleTitle: Improvement of DOA Estimation with FOCUSS Algorithm by Updating p-norm Iteratively
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient method to obtain a high-quality solution in the FOCUSS algorithm for DOA estimation with an array antenna. The computer simulation demonstrates the improved performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Flexible Rectenna For Wirelessly-Powered Flexible Electronic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A flexible rectenna has been designed for harvesting radio-frequency (RF) energy from a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi router. The rectenna consists of a textile-based patch antenna and a flexible rectifier. The patch antenna is designed to resonate at the 2.4 GHz ISM band, enabling the capture of RF energy and its conversion into AC signals. A 4-stage Dickson rectifier circuit converts these AC signals into DC signals to power electronic components. The rectenna demonstrates the capability to harvest power from the Wi-Fi router at a distance of 1.25 m. Experimental results show that the rectenna can achieve a maximum power output of 1423.70 nW and a maximum voltage of 0.62 V under an optimal load of 270 kΩ.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of Intelligent Devices and Environments for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents some ideas and results related to designing and characterizing intelligent devices and environments for wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Electrically Activated Split-Ring Slot Antenna With Simple Bias Decoupling Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new and simple electrically-controlled slot antenna design for circular polarization (CP) switching function. The antenna includes a ring-slot structure for a radiating element, and the microstrip lines for a feed network. To function together, they are designed on either side of the single-layer substrate. Switchable shorted branches are mainly employed to electrically realize the split-ring slot principle for CP diversity. Also, the feed network can avoid any additional lumped components for bias decoupling. The simulated and experimental verifications are further presented to confirm the proposed concept. Both results demonstrate that the proposed structure ensures for CP reconfigurability with simple biasing and design flexibility for arrays.

articleTitle: Passive Multi-Rectenna Channel Estimation Based on Beam-Spatial Smoothing for Microwave WPT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel passive multi-rectenna channel estimation method based on beam-spatial smoothing. The proposed method assumes cooperative/selective wireless power transfer using multiple wireless stations: one station transmits high-/low-power binary pilot signals with multiple beam patterns. Due to the rectenna non-linearity, the other receives pseudoload-modulated backscattered signals from the multiple rectennas. Then, multi-rectenna channels can be estimated from the correlation matrix of the received signals through beam-spatial smoothing. Ray-tracing simulation shows the proposed method achieves accurate channel estimation and high transfer efficiency.

articleTitle: Realization of Voltage Doubler-based Tri-band Rectifier for Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents the realization of a tri-band rectifier operating at practical frequency bands of 915 MHz, 1.8 GHz, and 2.4 GHz. It is imperative to note that the designed rectifier is based on an improved single-voltage doubler branch topology. This essentially makes the developed rectifier low-cost and easy to implement in various wireless energy transfer and energy harvesting applications. In addition, the realized rectifier was validated through experimental measurements, which showed that the power conversion efficiency ranges from 30% to 60% at three selected operating frequencies.

articleTitle: Dual-band Circularly Polarised U-slotted Waveguide Antenna for Sub-THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study describes the design of a dual-band circularly polarized (CP) U-shaped slotted array on the broad wall of the WR3 waveguide for Sub-THz applications. Short-range THz applications requiring high data rates can employ the suggested antenna. This work achieved an impedance bandwidth of 84.17 GHz and a peak gain of 14.36 dBi. Also, Dual-band CP is attained with an Axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 4 GHz and 13 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband MIMO Quad Element Antenna for mm-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact a compact wideband MIMO quad element antenna for mm-wave applications. The presented antenna comprised of four antenna elements having T-shaped configurations. The presented antenna is able to operate between 36.32-40.5 GHz. This antenna achieves a maximum gain of 7.180 dBi at 38 GHz. The diversity parameters of the proposed antenna is analyzed and it is seen that this antenna operates well in the desired frequency range.

articleTitle: Investigating Channel Capacity Characteristics of Millimeter-Wave Full-Duplex MIMO System with Mobile Terminal Space Diversity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a study of channel capacity characteristics for a millimeter-wave full-duplex MIMO system when interference between mobile terminals is suppressed using space diversity. The authors also explore a method of terminal-to-terminal interference suppression using Eigen-beamforming. The space diversity technique is then applied to the mobile terminal during Eigen-beamforming to achieve further interference suppression. The effectiveness of this approach is confirmed using millimeter-wave radio propagation simulation by the ray-tracing method in an outdoor environment.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antenna with Luneburg Lens for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the simulation result on a millimeter wave microstrip patch antenna with Luneburg lens for 5G beamforming application. The proposed design utilized a microstrip patch antenna with complementary split ring resonator at the ground plane feeding a plate Luneburg lens designed to achieve narrow beam (10°) at 28 GHz frequency. The size of the patch antenna is 8 mm × 8mm and produced 0.66 GHz bandwidth with 6 dB gain, and 76% efficiency at the desired frequency. Some of the advantages of the proposed method are the 133.33% increase of radiation gain and the narrow beam output from the lens. However, the structure experiences 19.73% decrease in total efficiency. Then, the number of patch antenna is increased to 5 and the result shows beam overlap at -5 dB. From the result, it is confirmed that the combination of MPA with CSRR and the plate Luneburg lens have narrow beam performance with increased gain. This work could contribute to compact beamforming and beam scanning application in millimeter wave frequency.

articleTitle: Measurement evaluation of the MACKEY broad banding model using an inverted-F antenna as the feeding element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: MACKEY has been proposed as a functional compact antenna that is not affected by surrounding metals. MACKEY II unbalanced inverted-F type has also been proposed to solve the problem of the conventional model by using an inverted-F type antenna as a feeding element to expand the bandwidth of 5-GHz band MACKEY. This paper describes the principle of operation of the inverted-F type antenna and the actual measurement results.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Multifunctional Dielectric Lens Antennas Based on Gradient-index Fiber Concept for Beam-steering and Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, based on gradient-index (GRIN) fiber concept, two types of dielectric lens antenna for beam- steering and imaging application were introduced respectively. The properties of beam-steering and high-resolution imaging for proposed lens antennas were analyzed based on ray tracing method and full-wave simulation. The prototype of proposed lenses can be fabricated by 3-D printing technique in a low-cost. Besides, the flexible beam-steering capability with switched- beam and subwavelength imaging resolution were measured and validated.

articleTitle: Multi-hop Beamforming in RIS-aided Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-hop reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) aided multiple-input single-output (MISO) system is studied to mitigate significant channel attenuation in Millimeter wave and terahertz communication. The achievable sum rate of the system is maximized via optimizing the passive elements at the RISs with an iterative algorithm. Simulation results imply that the proposed algorithm is able to improve the achievable sum rate by increasing the number of RISs.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Full Duplex Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband full-duplex antenna for 5G applications. The proposed antenna comprises a pair of microstrip patch antennas as transmitter and receiver parasitically loaded with the third patch to enhance isolation. Loading stubs obtain the ultra-wideband response in the microstrip patch antennas, which introduce additional resonances. Two shorting pins are incorporated in order to improve the impedance matching. The proposed antenna operates in a frequency band ranging from 25-40 GHz with resonances at 28 GHz, and 38 GHz and offers isolation ranging from 17 to 34 dB within this frequency range.

articleTitle: Right Hand Circularly Polarized (RHCP) Dual Band Flexible GNSS Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) flexible dual-band Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) antenna operating at L1 (1575 MHz) and L2 (1227MHz) and having dimensions (83×89×7.25) mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is presented. Two circular radiators with two slotted rings each enable the antenna to operate at L1 and L2 bands.

articleTitle: Generation and Steering of W-band OAM Beams Based on Liquid Crystal Metasurface with Pancharatnam-Berry Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams with different topological charges are mutually orthogonal to each other, which shows great potential in enhancing capacities of wireless communication systems. In this work, we demonstrate a W-band liquid crystal (LC) metasurface with Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase. The proposed metasurface can convert circularly polarized waves to OAM beams by PB phase and steer the OAM beams by transmission phase, which is controlled by applying an electric field to LCs. The two kinds of phase are combined under the guidance of the convolution theory of metasurface. The simulated results are demonstrated at 103GHz and can be further exploited in OAM communication systems.

articleTitle: Ray Tracing Simulation in Wide Urban Areas by Combining Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper studies the ray tracing simulation in a km-order urban area model. It is often difficult to calculate the massive model because of the calculation cost. In this paper, we propose a simple modeling method that combines several or many buildings into one block to decrease the elements of the analysis model. The height of each block is determined from area cumulative probability. The best result of comparison between measurements and simulations shows RMSE of 6.73dB.

articleTitle: Investigating Plasmons in van der Waal heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The deposition of atomically thin layers materials through tailored nanofabrication has led to a huge interest in exploring intriguing physics at the nanoscale, in particular the interaction with light. However, these methods are prohibitively expensive and often hard to repeat. In this paper, we present a dyadic Green function approach to analyse the surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) that exist at the interfaces in van der Waal heterostructure materials. Our results in particular the enhanced propagation length of the SPPs show that the extraordinary physics of light matter interaction in van der Waal materials can be effectively analysed. We believe our method can become an integral part of plasmonic and photonic photodetection devices at terahertz and mid-infrared frequency regions.

articleTitle: Design of Millimeter Wave Array-Based Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a compact and high-performance array antenna operating at millimeter wave bands. The array was constructed using the circular patch-based single antenna. Furthermore, it should be noted that the etched slots around the circumference were added to increase the achievable bandwidth. In particular, 7.16% bandwidth at the central frequency of 32 GHz was obtained. Finally, the developed array antenna showed an 11.3 dBi peak gain making it practical for numerous applications, including wireless body area networks.

articleTitle: Design of Post-Wall Waveguide Stacked E-plane Cruciform Cross Couplers for 120-GHz band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An E-plane cross-coupler with a center frequency of 120 GHz that can be fabricated on a multilayer printed circuit board used in a 2D butler matrix has been designed. The basic structure consists of a three-layer waveguide and two slots, coupled at the upper and lower sections and designed not to affect the radio waves in the middle section. The design with post walls resulted in low reflection and high isolation characteristics.

articleTitle: Performance Characterization of A Patch Antenna Embedded Partially by Magnetized Ferrite Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the performance characterization of a patch antenna which is embedded partially by magnetized ferrite within the host material. The substrate used as a host material is Rogers RO4003C configured in triple layers of structure. An external magnetic bias is applied using a magnetic field source aiming to magnetize the ferrite material. Measurement results show that the partially embedding of magnetized ferrite within the host material could affect the resonant frequency and S-parameter response.

articleTitle: Input Impedance Change of Meander Line Antenna in Human Body Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation results and evaluates the performance of the meander line antenna (MLA) in human body conditions, comparing different permittivity and conductivity values, including muscle, and fat tissues. The electrical characteristics obtained by simulation, such as input resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</inf>), and MLA self-resonant structure are discussed. The theoretical and simulation results are compared for the validation of the simulation environment. The absorption loss is calculated and compared with the simulation results. The input resistance increases when the antenna conductivity increases.

articleTitle: A Dual-Layer Gap Waveguide Antenna with Vertical Polarization for Full-Duplex Joint Communication and Sensing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A vertically polarized subarray antenna based on Gap Waveguide technology has been designed for Joint Communication and Sensing (JCAS) systems operating at the center frequency of 77 GHz. The proposed subarray consists of two radiating layers with an in-between cavity layer. The first layer is comprised of 3 up-pointing V-shaped slots with the inter-element spacing of λ and the second layer has 6 transverse-arranged slots that are employed to obtain vertical polarization. The S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> < –10 dB frequency bandwidth is from 75.7–78.3 GHz. The achieved peak Gain is 13.8 dBi at 77 GHz.

articleTitle: A Low RCS Microstrip Antenna Based on AMC Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a chessboard metasurface with artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) units is designed. With the aid of the equivalent circuit model (ECM) analysis method and the phase cancellation principle to achieve RCS reduction, two kinds of AMC units are designed, which can achieve 180 °± 37 ° phase difference in a wide frequency bandwidth. The chessboard metasurface is then loaded onto the microstrip antenna, and the RCS of the antenna is greatly reduced. Under the normal incidence of electromagnetic waves, the 10dB RCS reduction can achieve within frequency bandwidth of 7.81-14.76 GHz. When the oblique incidence angle of the electromagnetic wave is less than or equal to 50 °, the RCS reduction performance of the antenna has relatively good stability.

articleTitle: Machine-learning Assisted Synthesis for Series-Fed Microstrip Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A machine-learning assisted (MLA) synthesis for the series-fed microstrip array method is proposed. The series-fed microstrip array is divided into three types of base element (BE). Each BE is individually sampled and trained, significantly reducing the calculated budget. Once the design parameter of the series-fed microstrip array is given, the S-parameter and radiation pattern of the array can be approximated by the cascade of three types of BEs. Two practical array synthesis examples are given to verify the superiority of the algorithm.

articleTitle: The Design of Wilkinson Power Divider For 3-Way Output Ports
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the Wilkinson power divider for 3-way output ports is proposed by combining a conventional Wilkinson power divider(WPD) with unequal Wilkinson power divider. In the proposed, the unequal Wilkinson power divider is added in the output port2 and port3 of the conventional WPD, which selects an asymmetric 3-way output ports to configuration. Therefore, the proposed design formula of the Wilkinson power divider with 3-way output ports is derived, and the proposed formula is verified by the circuit simulation results on HFSS. An analysis of the Wilkinson power divider with 3-way output ports verified the performance at centre frequency of 2GHz with the circuit simulation results of insertion loss, return loss, and isolation, respectively.

articleTitle: Stretchable Patch Antenna Using Kirigami Technique for Wearable 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A stretchable patch antenna with a geometrical dimension of 47.0 mm (L) × 66.0 mm (W) × 5.00 mm (H) is proposed. To significantly increase the stretchability, Kirigami patterns are introduced on both the patch and the ground plane. Simulation is used to prove the stretchability of rigid metals using Kirigami patterns. The Ecoflex 0030 is employed as a stretchable substrate to encapsulate both the patch and the ground plane. The proposed antenna has a resonant frequency of 3.59 GHz and a broadside radiation pattern with a maximum gain of 0.306 dBi.

articleTitle: A 2-18 GHz 6-Bit GaAs Positive Voltage Driven Digitally Controlled Attenuator for Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband 6-bit digitally controlled attenuator MMIC for the active phased array that integrates positive voltage digital driving circuits was developed, utilizing GaAs enhanced and depletion mode p-HEMT process. The attenuator design operates in an ultra-wide bandwidth of 2-18 GHz, with a dynamic attenuation range of 0.5-31.5 dB and an attenuation accuracy of less than 0.9 dB over the entire frequency band. The integrated DCFL (direct coupling field effect transistor logic) inverter circuit on the chip enables direct control of the attenuator with a positive voltage while occupying a chip area of only 2.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Reduced Size Modified Square-Shaped AMC for Antenna Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a co-planar waveguide (CPW) antenna incorporated with 2 x 2 artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) operated at 2.4 GHz is proposed for gain enhancement. The proposed AMC is only 0.16 λ x 0.16 λ in size. The AMC frequency range is from 2.35 to 2.47 GHz. AMC is then incorporated to 12 mm x 36 mm CPW antenna. The gain of the CPW antenna is successfully enhanced by 3.7 dBi with incorporation of AMC. Results in terms of reflection phase, reflection phase and radiation patterns are discussed.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Asymmetric Horn Antenna Integrated With Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An additively manufactured horn antenna integrated with a printed circuit board (PCB) is presented. The designed antenna is composed of an additively manufactured horn together with a short waveguide in which one of the walls is shared with the printed circuit board. The PCB ground plane constitutes at the same time one of the metal walls of the waveguide, and the signal is delivered to the through-patch transition. The presented approach combines the advantages of low-cost manufacturing of horn antennas with the possibility of active circuit realization in microstrip technique. Both electromagnetic calculations and measured results of the designed antenna operating in X band are presented.

articleTitle: Estimating Direction of NLOS Mobile Terminal Using Covariance Matrix Prediction Based on AR Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to realize the direction estimation of Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) terminal. The proposed method uses a linear prediction method based on past measured elements of the covariance matrix of propagation channels and estimates the NLOS terminal direction using those predicted values. The simulation using the ray-trace model showed the proposed method realizes NLOS terminal direction estimation with 1.54° accuracy.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Reverse Fractal Reflector for RIS Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present the design and simulation of butterfly-shaped metamaterial reflectors at 12 GHz. The design is derived from fractal iteration that has the reverse angle of the iteration. The metamaterial reflector functions at a wide-ranging operating angle of incident electromagnetic (EM) waves. The Rogers's substrate is used to print a butterfly copper structure on the unit cell of the metamaterial, which is 0.51 mm thick. The simulation results indicate that the metamaterial reflector can reflect up to 40° of incident EM waves, which is more than 85%. For TE mode, the metamaterial structure can maintain 75% reflectance at an operating angle of 60°. The reflector is expected to be employed in reconfigurable intelligence surface (RIS) applications.

articleTitle: Pilot Study on Aerial Wireless Superdirectional Sound Sources Utilizing Parametric Array Loudspeakers via Local 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents a pilot study on the potential future use of aerial sound sources utilizing parametric array loudspeakers (PALs) in drones via fifth-generation (5G) networks. Integrating superdirectional loudspeakers with high-speed wireless communication is essential for projecting sound from the air to specific locations using drones. Herein, as an experimental approach, we have evaluated the performance of wireless communication, specifically local 5G, for realizing aerial sound sources. The results demonstrated the high performance of the local 5G connection intended for PALs in the air.

articleTitle: A 64-Element Antenna Array With a Low Wind Load for 5G Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a 64-element antenna array with a low wind load is proposed for sub-6 GHz base stations. The proposed array element consists of a radiating layer with regular cross-dipoles, a defected ground layer to improve isolation between input ports, a metal mesh reflector to reduce the size of the windward side and maintain electromagnetic performance, and the metal support structure to keep the physical structure stable and provide enough space for installing the radome. A prototype of the proposed 64-element array formed by using the above-mentioned antenna element is fabricated and measured. The results show that the -10-dB impedance bandwidth is 3.4–3.6 GHz, the realized gain is 24.2 ± 0.4 dBi and the front-to-back ratio is larger than 16 dB, which proves that the proposed structure is suitable for 5G sub-6 GHz base stations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Downlink Considering an Interference Source Moving along the Satellite Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an analysis of the low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlink when the interference source moved along the satellite’s trajectory with a specific elevation angle difference. To analyze the link budget more precisely in various situations, the ground station antenna radiation pattern is obtained by using geometrical optics (GO) and physical optics (PO) methods, and the regression model is applied to this radiation pattern to easily observe the tendency. Latitude and longitude data for the LEO satellite are obtained from the two-line element (TLE) data. Based on this data, we derive the latitude and longitude of the interference source on the same date and calculate the jamming-to-signal ratio (J/S), the velocity and path of the interference source that satisfies the requirement (J/S = 10 dB). The antenna gain of the interference source is 10 dBi (transmitted power of 90 dBm), and its height is 5 km with a difference angle phi of 2 degree. The results demonstrate that with a calculated velocity of the interference source J/S is maintained about 10 dB when the time from 251 to 457 seconds.

articleTitle: Application of Sierpinski Fractal Slot in Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The development of an antipodal Vivaldi antenna implementing the Sierpinski arrowhead curve slot for head imaging is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna has an overall dimension of 65 x 65 x 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> using Roger RO4350B as a substrate. The proposed antenna can produce a better reflection coefficient under -30 dB and higher gain achieving 7.35 dBi compared with the antenna without the fractal slot. It is also reported that the application of the fractal slot does not alter the antenna’s performance, which could interfere with the antenna design that already met the head imaging criteria.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Phase-Gradient Reflecting Metasurface for 5G mmWave Coverage Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a phase-gradient reflecting metasurface (MTS) to improve 5G mmWave coverage, following the principle of perfect anomalous reflection. The reflective responses of a simple structure with cross-shaped resonators have been investigated. The results from a full wave simulation show that the proposed MTS with a surface area of 23×23 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> can anomalously reflect a linear dual-polarized plane wave at 25.8 GHz from an incident angle of 30° to a reflection angle of 54° with a more than 10 dB radiation power ratio between the main reflected beam and its sidelobe at a specular reflecting direction.

articleTitle: Design of a 3-order Filter using New Spiral Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a 3rd order bandpass filter using new spiral resonators. The proposed resonator is a structure in which a closed loop resonator and a spiral form are combined. The coupling coefficient is adjusted through a gap between resonators and a line width of the resonator. The proposed filter is designed with bandwidth of 2GHz at 8GHz center frequency.

articleTitle: Thin Dielectric Lens Antenna for Small Focusing Spot in Human Body
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In hyperthermia therapy, it is necessary to ensure electromagnetic radiation is concentrated only on the targeted area and not in the surrounding healthy tissues. An initial focused dielectric lens operated at 2.45 GHz has been designed to achieve a small focusing spot in 2/3 muscle equivalent phantom. The thickness of the initial lens is then minimized to develop a thin lens. The spot size and power density at the focusing spot are evaluated between the thin lens and the initial lens design. Power density achieved by the thin lens is in good agreement to that of the initial lens. The treatment spot of 2.78 cm is capable of being achieved by the thin lens. The proposed thin lens design might be suitable for achieving small focusing spot on human body.

articleTitle: U Slot in Wearable Microstrip Antenna for Multiband Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: U slot patch antenna design is illustrated for multiband antenna design using textile material jeans as substrate and pure copper polyester taffeta fabric as conducting material. This antenna design exhibits multiband results for WLAN at 2.4GHz and 3.6GHz frequency and for Wi-Fi6E at 6.6 GHz. The first band functions between 2.40GHz and 2.44 GHz, the second band between 3.62 GHz and 3.73 GHz, and the third band between 6.6 GHz and 6.7 GHz frequency. Current distribution was plotted for the U slot in the patch to understand the optimization in the fabric material.

articleTitle: New Correlation Between Array Excitation and Beam Shift for Circular MIMO Antenna with C-Shaped Parasitic Element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of integrated antennas with parasitic elements (IAPE) for MIMO application. Parasitic structures are known for improving bandwidth and enhancing MIMO antenna isolation. Due to the integration of the structure to the fundamental-mode conventional patch antenna design, the theoretical relationship between array excitation coefficients (β) and beam radiation angles (θ) in the modified structure shall be validated. To illustrate this concept, an equally-spaced linear array of circular patches with C-shaped parasitic elements is used. The verification process involves analyzing simulation and measurement data and comparing it to the established equation for a traditional array. The relative phases between adjacent elements were set between 0° to 90° while maintaining equal amplitudes across all elements. As a result, a new correlation has been established by normalizing the beam shift to the half-power beam width, which is applicable for the proposed design. Additionally, the effectiveness of the IAPE was confirmed through MIMO diversity performance, including low mutual coupling, 75% radiation efficiency and a gain exceeding 14dBi.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Widening of A Planar Monopole Antenna Using Spline Shaping Optimization Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an attempt to widen the bandwidth response of a planar monopole antenna using a spline-based patch geometry representing an ovoid shape. The spline curvature is formed by arranging 10 control nodes with a symmetrical property, so position shifts to widen the bandwidth are carried out only on five control nodes. The attempt is conducted by changing the position of nodes through characterization to produce the antenna that works from the frequency of 3.75 GHz to observations at 20 GHz. These findings are followed by optimization based on the genetic algorithm (GA). The simulation results show that the antenna bandwidth is improved, working from the frequency of 3.27 GHz to 20 GHz or with the geometrical bandwidth of 206.9%. These results are then verified by measurements, yielding the measured bandwidth from the frequency of 4.03 GHz to 20 GHz or with the geometrical bandwidth of 177.9%.

articleTitle: FDTD Method Analysis of Moving Antennas Above Rough Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this research, an analysis method using the FDTD method is proposed for the Doppler shift that occurs during radio communication between antennas moving over a rough surface at equal velocities. Whenever there is radio communication between vehicles or between ships, the road surface or the water surface is the path of the radio waves. And because automobiles and ships are moving with speed, they are unavoidably reflected by the road surface. Depending on the relative speeds of the automobile and the road surface, these reflected waves are affected by the Doppler shift. To achieve stable communication, these reflections have to be analyzed. This study focuses on the quantitative analysis of the Doppler shift using the FDTD method. The road surface is treated as a rough surface considering its actual geometry. The analysis frequency in this study is 27.9 GHz.

articleTitle: Co-Design of Tapering and Dielectric Loading for Minimizing the Scattering Cross Section of a Near-Field Measurement Probe
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the antenna capabilities of a near-field measurement probe, such as the return loss (S11), radiation pattern and peak gain. For this purpose, a rectangular open ended waveguide (OEWG) is used, while minimizing its scattering cross section (SCS), to increase the accuracy of near-field measurements. In this context, the relation between tapering and dielectric loading of the measurement probe is analyzed, since the taper is simultaneously utilized as an air to dielectric transition for the antenna. Furthermore, absorbers are used around the opening of the OEWG, to reduce the SCS even further. It is shown, that the tapering and dielectric loading of the measurement probe are highly correlated and significantly influence the antenna capabilities. Finally, the best constellations to reduce the SCS and increase the antenna capabilities of a rectangular OEWG are shown with improvements up to 15 dBsm.

articleTitle: Development of a Passive Localization Method using Multi-link MIMO Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In our previous study, a multipath RTI (Radio Tomographic Imaging) method for a high-precision passive localization of targets within an indoor environment was developed. This method achieves highly accurate positioning by separating multipath components (MPCs) among sensor nodes and utilizing them as virtual nodes, thereby significantly reducing the number of sensor nodes compared to conventional methods. This paper presented a system configuration based on a multi-link multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) sensor network where MPCs are separated by spatiotemporal MIMO beamforming. The validation of the proposed scheme was shown by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-beam Holographic Metasurface Antenna Using Stepped-Impedance Distributions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a method of using stepped-impedance distribution for multi-beam holographic metasurface (MTS) antenna is presented. By minimizing the disturbance of adjacent sources, which is caused by the impedance deviations of averaging impedance method, the proposed approach helps to improve antenna gain and precision of steering angles. For validation, an MTS antenna for dual-beam steering at 10 GHz is designed. The antenna contains two ports designated for two independent steering angles: port 1 for 10° and port 2 for 0°. The simulation shows that the gain of 16.1 dBi and 16.23 dBi, SLL of 11.45 dB and 12.7 dB are achieved at port 1 and port 2, respectively.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Ultra-Wideband Phased Array Antenna With 9:1 Bandwidth and ±75° Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) dual- polarized tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) is proposed. A resistive frequency selective surface (FSS) is utilized to improve the bandwidth and scanning range. The average radiation efficiency of the designed antenna is above 84% for all scan cases. Furthermore, simulations show that the proposed antenna can achieve the active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) below 3 when scanning up to ± 75° and ± 60° in the E and H planes from 2 to 18 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband to Narrowband Reconfigurable Metamaterial antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of wideband to narrowband frequency reconfigurable metamaterial antenna. Bandwidth enhancement is achieved based on the effect of left-handed capacitor C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> by optimizing the position of slot between middle patch and top patch. Single PIN diode is used as switch for reconfiguration. Effect of biasing line position is also investigated and analyzed along the length of the antenna. The software used for the simulation work to investigate the effectiveness of the proposed antenna is Computer Simulation Technology CST software. The antenna covered bandwidth range of (2.3-5.4) GHz in ON state and switched to narrowband which resonates at 5.2 GHz in OFF state. Maximum gain of 2.4 dB and efficiency of 86 % are obtained at 5.2 GHz band when the switches are in ON state. For OFF state, maximum gain of 1.8 dB and efficiency of 75% are obtained at 5.2 GHz. By considering the results obtained, the antenna can be used for indoor WLAN application for short range connections.

articleTitle: CPW Pentagonal Patch Antenna with Multiple Slots Effect for WLAN and WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a dual band CPW pentagonal antenna with multiple slots technique for WiMAX and WLAN applications. Antenna A was a basic pentagonal antenna with CPW-fed, while Antenna B was the pentagonal island shaped antenna with CPW. Then it moves on to Antenna C, which has pentagonal island slot with mini pentagonal island slots while Antenna D is the modified version of Antenna C. The objective is to create dual band frequencies with the improvement of the antenna by addition of the multiple slots. The Antenna D has an improvement of - 25.22 dB at 3.5 GHz and - 23.92 dB at 5.92 GHz, making it appropriate for WiMAX and WLAN band, according to the research results.

articleTitle: Experimental and Simulation Evaluation of Reflection Characteristics of the Transparent Film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, as a fundamental study for using reflectors in the high-frequency band, we developed an evaluation system for reflectors. We conducted experiments and ray tracing simulations to evaluate the reflection characteristics of aluminum flat plates and transparent film. Experimental and simulation results were generally similar. In addition, time gating eliminated coupling between antennas, allowing accurate measurement of reflection characteristics.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz Propagation Channel Characteristics in an Urban Macrocell Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recent developments in wireless communication technology have led to a diversification of usage scenarios. As a result, there is a growing demand for channel models for the design, development, and evaluation of new wireless communication systems. Our objective is to build a channel model that takes into account site-specific characteristics and behavior in order to accurately reproduce channel characteristics in specific usage scenarios. This paper presents a propagation channel measurement campaign in an urban environment using an in-house sub-6 GHz band channel sounders at 2.4 GHz and 4.8 GHz and the resulting large-scale channel characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Layer Planar Wave Absorber Using Time Domain and Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the adjoint sensitivity analysis with an iterative first-order gradient descent optimization technique is proposed in conjunction with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method to design a broadband multi-layer planar electromagnetic wave absorber made of the expanded polystyrene mixed with graphite powder. The result obtained from the proposed design method is compared with the point frequency matching method. Smaller thicknesses and lower carbon content of a multi-layer planar absorber are obtained which can reduce the absorber weight.

articleTitle: A Quad-Tip Wideband E-Field Probe With High Spatial Resolution For Near-Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on a quad V-shaped tip design, this paper introduces a novel high-performance, low-cost, wideband, and high spatial resolution electric field probe that operates from 10 kHz to 12 GHz for identifying and locating the EMI problem of the electric and electronic systems for near-field measurement. The sensitivity increased to -19 dB which is 8 dB higher than commercial and other introduced probes. The spatial resolution increased to 0.75 mm at 10 GHz. This probe is fabricated in a four-layer printed circuit board (PCB) with high-performance dielectric (RO4450 and RO4003) with a tip width of 4 mm which is very suitable for the narrow and complex PCBs.

articleTitle: Cognitive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) for mmWave Integrated Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a concept of a cognitive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) for self-sustainable wireless communication system. Reconfigurable beamforming surfaces are integrated with lens-based beamformer for cognitive radios, enabling feedback loop for managing dynamic propagation channel links. Sustainable operations of the proposed cognitive RIS are experimentally validated by indoor and outdoor link-level measurements. This paradigm shifting investigation can be a promising solution for constructing energy-efficient green communications on future wireless networks.

articleTitle: Modelling of Micro-Doppler Effect in mm-Wave Antenna Due to Near-Field Insect Fly-By
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work studies the feasibility of using mm-Wave radio links for insect monitoring. It uses electromagnetic simulation to evaluate differences in antenna gain and reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) from micro-Doppler effect due to an insect passing in the antenna's near-field. The study is conducted for different frequencies in 10-40 GHz. It is demonstrated that an insect can be detected by characteristic periodic variation in both S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and gain, which correspond to its wingbeat frequency. As the wingbeat frequency is correlated with insect's size, this work shows feasibility for a new type of biodiversity monitoring system that is integrated into mm-Wave communication links.

articleTitle: Novel Vertically Exposure System Using Spatial Synthetic Antennas to Investigate Thermo-Physiological and Cellular Function Changes Induced by Millimeter-Wave Exposure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to study thermo-physiological reactions and changes in cellular functions of living animals and humans induced by millimeter-wave exposure, a novel localized exposure system at 60 GHz was developed using a spatial synthetic technique. We have confirmed that the exposure intensity at the desired area was sufficient to achieve desired temperature rise on the skin surface of living mice.

articleTitle: Design of a hollow-waveguide slot array antenna for a channel sounder in the 150 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this manuscript, we design a hollow-waveguide slot array antenna for a 150-GHz channel sounder. A hollow waveguide structure with low transmission loss is used to achieve a high gain with high efficiency. The antenna is an array of 16 slots with standing wave excitation fed from the center. A radiating element with the equivalent normalized shunt conductance of 1/8 is designed for half of the uniformly excited array. The simulated reflection of the eight-slot array is −19.8 dB at the design frequency of 158 GHz.

articleTitle: Characterization of A Compact Flexible Phase-Difference 4×4 Butler Matrix Realized on Ultra-Thin Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The development of a compact flexible phase difference (F-PD) 4×4 Butler matrix is presented. To achieve a compact size, the circuit is realized on an ultra-thin and very high relative permittivity substrate material. Therefore, a 0.127 mm thick RT/Duroid RO6010 dielectric substrate is selected for circuit prototyping and then measured for experimental characterization. The dimensions of prototype take 39.9 mm × 42.5 mm. Measurement result demonstrates that for the input excitation at port P3, the reflection coefficient value is less than –10 dB within a 280 MHz bandwidth from the frequency of 1.92 GHz to 2.2 GHz. Along the bandwidth, the average transmission coefficient value is –7.5 dB with the amplitude imbalance of ±3.4 dB, while the average output phase difference is –119.5° with the phase imbalance of ±20°.

articleTitle: Broadband Energy Harvesting Metasurface Covering WiFi band with Wide-Angle Incidence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband energy harvesting electromagnetic energy metasurface with wide-angle incidence characteristic is proposed in this paper. The structure consists of four quarter metal rings plus H-shaped metal patches. The lumped elements are placed on the surface of the metasurface Enables efficient broadband harvesting of energy at 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz frequency points. And the bandwidth with an efficiency of more than 90% reaches 2.6 GHz, and the bandwidth with an efficiency of more than 80% reaches 3.43 GHz. The relative bandwidth with an energy harvesting efficiency of more than 80% is 83.67%, and with an energy harvesting efficiency of more than 90% is 65.64%.

articleTitle: Ka-band array capable of 1-bit quantization and dual-polarization using unit cells with 4 PIN diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented the design of a low profile electrically reconfigurable antenna array at Ka-band based on the unit cell with 4 PIN diodes on one layer which produces 4 distinct operational states of dual linear polarization and 0°/180° phase-shifting capability for each polarized state. This unit cell reveals a bandwidth of 1 GHz at around 28 GHz and a gain of 3.8 dB in all states. Next, the proposed 4x4 array antenna allows for generating a low cross-polarization by applying the image configuration method and its 1-bit phase quantization. To demonstrate the concept, a 4x4 antenna array was designed and simulated. The full wave simulation result shows high cross-polarization discrimination greater than 35 dB for dual linear horizontal and vertical polarizations, and the gain of 14.5 dB.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Rasorber With Ultrawide Low Reflection Band and Wide Transmission Band Based on Dual Resistive Layers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with wide transmission band is presented. Dual resistive layers are utilized and designed separately to realize the ultrawide reflection suppression band, both of which achieves the same broadband transmission band. Together with the bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) corresponding to the wide passband, the full-wave simulation results show that the proposed FSR exhibits a -10 dB reflection suppression band ranging from 1.01 GHz to 11.83 GHz and a -1 dB transmission band covering 8.36-11.63 GHz simultaneously. The relative bandwidth of absorption rate over 90% achieves 151.0%, ranging from 1.01 GHz to 7.23 GHz, which is the widest of all the A-T type FSRs published previously. Equivalent circuit model (ECM) has also been constructed to provide further insight into the structure and highly consistency between the circuit analysis and EM simulation can be observed. Moreover, the angular stability of the proposed FSR can achieve 60° under TM-polarized and 45° under TE-polarized incidence.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Radio Frequency Level Sensor Based on Wheeler Cap
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel non-contact liquid level sensor based on the Wheeler cap. The sensor utilizes an electrically small antenna operating at 276 MHz enclosed within a metal cap, in conjunction with the liquid container. By analyzing the reflection coefficient at the antenna feed and evaluating the magnitude and frequency of the minimum value, the sensor enables determination of the water level. The experimental results demonstrate the sensor's effectiveness in measuring water levels within the range of 0 to 94 mm, in a water container measuring 109x109x123 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Notably, minimal variations in frequency and magnitude of the minimum reflection coefficient are observed at water levels below 50 mm, while the sensor exhibits improved sensitivity for water levels above 50 mm. The proposed sensor can offer a promising level sensing solution for liquids with extreme temperatures.

articleTitle: Broadband flexible metamaterial absorber using Carbon fiber loaded silicone foam
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new and original absorbing material based on silicone foam loaded with long carbon fibers (12 mm). This flexible composite is structured in a periodic way, like "metamaterials". The originality of the proposed absorbing material resides, on the one hand, in the association of two simple fabrication concepts (a simple production of the silicone foam and a simple periodic structuring of this foam) and, on the other hand, in the use of dielectric lossy material to make periodic broadband absorbing structures. The idea here is to replace standard metamaterial absorbers, based on structured metallic film (often copper) deposited on a dielectric substrate, by organic metamaterial. Thus, a flexible absorber of 16 mm thickness, with the shape of a "chessboard" and having a broadband absorption bandwidth with the reflectivity below −10 dB in the frequency range of 4-18 GHz is proposed and implemented. Moreover, we also obtain a good absorption response by varying the incident angle up to 30°.

articleTitle: A Wideband Fat Dipole Antenna Integrated with Solar Cells for Internet of Things Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a solar cell–integrated wideband fat dipole antenna. Implementing a dipole antenna with a solar cell provides dual functionality that simultaneously enables energy harvesting and wireless communication. RF decoupler circuits are used to operate the antenna and the solar cell independently. The proposed design uses a fat dipole structure incorporating a wide dipole arm and a pair of open stubs. These features make the antenna have wideband characteristics and a high-form factor. The proposed solar cell integrated antenna has overall dimensions of 102 mm × 52 mm × 0.571 mm (0.333 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> × 0.170 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> × 0.0019 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> at 0.98 GHz). It exhibits a –10 dB impedance bandwidth of 105% (ranging from 0.98 to 3.18 GHz), a form factor of 96%, and an optical transparency of 100%.

articleTitle: Investigation of 5G RU Placement Using 2D Radio Propagation Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Investigations on location of placement of 5G radio units (RUs) using a 2D radio propagation simulation tool is carried out. Specifically, a set of locations are investigated for the placement of two RUs in a campus block with indoor/outdoor environment. A Motley-Keenan multi-wall radio propagation modeling tool is used for the analysis. The investigation is carried out by defining two objective functions viz.,. a) maximizing radio coverage in the desired regions and b) reducing the interference between the two RUs. From the Pareto front, thus obtained with both the objective functions, optimal locations for placement of the 2 RUs are identified.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting the Dimensions of Rectangular Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antenna design process is time-consuming often involves a trial-and-error approach, which is not efficient. Machine learning algorithms can save significant time and effort in the design process and result in better antenna performance. This paper provides an analysis of suitable machine learning algorithms for predicting microstrip antenna dimensions by comparing six machine learning models based on four commonly used metrics in multi-output regression problems. The result shows that Random Forest algorithm is the most suitable algorithm since it gives the highest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score, namely 0.757, and lowest error value among the other algorithms, i.e. 0.674 for MAE, 4.097 for MSE, and 2.024 for RMSE.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band 8x8 MIMO Antenna for 5G Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Dual-band 8x8 MIMO antenna for the 5G communication services is proposed in this paper. It operates at 3.3-3.7GHz and 4.85-5.08GHz frequency bands. The antenna is printed 0.8-mm-thick FR4 substrate of relative permittivity 4.4 and loss tangent 0.02 and designed to be perpendicular to the edge of the system circuit board. It can be applied to the popular full-screen mobile phone. According to the simulation results, reflection coefficient is less than -6 dB, and the isolation is better than 12 dB over the band-frequency of 3.3-3.7GHz and 4.85-5.08GHz. It meets the needs of the future 5G applications.

articleTitle: Line-of-Sight Probability Estimation Formula for an Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses a line-of-sight (LOS) probability estimation formula in an urban environment. We developed a LOS estimation formula that adapts to changes of the road width and the building length of a uniform grid pattern city. The basic part of the formula is constructed on the basis of the theory of the d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> model, which has been standardized for the development of 5G. In addition, the LOS spread in intersection areas is represented by an empirical formula and is added to the basic formula. As a result, we obtain an overall LOS probability estimation formula that is adaptable to changes of the two parameters.

articleTitle: Non-Resonant Reflectarray using Stacked Striplines with Varying Propagation Path Lengths at 120 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a different reflectarray design exploiting controlled propagation path lengths within the dielectric, providing broader phase variation and reduced reflection loss. The beamforming capabilities of the reflectarray consisting of the proposed structure is validated through demonstration of gain of approximately 30 dBi at the target reflection direction. Furthermore, error vector magnitude (EVM) measurement exhibits a significant improvement in received power and a reduced EVM of 2.73 %rms compared to a normal metal plate. The results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed reflectarray structure in sub-terahertz band applications, simplifying reflectarray implementation and enabling various applications as well as within the wireless communication field.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Slot With Co-Planar Waveguide UWB Antenna for Wi-Fi RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna based on a coplanar waveguide transmission line designed with a rectangular slot is presented for ambient RF energy harvesting. The proposed antenna as a harvester antenna covers the ISM Wi-Fi bands of 2.45 GHz and 5 GHz over a relatively wide frequency range from 2.1 GHz to 6.3 GHz with an operating bandwidth of 4.2 GHz. Both frequencies achieve less than 10 dB reflection coefficient characteristics of about -13 dB with a gain of 3.653 dBi and 4.635 dBi at 2.45 GHz and 5 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Low-profile Directional Coupler Based on Staggered Mushroom-Like Double-Layer Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 3-dB directional coupler based on the staggered mushroom-like double-layer gap waveguide (SMDGW) transmission line with low insertion loss and low profile is presented. It consists of two hollowed substrates, two metal plates and three stacked substrates. Two pairs of metallic vias and a slot located in the mushroom-like electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure are designed to achieve the coupling between the two transmission lines, and the magnitude can be achieved by changing the number and distance of the vias. The simulated results show that the proposed coupler achieves a bandwidth of 19.9% ranging from 24.4 to 29.8 GHz, a profile of 0.22λ, a power equality of 3.45 ± 0.15 dB and an isolation of 18 dB.

articleTitle: Comparison of Large-Scale Channel Characteristics in the 5.4 GHz and 42.66 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To promote the development of millimeter wave (mmWave) wireless local access network (WLAN) and the compatibility with low frequency WLAN systems, the comparison of the measurement-based large-scale channel characteristics in indoor environments at 5.4 GHz and 42.66 GHz are presented. The closed-in (CI) path loss model is employed to analyze the effects of frequency and antenna polarization. Based on extensive channel measurements, the impact of propagation environment and antenna performance on the channel cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) ratio is analyzed.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Reflecting Surface with Integrated Rectenna Elements to Enable Direct Control of Reconfigurability through Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The more self-reliant the Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) is, the better to handle the tuning of such smart surfaces with low cost and maintenance. This work explores the study of integrating the rectenna with the unit cell of the IRS to achieve direct control of the tuning elements through Wireless Power Transmission (WPT). The dual frequency operation is proposed with a control channel of WPT at frequency f1, while the IRS operates at frequency f2. The IRS integrated with conjugately matched rectifying diodes at f1 can harvest RF power through WPT and translates to a DC bias voltage range within the unit cell for tuning the tuned element. Simultaneously, the proposed IRS operating at f2 can reflect the information/energy beam in the desired direction which is reconfigured by tuning. The proof of the proposed concept is presented through preliminary analysis and simulations.

articleTitle: Wideband Waveguide-to-differential-line Transition with Slots and Back-short in Multilayer Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband waveguide-to- differential-line transition with slots and a back-short structure for use in 300-GHz band. Slots and a back-short structure are formed in a multilayer substrate to create a double resonance. By controlling these resonant frequencies, a transition with wide bandwidth of low-loss connection can be obtained. As a result of the optimization, the simulated bandwidths were 107.5 GHz for reflection lower than −10 dB and 131.9 GHz for transmission higher than −3 dB.

articleTitle: Non-contact bedsore detection using numerical human models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Bedsores are localized injuries to the skin and subcutaneous tissue caused by prolonged pressure on the skin and decreased blood flow. Early treatment of bedsores can shorten the treatment period. In our research, an antenna is placed between a bed and a mattress, with the aim to detect bedsores in the early stage by non-contact microwave detection. In this paper, we reproduced bedsores in the sacral region of a numerical human model (Taro) provided by the NICT (National Institute of Information and Communications Technology), and detected the bedsores using a patch antenna in the 10.525 GHz band. As a result, it was confirmed that the bedsores could be detected even in the numerical human model. In the future, we plan to develop a method for detecting early stage bedsores such as Stage I, develop a phantom that simulates the numerical human model, and conduct measurement experiments to evaluate the validity of the simulation.

articleTitle: Vertical Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna with Cylindrical Slot Loop for Wideband Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband vertical polarized omnidirectional antenna with cylindrical slot loop is proposed. The proposed antenna obtains wide bandwidth by inserting slot in the copper cylinder. The diameter of the proposed antenna is 0.11λ, a height of 0.44λ, respectively. The proposed structure does not employ the ground plane for the flexibility of installation. The simulation results show that the operating bandwidth of proposed antenna is 68.2%.

articleTitle: An S-band Dielectric Rod Antenna Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
