abstract: In order to reduce the profile of an S-band high-gain antenna, this paper designs and simulates an S-band dielectric rod antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The antenna is composed of four media and achieves a low-reflection effect combination of feed-transition-emitter by leveraging boundary conditions and dielectric constants. The resulting printed dielectric rod antenna has a low electrical size profile and operates at 3.14-3.8 GHz with an impressive in-band gain greater than 8.5 dBi and a center operating frequency gain of 11.4 dBi. Its high gain, low profile, and small mass make it an excellent candidate for sub-6G applications.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of V-Shaped Slot Effects on DGS and EBG for Wideband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on the effects of integrating V-shaped slots into Defected Ground Structures (DGS) and Electromagnetic Bandgap Structures (EBG) for wideband planar antennas. The objective is to evaluate the influence of the V-shaped slot on the antenna’s performance, focusing on S-parameters and surface current distribution. Simulations using CST Studio Suite 2023 software are done to obtain the results. This study provides valuable insights into the effects of V-shaped slots on DGS and EBG structures with wideband antennas. It focuses on contributing to the progress and development of antennas for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: TOF and DOA-Based Positioning of UWB Tag Under Non-Line-Of-Sight Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a non-line-of-sight Ultra-Wideband (UWB) tag positioning method using the channel’s Time of Flight and Direction of Arrival. The mobile terminal continuously observes channels from a UWB tag while moving straightly in an environment where a UWB tag is stably placed behind an obstacle. The simulation result using the ray-trace method shows that the proposed method could estimate the UWB tag position with the accuracy of 1.0 m and 3.6 m at the 75 percentiles for no reflection and five times reflection cases, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Spherical Convex Multibeam Dielectric Lens Antenna for Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multibeam lens antennas are a potential future wireless communications technology. Finding the optimal feed position is necessary in multibeam applications. Focal region ray tracing is a highly effective approach for determining the optimum feed position. The focal region ray tracing on a spherical-convex lens is presented in this paper. Simple equations define the shape of the lens. The ray tracing is then performed and determination of feed position is applied. Finally, electromagnetic simulations at 28 GHz are performed for validation. It shows a good multibeam performance with 70% maximum aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: Interdigital CPW Metamaterial Surfaces for Modern Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of metamaterial surfaces based on interdigital coplanar waveguide (CPW) unit cells. By using this technique, the unit cell can have negative permeability with size reduction to λ/8. The result causes from the slow wave effect on transmission line in the structure, which electrical and physical lengths of transmission line are not equal from that effect. The proposed matamaterial surfaces at some resonant frequencies have been designed and used as reflectors and directors applied for antenna applications. Using the designed reflectors or directors, the antenna performances have been increased. The proposed metamaterial surfaces will be appropriate for modern wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Bragg Scattering Characteristic Evaluation of Thin High-Voltage Power Lines Using Low Transmitting Power Helicopter Forward-Looking 76 GHz Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper evaluates and discusses the detailed reflection characteristics, including Bragg scattering, of thin high-voltage power lines using a helicopter forward-looking obstacle detection 76 GHz low-transmitting power millimeter-wave radar system. Initially, we provide an overview of the developed radar system, which operates at a center frequency of 76.5 GHz and a transmitting power of 10 dBm, adhering to the low-power radar specifications. Subsequently, we measure the reflection power from thin high-voltage power lines approximately 370 m away with a diameter of around 13 mm. To conclude, a two-dimensional radar scope is employed to investigate the reflection characteristics including Bragg scattering.

articleTitle: A 3.5 GHz Wearable Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper represents a wideband wearable antenna for 5G applications. In this proposed design, an antipodal vivaldi antenna structure is implemented on a polyimide and polyester combined substrate. The 120 × 95 × 0.82 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> sized antenna acquired a wide bandwidth of 910 MHz with a realized gain of 5.42 dBi and efficiency of 96 percent.

articleTitle: Horn Antenna Gain Enhancement using 3-D Printed Dielectric Lens for Dielectric Properties Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 3-D printed dielectric lens for gain enhancement of horn antenna from 18 GHz to 40 GHz is presented in this paper. Fused deposition modelling (FDM) is used to fabricate the Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) lens as it is one of the well-known 3-D printing techniques. The results with and without dielectric lens are analyzed and compared from the simulation. From simulation results with the dielectric lens, a maximum gain of 26.7 dBi was achieved. The dielectric lens of 21.72 mm thickness was able to provide a gain enhancement up to 26.7 dBi when compared to the simulation result without the dielectric lens. The proposed dielectric lens can improve the gain of the horn antenna as good agreement between literature, simulation and measurement was achieved.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of A Spiral Antenna with Impedance Matching Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper explores the radiation characteristics of a spiral-shaped patch antenna with an additional impedance matching circuit at the feeding network. The proposed spiral antenna which adopts a proximity coupled technique for the excitation is designed on two layers of 0.8 mm thick Roger RO4003C dielectric substrate with the dielectric constant of 3.38 and the loss tangent of 0.05. The impedance matching circuit comprised of interdigital capacitors and meander-lines is positioned between the first and the second layers. The proposed design is then realized for experimental characterization, where-by the results demonstrate that the spiral antenna operates at the center frequency of 3.5 GHz with an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> value of –21.5 dB, and has the bandwidth response of 40 MHz with the gain of 1.67 dBi at its center frequency.

articleTitle: Advances in fast antenna measurements: use of single cut in near field measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the past years, the time in antenna measurements has become a constraint. This paper shows the possibilities and limitations for the characterization of antennas and radomes in near field using single cut or two-cuts acquisition. Also, the paper will show the possibilities for the measurement of only amplitude, and transformation to far-field, for the antennas in millimetre or submillimetre waves.

articleTitle: DOA Measurement of 300-GHz-band Signal Propagation through Tree
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a measurement of the direction of arrival (DOA) of 300 GHz signals diffracted and reflected by trees using a high-speed terahertz hemispheric scanner. The shadowing loss by a trunk with a diameter of 10 cm is approximately 15 dB, and that of a tree with dense leaves and thin branches was about 25 dB. DOA measurement results revealed that the density of thin branches and leaves has a great impact on DOA spread.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transmission by Propagation of Electric Field Waves on Metal Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer (CWPT) couplers transmit power via the electrical near field with high efficiency. However, the near field decays rapidly with distance and is therefore unsuitable for power transmission over long distances. On the other hand, Zenneck type surface waves are known to propagate over long distances on metal, keeping the power close to the metal surface and not dissipating much power into the air. This paper shows that the propagation of electric field waves along a metal surface allows power to be transmitted over relatively long distances with high efficiency: prototypes of electric field resonant couplers resonating at 13.56 MHz were built and the electric field waves generated by the coupler were transmitted 3m along the metal surface, and -5.8 dB (26%) transmission efficiency between couplers was obtained. The results of this measurement are also compared with the results of electromagnetic field simulations and discussed.

articleTitle: Living-Body Ranging Method Using SISO Wi-Fi Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a human-body ranging method using SISO Wi-Fi radar. This method estimates target distance using Time-Of-Flight (TOF) calculated by Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signal. The simulation showed that the proposed method reduces the estimation error by 4.59 m at 75 percentile compared to the case without removing phase error.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Metasurface Inclusion on A Bandpass Filter Developed Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses an experimental study on the effect of metasurface inclusion to the characteristics of a bandpass filter (BPF) developed based on substrate integrate waveguide (SIW). The metasurface is constructed by combining 14 complimentary split ring resonators (CSRRs) and 7 thin wires, whilst the SIW BPF is designed on two layers of 0.4 mm thick Roger RO4003C dielectric substrate with the dielectric constant of 3.38. The simulation result shows that the inclusion of metasurface into SIW BPF can enhance the filter performances indicated by the improvement of reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) and transmission coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) values. Meanwhile, the experimental measurement demonstrates that the SIW BPF with metasurface inclusion has the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> value of –57.8 dB and S21 of –6.2 dB at the center frequency of 3.28 GHz. Here, the low S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> value is contributed by the losses of materials used to develop the SIW BPF with metasurface inclusion.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Compact Antenna Solutions for 5G-IoT Applications at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research focuses on designing a compact millimeter-wave antenna for 5G-IoT applications at 28 GHz using a double-sided FR-4 substrate and copper layer. Simulation and measurement results indicate promising performance with a small size of 14.30 mm x 15.80 mm, a reflection coefficient of -45.11 dB, a VSWR of 1.011, a gain of 5.472 dBi, and a directivity of 6.694 dBi. The proposed design is anticipated to exhibit excellent performance characteristics for IoT applications and holds promise for efficient integration into 5G-IoT devices.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Antenna: Enabling Fat-Intrabody Communication at 2.45 GHz ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a graphene-based antenna designed for fat intrabody communication at 2.45 GHz. The antenna utilizes graphene’s unique properties, such as conductivity and compatibility with biological systems. It is a planar meandered inverted F antenna (MIFA) printed on a silicone substrate. The antenna’s efficacy is evaluated within a three-layered tissue structure and different inter-antenna distances. The results show adequate impedance matching within fat tissue, resonance at 2.45 GHz, and a competent transmission coefficient. The study explores the impact of three layered tissue separation and depth on antenna propagation performance between the transmission coefficient and distance. The graphene-based antenna offers promising potential for effective intrabody communication in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Resonance and Bandwidth Performance of Triband Antenna through Bending Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)

authors.preferredName: Mohd Adzimnuddin Bin Mohd Nor Azami

abstract: A triband antenna that has difference position of monopole arm is studied for wireless communication. The study of the bending effect of the monopole arm is discussed briefly in this paper. The simulation of the triband antenna can generate the frequency at 2.56 GHz, 3.51 GHz and 4.51 GHz. The measurement of gain of the antenna is 3.21 dB, 0.01 dB and 0.80 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Novel Wideband E-plane Bend Waveguide Phase Shifters for W-band Monopulse Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two novel full-band E-plane bend waveguide phase shifters (PSs) are proposed in this paper. These designs combine the conventional wideband phase self-compensating PS with the bend waveguide for the first time. For the bend waveguide, by employing the self-compensation characteristics of the phase between the extended H-plane structure and the E-plane stub-loaded structures with staggered arrangement, two near-constant 90° PSs are obtained in the whole W-band. The configurations of the two PSs are the 90° and 180° circular bend waveguides, respectively. These proposed PSs can replace the bend waveguides and straight waveguide PSs of the feeding networks, thereby reducing the network size and loss. The two W-band 90° waveguide PSs are designed and optimized. In the whole W-band, the simulated results show that the 90° circular bend waveguide PS achieves the phase shift of 90°±1.8° and the reflection coefficient of less than -20 dB. Additionally, the 180° circular bend waveguide PS achieves the phase shift of 90°±1.7° and the reflection coefficient of less than -24 dB.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of a Flexible Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna on Various Rubber-Carbon Compositions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a flexible circular microstrip antenna using rubber substrate is proposed to operate at 2.45 GHz within the ISM band for wearable applications. Several rubber materials with different carbon filler compositions have been selected as the substrate for the antenna. This includes natural rubber (no carbon filler), rubber with 20% carbon filler, rubber with 25% carbon filler and rubber with 50% carbon filler. The performances of these antennas are simulated and analyzed based on the S11, bandwidth and gain. The antennas are also compared to two other flexible substrates; PDMS and RO3003. Based on the simulation results, antenna with natural rubber exhibits the best gain, while antenna with rubber and 50% carbon filler exhibits the widest bandwidth.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Microstrip Antenna in 920MHz Band for Ocean Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile antenna is proposed for remote monitoring of offshore turbines. Simulation results show that 10dB-return loss satisfies the 920.6-928MHz of the specified low power base station. The radiation pattern is omnidirectional and the direction of the maximum radiation is in low elevation angle.

articleTitle: Achieving minimal PWB link loss due to fiber weave influence for multi-Gigabit transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the printed wiring board (PWB) laminate fiber weave influence on differential signal integrity for 20 Gbps transmission. The influence of non-homogenous PWB laminate segment ratio within the fiber weave on signal integrity is investigated with two-dimensional electromagnetic (2DEM) modeling in Advanced Design System, followed by analyzing the line impedance, link loss (Sdd21) and eye diagram for 20 Gbps transmission. Higher non-homogeneous PWB laminate segment ratio intensifies the link loss. By maintaining the non-homogeneous laminate segment ratio below 15 %, the link loss due to fiber weave influence is below 1 dB at fundamental frequency 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Passive Millimeter-Wave Imaging Based on Focal Length Agility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that existing millimeter wave/terahertz imaging systems have a narrow depth of field and cannot meet the requirements of both close-range imaging and standoff imaging, we propose a digital refocusing technology that applies the principle of light field imaging to passive millimeter wave imaging system. The angle information of the millimeter wave radiated from the target can be collected by adding a micro-lens array before the main lens. The refocusing algorithm can realize arbitrary focal plane imaging, which can improve the imaging depth of field and realize non-cooperative security imaging. This technology also has potential applications in other millimeter wave imaging application scenarios.

articleTitle: A mm-Wave T-R RF Switch Incorporated With CSRR Switchable DGS for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a millimeter-wave transmit/receive switch that applies a switchable defected ground structure for 5G applications. The switch shows a high isolation level of up to 42 dB and can be operated optimally around 24.23 to 28.31 GHz. Furthermore, the switch's accessibility to swap between bandstop and allpass responses gives it an edge in being appropriately used in 5G time division duplex communication.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Folded Dipole Integrated On-chip Antenna for 5.8GHz Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, the transition from large to miniaturized devices has been increasing, and as a result, the demand for pertinent and footprint-size antennas has become necessary. In this study, a design of a miniaturized antenna on-chip resonating at 5.8GHz is proposed. A coplanar waveguide coupling technique was adopted, modelled on a five-layer structure. A slotted metal layer was introduced as an electromagnetic shield between the antenna element and the silicon substrate. The design was reduced to one-fourth of the original antenna size with a configuration of 4.1x4x0.508mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Thus, achieved a gain of 2.14 dBi, a radiation efficiency of 68.7% with a bandwidth of 0.65 GHz below a return loss of -23 dBi. Hence, the design is suitable for Wi-Fi, WLAN and WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: Scalable and Connector-less 3D Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reviews different 3D antenna arrays with connector-less interface to active components. The examples show that 3D antennas may provide superior bandwidth, efficiency and beam steering range as compared to their thin, planar counterparts. 3D antenna arrays can additionally facilitate denser integration of electronic components and be used as a radome or for cooling.

articleTitle: New Method for Doppler Shift using a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We provide a new method to generate Doppler frequency shifts (DFS) using a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). In conventional methods, the required Doppler shift is acquired by modulating RIS’s reflection phase. However, this method is greatly dependent on the variation of the reflection magnitude and phase of RISs, which are not constant in the frequency band of interest. To alleviate this unwanted dependency, our RIS structure directly transforms the input signal to the target Doppler shift, which is based on sensing the difference between the input and the output signals. Consequently, our RIS can enhance both a conversion loss (CL) and a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR), simultaneously.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Dual-Band Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact dual-band frequency reconfigurable antenna for WBAN applications is designed and analyzed in this paper. The proposed antenna is simulated on a flexible Rogers Duroid RO3003TM material with a compact size of 38 mm × 40 mm × 0.5 mm. In the OFF state of the PIN diode, a single resonance (ISM 5.8 GHz) with a percentage bandwidth of 5.2% at 5.8 GHz is achieved. However, in the ON state, dualresonance (ISM 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz) with a percentage bandwidth of 3.9% and 5.4% are achieved. Bidirectional and directional radiation patterns are observed in the E-plane while omnidirectional radiation patterns are observed in the H-plane. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for WBAN applications.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of Electrodes for Through-The-Earth 350 kHz MF Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an experimental investigation of electrodes for Medium Frequency (MF) communication Through-The-Earth (TTE) at an operating frequency of 350 kHz. The electrodes are spiked into the ground at the end of each earth-grounded antenna lead. The experiment includes a transmitter system and a receiver system, and the received signal power, conductivity, and impedance are measured using a spectrum analyzer and an LCR meter when the type and number of electrodes are varied. The results show that different electrode types impact conductance and impedance, with higher conductivity and lower impedance electrodes receiving greater signal power compared to other electrodes. Moreover, increasing the number of electrodes enhances the system's ability to receive higher signal power due to improved conductivity and lower impedance, bringing it closer to the impedance of the radio transceiver. These are the importance of selecting suitable electrode types and numbers for optimal signal transmission and receiving in TTE communication at 350 kHz.

articleTitle: A New Circuit-Type Multibem Antenna Array Employing Generalized Joined Coupler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Analogue multibeam antennas are poised to become a major technology for 6G. In this talk, we present an overview on circuit-type multibeam antennas and present a new type of feed networks for multibeam antennas, known as the generalized joined coupler (GJC) matrix. A salient feature of the GJC matrix is that the same phase shifters can be used for tuning each beam, and different beams can be steered continuously and independently. Different configurations of the GJC matrix and the different theories for designing the GJC matrix are discussed. Some implementations issues and new experimental results will be reported.

articleTitle: Quantization with Infinite Classical Fields: The Quantum/Classical Correspondence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: It is shown that quantization of an external field apart of being intrinsic in quantum field theories, it can be also done in a fully scenario of classical electrodynamics. In this paper the quantization of field is demonstrated that is dual in the sense that not only is exclusive from quantum mechanics, but also in classical electrodynamics. To accomplish this, the Dirac-Delta function is derived because in according to Feynman rules, the argument gives direct information on the conservation of momentum and energy of particles under interaction. Thus, in scenarios of interaction with strong laser, apart that nonlinear Compton scattering is identified, that classical electrodynamics can arrive to same results.

articleTitle: Low-Profile High-Gain Reflector Antenna Fed by Ku/E Dual-Band Feed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-profile dual-band reflector antenna with high gain is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a main reflector, a dual-band feed and the subreflectors (SRs). The dual-band feed, which includes a higher-band circular waveguide and a lower-band coaxial horn, is employed to illuminate the SRs. The metallic elliptical surface serves as the SR in the higher band, whereas the lower-band SR is a planar reflectarray. Consequently, a dual-band reflector antenna with a focal-to-diameter (F/D) of 0.2 is designed. According to the simulated results, the proposed reflector antenna achieves the gain higher than 30 dBi and 43dBi at 16 GHz and 77 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Radiation Dissipation on Double-Crossed Bowtie Antenna for THz Bolometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Bolometer is a thermal detector that senses the change in the resistance of a metallic film caused by the temperature rise. The sensitivity of a bolometer is affected by the capability of the coupled antenna to absorb the THz radiation, thus optimally transferring the energy to the bolometer and raising its temperature. Aiming for the detection and imaging applications at 1 THz, a novel double-crossed bowtie antenna is proposed. The antenna is coupled to a Ti bolometer to absorb the incident THz radiation. A numerical study is performed based on the power dissipated in the bolometer. The results show that double-crossed bowtie could improve the absorption rate by 25 % compared to a conventional bowtie antenna when the incident radiation has dual polarization at the x- and y-axis. This research demonstrates the prospect of double-crossed bowtie antenna to enhance and tune THz absorption in bolometric-based detection with great potential in the application of real-time imaging.

articleTitle: Applications of Contactless Characteristics of Gap Waveguides in Mechanical Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Three reconfigurable transmission lines (TLs) (a sheath rectangular waveguide, a movable rectangular waveguide, and a universal-joint circular waveguide) have been proposed in this work to extend the applications of gap waveguide technology in the domain of mechanical reconfigurability. These three reconfigurable TLs enable movements of waveguide ports through mechanisms of sheathing, displacement, and rotation without wave propagation leakage, and thereby provide possibilities for antenna mechanical reconfigurability.

articleTitle: Wideband Design of 2×2-element Post WallWaveguide Slot Subarray for 350-GHz band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband design of a 2×2-element post wall waveguide slot subarray for the 350-GHz band. The subarray is fed by a corporate feed circuit and is composed of a cavity and slots. The subarray is analyzed by a hybrid method of moments and finite element method and optimized by a genetic algorithm. The subarray shows 11% reflection bandwidth where reflection is below -14dB. In the future, we plan to analyze the overall structural model and evaluate the actual measurements.

articleTitle: A compact wideband circularly polarized MIMO antenna with polarization diversity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The present work describes a two-element MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) antenna with circular polarization, which operates in the sub6 GHz 5G frequency range. The antenna design consists of two printed monopole antennas which are arranged in the mirror position with a spacing distance of 0.057 λ0 at the lowest operating frequency (where λ0 represents free space wavelength). A parasitic element has been deployed to achieve the circular polarization. A flat reflector is installed in the back of the antenna to improve the antenna gain in the boresight direction. The 10dB impedance bandwidth overlapped with 3dB axial ratio bandwidth is 38.1%, ranging from 3.4 to 5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Primal-Dual Interior Point Method for Efficient Probe Weighting in MIMO OTA Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In over-the-air (OTA) performance testing, the pre-faded synthesis (PFS) method is widely used to reconstruct the spatial profiles of the target channel by assigning appropriate power weights to each probe. Most research uses general-purpose solvers, e.g., CVX, for accurate probe weighting. These off-the-shelf solvers use various interior point methods (IPMs) to solve convex problems but at the cost of consuming significant amounts of time due to their general-purpose nature. This paper presents a specific probe weighting algorithm based on the primal-dual IPM (PD-IPM). The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves high computational efficiency for probe weighting with the same level of accuracy as CVX.

articleTitle: Focal Region Ray Tracing of a Negative Refractive Index Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A negative refractive index (NRI) lens antenna is known to provide a thin lens shape compared to conventional lens antenna. By using a NRI lens antenna, a good multi-beam characteristic is expected as a result. To obtain the multi-beam results, best feed position should be determined by using a focal region ray tracing method. For different refractive index, n values of -√2 and -3, the focal region rays of concave-plano lens are obtained. The locus of best feed positions is determined. The results obtained are discussed for future implementation to achieve a good multi-beam radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Design and SAR of Sub-6 GHz Multiband Antenna with Slots and Defected Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The sub-6 GHz multiband microstrip antenna with slotted radiating element, air gap insertion, and defected ground plane, which is fed by coaxial presented in this article. Initially, the design is based on the common microstrip rectangular antenna, which then L slot is implemented to obtain multiband, and loop slot, defected ground and air gap loaded to improve bandwidth. This designed antenna utilizing Rogers RT5880 substrate has multi-operating frequencies within sub-6 GHz, which are 1 GHz, 1.4 GHz, 2.8 GHz, and 3.5 GHz. The designed antenna has a maximum 7.8 % impedance bandwidth at 3.5 GHz with the highest gain of 4.9 dBi. The design and analyses are executed, and the specific absorption rate (SAR) is studied using CST Microwave Studio (MWS).

articleTitle: Design of a Rectifying Metasurface for Wireless Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel rectifying metasurface structure for RF energy harvesting at the Wi-Fi band is proposed. The metasurface structure unit adopts a double ring structure, and receiving resistors (or diodes) are placed between the units. The RF energy harvesting efficiency at 2.45GHz can reach 97%. It has the characteristics of polarization insensitivity, and the efficiency is still above 80% when the oblique incidence angle is 60°. Compared with traditional rectennas, this structure eliminates the complex power combining network by directly connecting the rectifying diodes to the metasurface unit, and is more concise. When incident wave input power is 0dBm, its rectification efficiency can get 48%. This metasurface structure can work in a complex RF environment, and has great potential for wireless power supply applications in low-power sensor networks.

articleTitle: Wireless Channel Customization using Direction- Of-Arrival Sensing Method and Reflective EM Skin
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a cost-effective direction-of-arrival (DoA) measurement method at 28 GHz using a Rotman lens to address challenges in implementing reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) for enhancing wireless communication coverage. By diagnosing an environment and installing electromagnetic (EM) skins, it demonstrates how to create a customized wireless channel to efficiently improve wireless coverage. When comparing simulation and measurement results, a maximum S21 enhancement of 14.6 dB is observed in the simulation and an increase of 12.1 dB in received power is confirmed in the measurement similarly. Furthermore, the difference of the EM skin locations between the simulation and the measurement validates that the measurement is much more critical in understanding the propagation characteristics of the actual environment under realistic conditions.

articleTitle: Low-cost Reflective Metasurface with Rotatable Unit Elements for 5G mmW Signal Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel Ka-band radio frequency reflectarray is proposed to refocus the radiation fields from antennas in the near- and far zones of the reflectarray at the Ka frequency band. The forming unit-cell structure consists of two double-layered and single-layered boards. The required phase shifts are produced by circularly rotating the phase delay lines on the single-layered board with a z-shaped pattern, which makes it easy for mass production. To demonstrate the reflectarray behavior, a 21x21 reflectarray antenna operating at 28 GHz is designed. By properly arranging the array elements, the cross-polarization is reduced. The simulated results show 4% 1 dB and 7% 3 dB gain bandwidths. The maximum gain at 28 GHz is 25.6 dB, and the aperture efficiency is approximately 37.8%.

articleTitle: A Method to Improve the Axial Ratio of Microstrip Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to improve the axial ratio of the circular polarized microstrip patch antenna, a method is proposed in this paper. By changing the size of the rectangular slot loaded on one side of the top corner of the non chamfered patch, the axial ratio of the circular polarized microstrip patch antenna element can be improved by more than 0.6dB. Use this unit to form 2 × 2 array, the array’s axial ratio can be improved by more than 1dB. Finally, the array’s axial ratio is less than 2dB and its gain reaches 10dBic (in 2.4-2.5 GHz). The simulation results are in good agreement with the experimental results.

articleTitle: 150 GHz Embedded Patch Antenna With Radiation From the Substrate Edge for Antenna-in-Package
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, multi-element antenna modules consisting of multiple antenna elements and RF front ends have been considered to satisfy high-gain, wide-angle antennas in the subterahertz band. This paper discusses a loop-shaped patch antenna with radiation from the substrate edge. The antenna is a substrate-embedded antenna made of copper foil and vias, and good antenna characteristics with a frontal gain of 8.4 dBi and a half angle of 62 degrees at 157.75 GHz are achieved by simulation.

articleTitle: Efficient Wireless Power Transfer System for Mobile Devices: Asymmetric and Planar Magnetic Resonance Coupling Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an asymmetric, doublelayered, and fully planar magnetic resonance coupling-based (MRC) wireless power transfer (WPT) system that operates at 13.56 MHz. The transmitter is designed on a FR-4 substrate measuring 100 mm × 100 mm, while the receiver is developed on a flexible polyimide substrate with a footprint of 50 mm × 50 mm. Complete planarization is achieved by applying printed spiral coils on both the transmitter and receiver. At a separation distance of 60 mm between the transmitting and receiving coils, a maximum measured efficiency of 67% was attained. The thinness of the polyimide substrate allows the receiving unit to be compact, making it easily compatible with various mobile charging devices.

articleTitle: Consideration of Feeding Element Structure of Circularly Polarized MACKEY Q-type
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metasurface antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY) is a functional miniature antenna. The MACKEY is constructed by combining an artificial magnetic conductor substrate with a dipole antenna, which allows it to operate even on metals. The MACKEY Q-type was proposed as a miniaturized 1/4-wavelength square model of the MACKEY with a short-circuit plate. In this paper, we propose an antenna that radiates circularly polarized waves by varying the angle and position of the feeding element of the MACKEY Q-type.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO Channel Sounder for Sub-THz Based on Virtual Array Concept
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The sub-THz frequency spectrum ranging from 90 GHz to 300 GHz offers huge untapped frequency band, up to several tens of GHz, which is highly promising for achieving extremely high data rate transmission. Therefore, sub-THz technology is considered as one of the key technology candidates for beyond 5G communication systems. However, sub-THz communication relies on dominant propagation path in the environments. It is essential to identify and track the dominant paths in the channel to maintain the communication link. Understanding the spatial profiles of the channel is therefore essential. In this work, we present a long range sub-THz channel sounder we developed at Aalborg University Denmark, which is capable of capturing the spatial profile of the channel with high spatial resolution based on the virtual array concept. The channel sounder is experimentally validated in field measurements.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Wideband Antenna with Reliable Experimental Microwave Imaging for Early Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband antenna utilizing a stubline and notch-staircase shape on the radiating patch for microwave imaging application. The antenna array consisting of up to 12 units is arranged around foam and glass marble objects, mimicking a breast phantom and tumor, respectively. Microwave Radar-based Imaging Toolbox (MERIT) is used for generating detected object images. The proposed antenna demonstrates a fractional bandwidth of 130.1% and a realized gain ranging from 1 to 5 dB across the frequency range of 1.78 to 8.41 GHz. Simulation results highlight the time domain performance, including input and received signal response, as well as group delay. The study further establishes that increasing the number of antennas enhances image resolution. The findings showcase the potential of the proposed wideband antenna in early breast cancer detection.

articleTitle: L-band Array with Full Digital Beamforming Using the Xilinx RFSoC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An L-band antenna array with eight elements and full digital beamforming using the Xilinx RFSoC is presented. Details of the implementation in the hardware, high level synthesis, and the software are provided. Digital beamforming is at the element level without the need for phaseshifters or true time delays.

articleTitle: Classical Electrodynamics Formalism to Derive Quantum Mechanics Amplitude
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In some concrete examples such as the classical Compton backscattering, quantum mechanics phenomena can be also derived from rules given entirely inside the classical territory. In this paper the quantum mechanics amplitude and propagator were derived from classical electrodynamics without any condition of quantization. For this end the integer-order Bessel functions have been employed. In addition, the imaginary prescription encompassing the well-known quantum procedure is also derived. The results of this paper would corroborate the idea that classical formalisms are useful to attack problems as quantum mechanics does.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Tri-Polarization Reconfigurable Annular Ring Antenna Based on Slow-wave Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized tri-polarization reconfigurable antenna implemented by slow-wave transmission line (SW-TL)-based annular ring is presented. Due to the slow-wave propagation characteristics of the SW-TL, the size of the developed antenna is reduced by 50.9% compared with a conventional annular ring antenna. A narrow slot along the – y-axis is etched on the annular ring and two PIN diodes are utilized to reconfigure one linearly polarized (LP) state and two circularly polarized state. Simulation results manifest that the overlapped bandwidth for the three polarization states is 1.08%, and the peak gain within the overlapped bandwidthis 7.68 dBi.

articleTitle: Propagation of potentiometric signals based on electric conduction of sea water
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research proposes a seawater wireless communication system that utilizes the electric conductivity in saltwater in a space electrically isolated from the open sea. An insulator (polyvinyl chloride) tube with a length of 1-25 meter was filled with an electrolyte solution to evaluate its characteristics based on electrolyte concentration. In 1 meter tube, the output signal was stronger with higher NaCl concentrations, and an output of 0.14 V was obtained with an input of 1 V voltage amplitude and 1MHz frequency for 3.5% NaCl(aq). An equivalent circuit of the experimental system using the polyvinyl chloride pipe was created, and a bandpass filter was designed using an inductor. As a result, with a frequency of 1.1 MHz and a voltage amplitude of 1 V, a 1 V output was successfully obtained. In a large area propagation, the signal characteristics were measured using an electrically seawater pool from the open sea with dimensions of 25 m×15 m ×0.9 m. Signals with a transmission range of 15 meters, input voltage of 50 V, and frequency of 5–10 MHz were able to be transmitted with a signal strength of −40 to −50 dB. Similarly, when an inductor was inserted as a bandpass filter, a signal with a strength of −25 dB, which was 33 dB greater than when no inductor was present, was transmitted at 1.5 MHz, which is enough for real-time video communication.

articleTitle: The Study of High Gain Transparent Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this article, a 1x4 wideband transparent array antenna for 5G N78 (3.3-3.8 GHz) band was designed. The design utilizes a low-loss transparent dielectric and a multilayer dielectric structure, with a conductor layer of antennas plated on its top and bottom surfaces. Metal mesh is used to increase the antenna's transparency, the optical transparency (OT) of the metal mesh is 82.6-93.3%. The antenna bandwidth (return loss more than 10 dB) is 0.71-1.0 GHz, the peak gain is 7-10.5 dBi. Furthermore, compared with solid antennas in simulations, the meshed antennas showed an increase in bandwidth of 0.18 to 0.47 GHz, while the Peak Gain decreased by 1 to 3.5 dB in the n78 frequency band.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Circularly Polarized Folded Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain circularly polarized folded reflectarray (CPFRA) centered at 37 GHz is developed for satellite and point-to-point communications. The proposed CPFRA is consisted of a circular polarization selective surface (CPSS) on the top, a broadband reflectarray panel on the bottom, and a broadband CP feed fulfilled using a meander-line circular polarizer and a linearly-polarized horn. The CPSS is designed based on the Pierrot structure, while the phasing element of the reflectarray is created by using a fan-shaped cross surrounded and coupled by a circular ring. The phasing element only requires a single layer which reduces the cost and complexity. In addition, the combination of the cross and ring enhances the resonance of the unit cell, which results in an improved bandwidth. The phase coverage of the unit cell is about 500°, while the reflection loss is maintained within 0.5 dB. The measured results show that the CPFRA can achieve a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 9.45%, an aperture efficiency of 30.6%, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 12.2%, and a peak gain of 26.8 dBic at the broadside direction.

articleTitle: Misalignment Study of Dual-Band SIMO- and MIMO- WPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the misalignment study of single input-multi output (SIMO) and a multi input-multi output (MIMO) defected ground structure based dual-band wireless power transfer (DGS-WPT) system is discussed. As a case study, WPT systems operating at 300 MHz / 700 MHz are designed in CST and prototyped. In this case, the best system efficiency is obtained for the separation of h = 18 mm between the transmitter (TX) and receivers (RXs). The misalignment study includes a detailed analysis of shift in the lateral and angular position of RXs with respect to the TX. It was observed that the misalignment has more negative impact on the performance of SIMO than the MIMO type WPT system.

articleTitle: Efficiency Improvement by Loading Impedances for Dual feeding Magnetic Field Coupling WPT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In magnetic coupling wireless power transfer (WPT), the ability to transmit power in both directions from a single power transmission coil is a desirable feature, leveraging the generation of magnetic fields on both sides of the coil. This study investigates the impact of impedance loading on the coils used for magnetic field-coupled WPT, specifically focusing on a bi-directional simultaneous power supply. The aim is to optimize the reactance and capacitance values to maximize wireless power transmission efficiency at different distances between the coils: 10 mm, 75 mm, and 150 mm. The analysis reveals that the efficiency at a distance of 75 mm approaches the optimized value obtained at a distance of 10 mm.

articleTitle: Effects of Drone Height Fluctuations on Detection of Respiratory Vital Signs Using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: After disasters such as earthquakes, the highest priority in post-disaster is to find and save survivors trapped under the rubble. Vital sign detection using radar-drones potentially contributes as a tool for helping live victims faster. Radar Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) is an example of a radar system that was studied for vital sign detection. When the radar is attached to the drone that functions to convey the radar over a disaster area, the fluctuation of the drone elevation during flight potentially contributes a doppler interference to the radar. In this research, the effect of drone height fluctuation on vital sign detection is investigated by conducting a simulation and laboratory modeling. The result shows that the drone height fluctuation potentially degrades the radar detection performance. The study also shows that the information on drone height fluctuation helps mitigate the effect on the vital sign detection result.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Plural Circular Array Antenna to Control the Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An array antenna composed of radiating elements arranged on concentric circles is proposed in this paper. Its equivalence to an aperture antenna is deduced so that the radiation pattern can be controlled by shaping the excitation of the array elements. Its validity is shown by simulation, and the radiation pattern is well illustrated in a two-dimensional diagram of contour.

articleTitle: A Portable 3D-Printed Dielectric Lens Antennas for Liquid-Mixture Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) method is utilized in this research to present dielectric lens antennas that were 3D printed. The ultra-wideband (UWB) stub antenna’s antenna characteristic is intended to be improved by the 3D-printed dielectric lens antennas. The proportion of ethanol in the liquid mixture sample is categorized using the transmission-line measuring technique. The device-under-test (DUT) is placed between two 3D-printed dielectric lens antennas. The glass bottle is filled with a 100-ml liquid sample and covered with a plastic cap. The 3D EM Simulation CST Studio is used to optimize the 10 mm gap between the dielectric lens antennas and the DUT. Six concentrations of the ethanol/water mixture, such as empty, 60%, 65%, 70%, and 80%, are measured to examine the measurement system. The measurement outcomes indicate the various S21 (transmission coefficient) levels between 9 GHz and 11 GHz. According to the trend of the suggested system, the level of the transmission coefficient, S21, will change downward when the proportion of ethanol is increased. Several better advantages, such as a non-destructive method, non-contact measurement, and support with a real-time monitoring system, are provided by the transmission-line measuring methodology using 3D-printed dielectric lens antennas.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Transmissive and Reflective Electromagnetic Surface with Complete Control of Amplitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a unit cell with high efficiency for simultaneous transmission and reflection (STAR) surface operating at millimeter wave frequencies. Applying two perpendicular metallic gratings in the top and bottom of a dual-C shaped resonator, the unit cells can simultaneously control amplitude and phase of reflected and transmitted waves by adjusting the geometrical parameters. This structure can be leveraged to realize full-space electromagnetic manipulation in a simple way for potential applications in mutlifunctional devices.

articleTitle: Multi-mode Combinations for a Millimeter-wave Dielectric Resonator Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) in the millimeter-wave (mmW) band due to the combination of multi-mode. Traditional aperture-coupled DRAs are excited by a regular rectangular aperture, which usually creates one mode and thus contributes to a narrow bandwidth. The proposed method widens the coupling aperture under the DRA, which excites both fundamental mode and higher-order mode of the DRA simultaneously. This results in good impedance matching over a wide frequency range. In addition, it solves the bandwidth limitation of a DRA element in high frequencies. To increase the number of modes, a parasitic metallic patch is placed on the top surface of the DRA. By combining the fundamental mode and the higher-order mode of the DRA with the patch mode, the proposed antenna element achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 41.5% from 24.7 to 37.6 GHz (for the reflection coefficient ≤ -10 dB) with a maximum gain of 7.8 dBi. Throughout the entire operating band, stable broadside radiation patterns with cross-polarization levels under -35 dB (E-plane) and -18 dB (H-plane) are observed.

articleTitle: Design of Beam Steering Resonator Antenna for 5G using Switch-Coupling Parasitic Element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed beam steering MIMO antenna for 5G application at 3.5 GHz of mid-band. The beam steering performance is based on the integration of the driven parasitic element and switches. The RT Duroid 5880 is used as substrate with thickness 1.57mm. The geometry of the center rectangular patch antenna to achieve the desired resonance frequency which 3.5GHz. The integration of the HPNP 4005 PIN Diode with the parasitic element is tested which the antenna manages to steer the direction at -30°, 0° and +30° with gain of 6.4dBi. In the proposed design, a simple biasing circuit is employed to control all the PIN Diodes switches. The proposed MMO antenna could be potential for 5G application.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Indoor Positioning System Based on WiFi Signal Strength Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multiple indoor positioning approaches have been developed over time due to the increased business interest in indoor location-based services (ILBS). As the Global Positioning System (GPS) signal is unavailable indoors, several other signals have been introduced. Due to the widespread deployment of wireless Local Area Networks (LANs), WiFi appears as a potential option. WiFi fingerprinting, in particular, has garnered significant attention recently because it does not require a line-of- sight path between the transmitter and receiver. Therefore, it achieves promising performance in a complicated interior environment. In this paper, we proposed an Indoor Positioning System's (IPS) tracking based on WiFi fingerprinting and examined it in a house and office environments. The approach proposed in this paper may be directly implemented in office and factory environments at minimal cost using existing infrastructure to track the movement of workers for productivity monitoring.

articleTitle: Superdirective Unidirectional Mixed-Multipole Antenna Designs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Highly directive antenna systems are being sought to address the perceived needs of the NextG wireless systems and their applications. However, practical alternatives to complex, power hungry phased arrays are truly desired. Unidirectional mixed-multipole antennas (UMMAs) offer superdirective performance characteristics with high efficiency in a compact format. Superdirective uniform end-fire arrays of active closely-spaced equal-length idealized wire dipoles will be exemplified as reference cases. The Rayleigh quotient (RQ) method typically used to determine their amplitude coefficients and its recent extension to achieve unidirectional outcomes will be discussed. UMMA designs that are approaching those ideal performance characteristics will be presented. These efforts further confirm recent research advances demonstrating practical superdirective systems are achievable.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Meandered Line-Slot Patch Antenna for On- and In-Metal RFID Tag Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel hybrid patch antenna that is embeddable in metal is proposed for radio frequency identification (RFID) tagging applications. The antenna features a simple design, consisting of a meandered line and a complementary slot surrounding a shorted radiating patch. This hybrid patch antenna can easily achieve high compactness by tuning the dimensions of the meandered line. The complementary slot is also playing a crucial role in enhancing the broadside radiation by promoting fringing fields from the radiating patch. As a result, the tag antenna becomes less sensitive to the cavity walls at surrounding. The proposed tag antenna, with dimensions of 30 × 30 × 3.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, can achieve high realized gain of −0.6 dBi when placed on a 200 × 200 × 20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> metal block or in a 100 × 100 × 10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> recessed metallic cavity. Although reducing the cavity’s size and depth can cause antenna’s realized gain to deteriorate to −2.5 dBi, the antenna’s resonant frequency remains stable at 0.915 GHz across all simulations.

articleTitle: Fast Optimization Method of Irregular Phased Antenna Array with Low Side-Lobe Level
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel optimization method of irregular phased antenna array with low side-lobe level is proposed in this paper. The method is divided into two parts. At first, an Element Exchange Algorithm is proposed to achieve a fast generation of the irregular array tiling with high entropy, which is beneficial to grating-lobe suppression. Secondly, the amplitude and phase excitations are optimized through convex optimization (CVX) theory to realize low side-lobe level (SLL). The effectivity of the proposed method is verified in 16×16 irregular phased antenna arrays composed of 2-element, 4-element and 8-element subarrays.

articleTitle: Analysis of Indoor Transmission Characteristics in Beam Modulation Using Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we evaluated the transmission characteristics of low-power beam modulation communication with millimeter waves for IoT devices in the room environment. This was proposed as a solution to the bandwidth shortage caused by the increasing number of IoT devices.

articleTitle: A Scalar Impedance Surface Antenna for Far-field Radial Vortex Beam Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Holographic impedance surfaces (HIS) have the potential to achieve multifunctional multiplexing. This letter proposes a low-profile scalar impedance surface antenna to achieve far-field multiplexing of different radial orbital angular momentum (OAM). The antenna is designed by holographic method, and the far-field scalar vortex beam of +1 mode at 30° and +2 mode OAM at -30° is realized by the regular arrangement of surface impedance. A monopole antenna is placed at the center of the surface to serve as the excitation source for the surface. A good surface impedance is obtained for the 3x3 mm2 square scalar cell at 17GHz operating frequency. The overall size of this antenna is 117x117 mm2. The reflection coefficient of this antenna is less than -10dB at 14.1-20.7 GHz and the theoretical, simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Characterization of Spatial Consistency of Millimeter-Wave Cluster Channels in an Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented the spatial consistency of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) multipath cluster channels based on propagation measurements at 24 and 60 GHz in an urban cellular environment. Understanding site-specific propagation channel characteristics at mm-wave frequencies is crucial due to its highly environment-dependent nature. This study simultaneously measured double-directional angle-resolved channel impulse responses at two frequencies moving the receiver along a route using the channel sounder with fast beam steering capability. A high-resolution path parameter estimation algorithm was used to extract multipath components (MPCs) from the measured data. Then, a clustering algorithm was applied. As a spatial consistency measure, the statistical results of the correlation distance of clusters obtained at two frequencies by cluster tracking were presented and compared with the 3GPP model.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Different Assignments for Special Configurations of 1-D Parallel Switching Matrices with Four Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This manuscript compares the assignment of well-known conventional configuration and the assignment having the best performance on adjacent output phase differences, which is a special case of the general configuration on one-dimensional parallel switching matrices with four beams having the same topology as a single-layer Butler matrix, though the values of phase shift differ.

articleTitle: Leaky Wave Slot Array Antenna Based on Gap Waveguide Technology with Cosecant Squared Pattern for 5G BTS Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel leaky-wave antenna based on utilizing the high bandwidth and low loss ridge gap waveguide concept, featuring a cosecant squared radiation pattern. The antenna is designed to operate within the frequency range of 25 GHz to 29 GHz. At the center frequency of 28 GHz, the antenna achieves a maximum gain of 10 dBi. Additionally, at a frequency of 28.8 GHz, the antenna exhibits a maximum return loss of -16.9 dB. Moreover, the proposed leaky-wave antenna demonstrates the potential of the radiation technology for 5G systems by enabling scanning angles ranging from approximately 5° to 20° across the specified frequency range. This feature highlights the versatility and suitability of the antenna for various applications in 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: A Super Thinnest Film Antenna for Wireless Communications with Notched Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This antenna which will be presented is created on a thin-film substrate. It has a dielectric constant of 3.01, a loss tangent of 0.016 and a thickness of 0.056 mm. which is extremely thinner than others. A normal structure is circular patch monopole antenna operates in range 1.3-18.7 GHz easily to cover WPAN, WBAN, and UWB. By adding a C-shaped slot for notched characteristics of Wi-Fi band 2.4 GHz. The proposed antenna can be applied well to the automobile. It still has excellent performance when mounted on the windshield.

articleTitle: Radiation Field from a Metaloop Antenna with a Traveling-Wave Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the radiation field from a metaloop antenna, using a generalized loop antenna model. It is assumed that a forward current flows without attenuation. The investigation is performed at the nion and hion frequencies, where the peripheral length is one guided wavelength. We focus on two current cases: C-s type current and C-t type current. The radiation field generated on the antenna axis normal to the antenna plane is formulated for these currents. It is found that, when C-s and C-t type currents coexist, the radiation field is increased at the nion frequency and decreased at the hion frequency.

articleTitle: Genetic-CNN based fault diagnosis in antenna array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Rise of deep learning techniques for providing solution in the domain of prediction or diagnosing, motivated author to utilize convolutional neural network (CNN) a deep learning technique to detect and locate fault in an antenna array. In this experimental analysis CNN hyper-parameters are optimized by genetic algorithm and the result of fault diagnosis are compared with grid search optimized support vector machine.

articleTitle: Dual-Band MIMO Decagonal C-Shaped CSRR Metamaterial Textile Antenna for WLAN and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study proposed an enhanced two-port dual-band textile Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna integrated with a metamaterial unit cell of symmetric decagonal C-shaped Complementary Split-Ring Resonator (CSRR) structure in terms of gain. The proposed MIMO antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 6.3% and a maximum up to 18.2% for lower and upper bands, respectively, at port 1. Mutual Coupling (MC) of less than -20 dB for both ports is obtained. The proposed antenna offers high realized gain of 5.6 dBi and 8 dBi at 2.45 GHz and 3.5 GHz, respectively, compared to existing dual-band MIMO textile antenna. Good diversity characteristics in respect of Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) less than 0.001, and Diversity Gain (DG) of about 10 dB are achieved.

articleTitle: Independent, Simultaneous Operation of Phased Array Without Grating Lobes and Beam Squint from f1 to 2f1 Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an unprecedented phased array for millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless communication, capable of independent and simultaneous beamsteering in the 24-30 GHz and 39-50 GHz frequency ranges without grating lobes or beam squint is presented. The design employs a newly devised compact, low-loss, high-selective coupler (CLSC) feed network. The 1 × 4 antenna array exhibits peak realized gain of 9 dBi at 24 GHz and 12 dBi at 48 GHz, along with a scanning angle of +/- 45 degrees for both frequencies. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to demonstrate phased arrays operating simultaneously without grating lobes in the f1 to 2f1 frequency range.

articleTitle: Design of a Wireless Passive Temperature Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design scheme for a passive wireless temperature measurement system in high-temperature environments. A slotted cylindrical resonator is used as the sensor, and a high-gain horn antenna is used as the external excitation source. Simulation results show that the system can achieve a test distance of 58 mm and sensitivity up to 386.35 MHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>@17.8 GHz. The proposed temperature measurement system has a simple structure, high sensitivity, and long contact distance, and it can be used for temperature measurement from 25 °C to 700 °C in harsh environments.

articleTitle: A Sub-6GHz 8x8 MIMO Antenna Array for 5G Mobile Phone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents a sub-6GHz MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) antenna array for 5G (fifth generation) mobile phone. The antenna comprises an invert-F with a serpentine arm and a L-shape slot antenna. The measured 6-dB impedance bandwidth is from 3.23 to 5.41 GHz and covers n77/78/79 bands in 5G NR (new radio) bands. Those antennas are arranged on two side-edge of the mobile phone. The MIMO antenna has a low transmission coefficient of the two adjacent antennas below 15 dB.

articleTitle: RF Performance Test of Sub-6 GHz Switching System for Multiple Concurrent Users on a Single Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study aims to develop a switching system that enables the simultaneous measurement of various devices using a vector network analyzer (VNA). Although the VNA plays an important role in the production of RF equipment, the existing system is limited to a single user, leading to be low efficiency and high cost. To overcome this limitation, we present a multi-user switching system, allowing eight users to concurrently share a single VNA. The developed switching system has been validated by measuring insertion loss, return loss, and isolation.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Microstrip Comb-Line Array Antenna with Low Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a bottleneck-shaped radiating element in designing a comb-line array antenna with a low sidelobe level in the millimeter-wave band. The conventional wide rectangular element has transversely flowing currents in it, deriving unavoidable radiation conductance components by the transverse currents, and making the low sidelobe design difficult. However, the proposed element has ignorable radiation conductance caused by transverse currents, and this makes it challenging to design the comb-line array antenna with accurately tapered amplitude distribution. To show the usability of the proposed elements in designing tapered amplitude distribution, the proposed elements are applied to the array having Taylor distributions with -20 dB sidelobe level and the performances are measured. The array using the conventional rectangular element is also designed and measured for comparison.

articleTitle: Effect of Angle Detection on Respiration Vital Sign Measurement Using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In implementing radar system for non-contact human respiration need to consider the radar placement in the monitoring area. The radar placement in the monitoring area may cause the measurement to be conducted with various angle detection. The effect of angle detection on respiration measurement using Frequency Continuous Wave Radar (FMCW) is reported in this paper. The laboratory experiments using 24 GHz FMCW radar were carried out in investigating the angle detection effect. This paper presents the results of respiratory detection using FMCW radar that was performed on several angle detection. Angle detection influences detection performance. For improving the detection accuracy, the correction is required.

articleTitle: 3D Numerical Simulation of Radar Response from Corroded Rebar in Concrete
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Three-dimensional numerical simulation of radar responses from corroded rebar in concrete is carried out to theoretically verify the feasibility of nondestructive inspection of reinforced concrete using ultra-wideband (UWB) radar. The FDTD method is used as the analysis method. The effectiveness of radar-based corrosion estimation is verified by investigating the relationship between the progress of corrosion and the distortion of the response waveform.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Display-Integrated FMCW Radar for Hand Gesture Recognition in Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a display-integrated radar for hand gesture recognition (HGR) in mobile devices. The array antennas of the proposed radar are implemented in dead space, which is the edge part of the display panel to overcome lack of space problem in mobile devices. The proposed radar module is fabricated, and by signal processing, distinct four micro-signatures are generated for each gesture. The performance of HGR of our radar is verified by training and testing the micro-signatures using machine learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Electromagnetic Response of Stent Antenna in Endovascular Aneurysm Repair
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study introduces a novel stent antenna system for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). The stent antenna consists of meshed rings formed by multiple helical wires connected to a single feed wire, enabling controlled current distribution. It offers improved antenna characteristics, including omnidirectional radiation, high gain, and optimal impedance matching. Simulation and measurement results validate the performance of the stent antenna across the frequency range of 850-950 MHz, including ISM 868 and 915 MHz bands. This research demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed stent antenna for EVAR in AAA treatment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation of Transmission Characteristics in Flip-Chip Bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the flip-chip bonding, which connects the GSG pads of the chip and substrate with solder bumps of 40 um in height, was simulated and evaluated the high-frequency transmission characteristics. The transmission coefficient S21 was evaluated between GSG pads in the chip and substrate. It was found that below 100 GHz, S11<-10 dB and S21>-1 dB, and the transmission characteristics are good, while at higher frequencies, the transmission characteristic gradually deteriorate.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results on the Impact of Grouping in Multilateration Positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents preliminary results on the impact of signal grouping in multilateration (MLAT) positioning. MLAT is a surveillance system for estimating aircraft positions. This system deploys multiple receiver stations that detect signals from onboard transponders and calculate aircraft positions based on the time difference of arrival. In this paper, we discuss the evaluation methods for MLAT performance and show the influence of signal grouping on the reception status.

articleTitle: Estimating Relative Permittivity of Material Filled in Waveguide Using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a compressed-sensing based method to estimate the relative permittivity of a material filling up a waveguide. Two monopole antennas are placed at both ends of the waveguide, and the S-parameters between the antennas are measured. Relative permittivity is estimated by applying compressed sensing to the frequency characteristics of the S21, where two-dimensional bins for distance and relative permittivity are defined to find unknown parameters. The simulation result showed that this technique can estimate the relative permittivity within a 7.3% error.

articleTitle: Wideband Reconfigurable BOR Antenna Compound
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-profile wideband reconfigurable antenna compound is investigated, where the height above the ground plane is less than 0.09 wavelength at the operating lowest frequency. The compound is composed of a fed BOR (body of revolution) and multiple parasitic elements printed on a thin dielectric substrate. The terminal point of each parasitic element is connected to the ground plane through an on-off switching circuit. The omnidirectional beam generated from the BOR can be tilted in the elevation plane and steered in the azimuth plane by changing on-off state of the parasitic elements. The proposed compound operates across a wide frequency band of approximately 35%.

articleTitle: Single-Shot Method for the Analysis of Non-Linear Circuits in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper we are presenting an analysis method for studying a rectenna circuit when it is excited by harmonic or non-harmonic waves. An ultra wideband antenna is used to capture the power and is transferred to a half wave rectifier through a matching network. The RF-DC conversion efficiency of the proposed method is compared and verified with the same quantity obtained by using the conventional approach using a sinusoidal waveform.

articleTitle: Radio Propagation Modeling of an Island
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the propagation modelling efforts of an island in Malaysia, where uneven terrain exists. An open source software, namely, MATLAB was utilized in the modelling process to vary parameters such as distance, frequency, and antenna heights, among others. For this purpose, a graphical user interface (GUI) was first created to allow for customized values to be input to different models such as Free Space, Hata, and Okumura models in plotting path loss. The obtained results are subsequently used to train a machine-learning model to do propagation prediction. We have adopted a non-artificial neural network based machine-learning model, which uses a regression algorithm that is common for propagation prediction. A validation check shows that our results are compatible with other published results. This work demonstrates the benefits of using machine learning to explore more possibilities in conducting propagation modelling and prediction across different environments.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Permittivity Measurement Using Lens Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A free-space measurement system based on lens antennas for measuring the complex permittivity of anisotropic materials in the band from 8.5 to 12.4 GHz is proposed.
