The multireflect-thru method is used to calibrate the measurement system in the whole band. Only the transmission coefficient (S21) is used to solve the permittivity. The validity and accuracy of the system for measuring permittivity are verified by the measurement results of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE).

articleTitle: An Energy Harvester Using Rolling Magnets with Integrated Rotor and Stator for Wireless Sensor System on a Marine Shaft
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel energy harvester (EH) using rolling magnets, which can supply power to a wireless sensor system (WSS) for monitoring the status of rotating ship shafts. The EH consists of twelve coils and seven magnets, which generate energy from the shaft's motion and supply it to the WSS for monitoring the shaft system's status. We installed the EH on a 20 cm diameter shaft and obtained a transferred voltage of 0.84 V and an output power of 47.2 mW with 2000 turns of each coil, despite a rotation speed of 25 rpm and a 3 mm air gap. The proposed EH shows great potential for monitoring rotating shaft on ships.

articleTitle: High Power BandPass Filter Design for 5G Satellite Based Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper an all metallic band pass filter with high power handling capability is proposed. The operating frequency bandwidth of the design can be determined by tuning the proposed modulation parameters of the ridge in the waveguide. As a proof of concept, a bandwidth from 11GHz up to 29GHz is selected to force the waveguide to operate in single mode scenario to mitigate multi mode dispersion by simply adding a transition from ridge waveguide to a normal one.

articleTitle: Extraction Formula for Microstrip Antenna as Soil Water Content Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Assessing and monitoring the soil fertility level relies on the crucial factor of soil water content, as it helps prevent late detection of water deficit, which could lead to crop failure. A cost-effective and efficient method to measure soil water content has been proposed in this research which using microstrip antenna as indirect measurement. The findings indicate that microstrip antenna have potential to serve as highly sensitivities sensors to precisely measure soil water content by analyze the electric characteristic of the soil, dielectric permittivity. As further investigation, it is essential to established connection between dielectric permittivity and the antenna parameter, specifically the resonant frequency. This research has successfully extracted a formula by examining the relationship between both parameters, enabling the estimation of soil water content percentage. This paper shows that extraction formula can be obtained by considering theoretical approaches, numerical results and the discrepancies between them. The research demonstrates the proposed microstrip antenna sensor and derived extraction formulation can achieve accurate detection of soil water content.

articleTitle: Influence of Scattering Order on ILS Localizer Using Ray-Tracing Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the influence of the scattering order of electromagnetic waves on the performance of the ray-tracing method (RTM). ILS Localizer (LOC) is a ground-based navigation aid to guide aircraft in airports. LOC emits analogue signals, and transmitted signals are distorted by multipaths caused by obstacles. To numerically simulate the interference of electromagnetic waves in ILS systems, an appropriate scattering order must be considered to obtain results close to the actual values. In this paper, we show differences of scattering orders and their effects on the numerical results of RTM. Based on the numerical results, we discuss the elements of the electromagnetic field that are vitally important in simulating LOC signal interference using RTM.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide with Series Fed Antenna for Millimeter-wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the design of series feed antennas with two and four radiating elements. Both are designed to resonate at 26GHz. The proposed (1 x 2) and (1 x 4) series feed antennas are attached to a Substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). Over 0.75 mm tape around the antennas, the 0.5 mm vias diameter is attached by 0.9 mm space between visas. Gain increased from 10.6 dBi to 11.2dBi for the two elements' structure and from 13.5dBi to 14dBi for the four elements. The proposed structure encourages future work N x N elements to be developed by SIW and is used for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Microwave Energy Devices Composed of Dielectric Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave surgical energy device is excellent energy device for coagulation of biological tissue and can reduce the generation of surgical smoke during surgery. However, since they directly touch biological tissue during surgery, they are disposed of after single use for hygienic reasons. Therefore, it was considered that if microwave energy devices could be fabricated using dielectric waveguides without metallic parts, it would be possible to simplify the device structure and reduce waste in medical devices. In this study, numerical analysis confirmed that microwave surgical energy device composed of dielectric waveguide can be used for heating biological tissue.

articleTitle: Wideband Wide-Angle Polarization-Independent Metasurface for Wireless Power Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a wireless energy harvesting metasurface with wide-angle and polarization insensitivity characteristics. The proposed metasurface unit cell consists of four parts. The top layer is composed of four 90-degree metal arcs with an orthogonal X-shaped metal strip in the middle, which connects the whole patch. Four resistors on the top layer connect the four metal arcs and the arrangement is laid out on the FR-4 dielectric substrate. An air gap layer is set between the FR-4 dielectric substrate and metal ground. Experimental simulation results demonstrate that the metasurface achieves a bandwidth coverage of 4.3 GHz with a collection efficiency of more than 80% and a bandwidth coverage of 1.3 GHz with a collection efficiency of more than 90%, of which the efficiency reaches 92.7% at 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Grating lobe Analysis and Suppression of a Waveguide-Fed Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A closed-form analysis of the grating lobes of the waveguide-fed metasurface antenna is presented in this paper. Based on the closed-form analysis, a boundary condition is derived to ensure full-space beam scanning without grating lobe. Furthermore, two methods for suppressing grating lobe beyond the boundary condition are investigated.

articleTitle: Source Reconstruction Method Using Fourier Transform and Eigenmode Currents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a source reconstruction method using Fourier transform and eigenmode currents. Firstly, an equivalent current distribution over an estimation area is reconstructed via Fourier transform. The equivalent current distribution is expanded using the eigenmode currents of a small dipole array and a dipole element whose contribution to the equivalent current distribution is small is thinned. Finally, the equivalent current distribution is expanded using the eigenmode currents of the remaining dipole elements and is updated. Performance of the source reconstruction method is demonstrated via numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Compact and Ultrawideband Circularly Polarized Vertical Ground Fractal RDRA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: New compact and ultra wideband circularly polarized (CP) vertical ground Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is proposed using strip feed. Minkowski fractal till second iteration is used to make the geometry compact and partial ground plane with a slot is used to attain ultra wideband response. The CP response is obtained by attaching two strips diagonally at the ends of the DRA. The proposed CP DRA offers 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW), impedance bandwidth S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≤ -10 dB of 50% (3 - 5 GHz) and 108% (3 - 10 GHz) respectively. The proposed structure offers acceptable LHCP gain and good radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Amplitude-Phase-Coding Metasurface Reflector for Reconfigurable Multibeam Forming
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this article, we propose a reconfigurable amplitude-phase-coding metasurface (RAPM) reflector operating in the 10.8-12.2 GHz broadband. The unit of RAPM is composed of a simple three-layer structure thereby minimizing processing complexities. Through manipulation of the bias voltage applied to the PIN diode embedded into the meta-atom, active reflection amplitude and phase control are obtained. Furthermore, by employing coding sequences, the quantity of reflected beams can be dynamically adjusted from one to five in one-dimension space.

articleTitle: Air-Ground Radio Channel Analysis by Opportunistic DAPs Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for air-ground radio channel analysis at the 1090 MHz civil aviation band. Signals used by the Down-Link Aircraft Parameters (DAPs) systems, which is an air traffic control system operating at this frequency band, are passively measured and analyzed. Various information contained in DAPs signals can be exploited for radio channel analysis. As an example, aircraft roll-angle and received signal strength (RSS) were analyzed to investigate the effect of turning.

articleTitle: Dual Band Antenna Covering Millimeter Wave and Sub-6 GHz Bands for 5G Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The proposed dual-band antenna covering millimeter wave and sub-6 GHz bands is a necktie round shape patch design connected with a meandered radiating patch element at the top front with an H slot shape and a fractional or truncated ground plane at the back to enhance the antenna’s functionality and performance. The antenna is designed using CST microwave studio on a substrate Rogers 3003 with a dimension of 27.8 mm, 14mm, and thickness of 1.52 mm with a dielectric constant of 2.2 and a loss tangent of 0.0009 respectively. The proposed antenna has an ultra-wide bandwidth of 19.65 GHz covering almost all the milli meter wave bands of 23 GHz, 28 GHz, and 38 GHz (from 22.65 – 42.30 GHz) while the sub-6 GHz band has a bandwidth of 962 MHz (3.02 – 3.99 GHz) respectively. The return loss of the antenna is -31.33 dB and -49.72 dB at 3.5 GHz and 28 GHz respectively. However, this antenna is compact and combines two different frequency bands, the large frequency ratio between the millimeter wave band to the sub-6 GHz band is 8.

articleTitle: Design of a Connector for Connecting a Dielectric Waveguide and a Rectangular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Dielectric waveguides are transmission lines that have lower losses than coaxial cables at frequencies above millimeter waves. However, when connecting dielectric waveguides to network analyzers for experiments, mode conversion is required due to the different propagation modes between dielectric waveguides and coaxial connectors or rectangular waveguides. In this paper, we report the design of a connector that performs mode conversion to connect a dielectric waveguide and a rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: Wideband Class-E Power Amplifier at 54.24 MHz using Reactance Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses about reactance compensation technique. This technique is applied to conventional Class-E and able to achieve wideband Class-E operation. From the simulation result, for reactance compensated Class-E, 90% efficiency covers from 49 to 60 MHz compared to conventional Class-E which only covers from 52 to 57 MHz. Based on the result, the reactance compensation technique is promising in realizing wideband Class-E.

articleTitle: A Study of Dielectric Sensing Based on the Bi-Characteristic-Impedance Transmission Line (BCITL) Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper studies a dual-probe microstrip antenna, based on the bi-characteristic impedance transmission line (BCITL) model, applied in dielectric sensing systems. By changing dielectric constant of materials, associated scattering parameters and BCITL parameters are changes noticeably as well, enabling effective dielectric sensing. In addition, numerical results are provided to validate the proposed approach for dielectric classification.

articleTitle: A New Bidirectional Surface Design: Independent Transmission and Reflection on Both Sides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The simultaneous transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) leverages the space of both sides of the surface, extending the application of RIS. But the existing STAR-RIS is symmetrical, resulting in half of the energy being wasted in the uplink. To address this issue, we design a new asymmetrical bidirectional surface that can independently control transmission and reflection on each side. The element is comprised of three layers, including the polarization conversion layer, the grating layer, and the strip layer. Simulation results show that both the transmission and the reflection coefficient are greater than 0.55, with their phase range from 0 to 360 degrees. Furthermore, the findings highlight the significant potential for achieving substantially greater energy efficiency using the proposed surface in contrast to the STAR-RIS.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Aided Design of Handset Antennas with High Isolations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The public frequency spectrum of 2.4-2.485 GHz is shared by WLAN, Bluetooth, Micro-oven and etc. When multiple functions are integrated in one device, the isolations between antennas should be as high as possible for mutual interference. In this work, a dual-antenna system in the mobile handset working at 2.4-2.485 GHz is designed with high isolations so that they can work for different communication protocols with less requirement on the filter. The two antennas are designed on the top half of the handset to save more space for other antennas. Given the position of the first antenna, the feeding position of the second antenna is calculated based on characteristic mode theory. According to the full-wave simulation results, an isolation of above 40 dB has been achieved. The correlation coefficient is 0.03 at 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: A Derivation of Monostatic RCS of Reflectarray for Prediction of Bistatic RCS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a derivation of monostatic radar cross section (RCS) of reflectarray. In 5G, the reflectarray and reconfigurable reflectarray have gained attention to reduce the coverage holes. The reflectarray is evaluated by the bistatic RCS measurement. However, the bistatic RCS measurement is relatively complicated as compared to monostatic RCS measurement. This paper proposes the theoretical equation of monostatic RCS of reflectarray is derived to predict bistatic RCS of the reflectarray. By using these equations, the relation between the design reflection angle of bistatic RCS of the reflectarray, and the monostatic RCS of the reflectarray. The derived equations is validated by the comparison of the simulation which is the reflecarray operating at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Independent Permittivity Sensor Based on Dual T-Shaped Resonator for Solid Material Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an independent permittivity sensor for solid material characterization. The proposed sensor consists of a dual T-shaped resonator with a single port operating at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r1</inf> = 2.32 GHz as 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> resonator and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r2</inf> = 1.82 GHz as 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> resonator for direct detection which has independent performance with different sensing hotspot so it can be used independently. The permittivity of the MUT is detected directly by placing the Material Under Test (MUT) above the surface of the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> resonator. Based on measurement result, the proposed sensor can detect four different MUT independently with different sensing hotspot. This research is very useful for the characterization of solid materials independently for several applications such as biomedical, quality control and pharmaceutical industries.

articleTitle: A Broadband Low RCS Antenna Based on Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization conversion unit consisting of a notched square ring and a cross structure with different lengths is designed. An air layer is added between the dielectric substrate and the grounding plate of the unit to broaden the working bandwidth. The unit can convert the normal incident wave of linear polarization into cross polarization within 7.91-25.01 GHz, and the polarization conversion bandwidth is 103.88%. A low RCS slot array antenna based on polarization conversion metasurface has been designed, the RCS reduction can reach more than 10dB within 8.36-23.38 GHz, which is very effective in reducing RCS.

articleTitle: Design Trade-offs between Patch and Horn Antenna for Self-Sustained Wireless IoT Sensor Node
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we propose trade-offs between patch and horn antenna designs in terms of frequency, gain, power and area for self-sustained wireless IoT sensors. Regardless of having a minimum area, a single patch stub antenna cannot support self-sustained IoT-sensor operation. Similarly, the horn antenna having ≈5x more gain and ≈2x more power compared to the stub, cannot aid self-sustained operation unless a dedicated source is used. Thus, as a proof of concept, a horn antenna designed at 10dB gain with a dedicated source has been shown to harvest enough power for self-sustained operation at a reduction of ≈3.8x harvested power, ≈2.5x length and ≈2.8x width compared to that of the horn antenna at 15dB gain.

articleTitle: Shaped Radome for Wide-Angle mmWave Automotive RADAR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a novel radome concept for wide-angle mmWave automotive RADAR antennas. The resulting radomes show superior electrical performance as compared to the industry standard approach. By means of numerical computations, we show that the 5 dB beamwidth is reduced by less than 6° compared with 38° by the proposed and the standard radomes, respectively.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics Estimation for Indoor 5G Wireless Environment Including Human Body Shielding Using Parallel FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: his study aims to investigate the propagation characteristics of private 5th-generation mobile communication system (5G) frequency bands, including the human body shadowing in indoor environments. We conducted a large-scale three-dimensional numerical analysis using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method to model an indoor propagation environment containing humans and evaluate the propagation loss characteristics. The precise electric field distribution excited by a 5G transmitting antenna, which is used as the private-5 G access point, was calculated. Shadowing and scattering effects due to a real human body were evaluated in the full-wave simulations. Our simulation results show that the effect of reflected waves is significant for indoor radio propagation, and multipath fading increases significantly even though the loss due to human shielding is ameliorated.

articleTitle: Holistic Interaction Suppression in Dual-Band Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces holistic approaches to address the challenges faced by a typical dual-band side-by-side antenna array arrangement, where antennas with close spacing suffer from significant interactions leading to degradation in radiation patterns and port-to-port isolations. The proposed methods utilize three multifunctional loading structures, including a 2.5-dimensional (2.5-D) cloak, defected ground structure (DGS), and resonance shifter (RS), to simultaneously suppress both cross-band scattering and coupling. These structures effectively mitigate the cross-band interactions between the low-band (LB) and high-band (HB) antennas. Moreover, the 2.5-D cloak and RS also contribute to in-band coupling suppression and improved isolation between adjacent HB antennas. In addition, all these structures can be designed on the same substrate as the original antennas, eliminating the need for additional layers. This feature not only ensures cost-effectiveness but also facilitates the implementation process, making it easy to integrate the proposed techniques into existing antenna systems.

articleTitle: Double Layer Metasurface for Gain Enhancement of 5G Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a double layer metasurface antenna design is proposed for 5G technology to facilitate human activities. This antenna is made with double layers metasurface to produce high gain. This antenna operates at a frequency of 3.5 GHz with a bandwidth of 200 MHz, return loss -14.759 dB, gain reaches 6.22 dBi. The results show that the antenna has a wide bandwidth with a high gain. Thus, The proposed antenna has a suitable specifications for 5G technology.

articleTitle: Characterization of 5G-based Reconfigurable Wearable Antenna for Healthcare Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 5G-based reconfigurable wearable antenna that will be used in a wearable health monitoring system. The substrate material is Roger3003 and stubs are used to match the impedance between source and load. To enhance antenna performance, the defected ground structure technique is used along with PIN diodes to achieve desired frequency reconfigurable properties. Simulation and measurement results indicate that the S11 value is < -10 dB for the 5G n38 and n78 bands, while the SAR value is below the threshold.

articleTitle: Reflection Coefficient Measurement in a Real Room for 300 GHz Indoor Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports the results of evaluating the reflection coefficients of walls, windows and fixtures in an actual indoor environments by measurement in order to investigate the reflection paths that can be used for MIMO communications in the 300 GHz band indoor wireless communications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Microstrip Passive Mixer for Radar Applications at 9.3 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes designing and developing a microstrip passive up-conversion mixer that operates at the requisite 9.3 GHz (X-Band) frequency for radar applications. The mixer is made of Rogers Duroid 5880 with dielectric constant (εr) = 2.2, dielectric layer thickness (h) = 1.575 mm, and loss tangent (δ) = 0.0001. Advanced Design System (ADS) is used for design and simulation. The proposed mixer has a bandwidth of 200 MHz and performs well at 9.3 GHz. The measurement yields marginally different results than the simulation. Probably due to imprecise procedure prototype development and measurement.

articleTitle: Changes in Mediumwave Broadcasting Antennas and Matching Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Mediumwave broadcasting in Japan began in 1925. Celebrating 100 years. For about 40years, I have been engaged in research and development of broadcast transmission technology, matching research on medium-wave antennas, and operation management of transmission equipment. In this report, I explain the vector matching method of the antenna developed by the author. In addition, we will introduce some aspects of lightning counter measures.

articleTitle: High Isolation of mm-Wave T-R Switch Design Using Open Loop Square Ring DGS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research studies the use of a switchable open loop square ring defected ground structure (DGS) to provide high isolation in a discrete transmit-receive (T-R) millimeter-wave (mm-wave) RF switch operating in the 26 GHz band for a 5G application. The simulation demonstrated that the switchable DGS had aided the T-R switch in generating a large isolation performance of more than 30 dB in the 26 GHz band.

articleTitle: Development of a Wirelessly Powered Aortic Stent with Smart Sensors for Endoleak Treatment and Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents a wireless-powered smart sensors-integrated aortic stent designed to address endoleak treatment and enable data transmission capability. The novel stent antenna system offers promising advancements for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). The stent antenna incorporates meshed rings formed by multiple helical wires connected to a single feed wire, allowing for controlled distribution of currents. This design enhances the antenna’s performance, providing features such as omnidirectional radiation, high gain, and optimal impedance matching. Simulation and measurement results validate the effectiveness of the stent antenna across awide frequency range, including the ISM 868 and 915 MHz bands, spanning from 850 to 950 MHz. By integrating wireless-powered smart sensors, the developed aortic stent not only addresses endoleak treatment but also enables data transmission capability, opening new possibilities for continuous monitoring of patients.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Buffer Material’s Electrical Conductivity for the Underwater Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the finding of the effect of different conductivity of surrounding the proposed underwater antenna. The proposed antenna consists of helical antenna and a buffer medium. The axial-mode helical antenna acts as a base antenna, designed at 433 MHz operating frequency while the function of the buffer is to provide a matching layer between the antenna structure and the surrounding environment. The antenna performance is analyzed in terms of return loss, gain, radiation pattern and the surface current. Specifically, it is shown that the conductivity of buffer acts as a main contribution in designing an underwater antenna. The antenna is designed and analyzed using CST software.

articleTitle: Electrically Tunable Microstrip U-Slot Antenna Using Ferroelectric BST Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A tunable U-slot microstrip patch antenna has two different antenna substrates operating around 5.4GHz. This design employs the BST material manganese-doped Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> soft ferroelectric thin films with relative dielectric permittivity of >150 and loss tangent of <0.02 to provide a practical frequency tuning. It is found that incorporating BST in the same plane within a U-slot gap in a microstrip patch can provide frequency tuning of 70MHz at 5.65GHz with an appropriate electric field of 19kV/cm.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependency Characteristic of a 4x4 Butler Matrix for 5G sub-6 GHz application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Butler matrix (BM) is a widely used beamforming technique in array signal processing that enables efficient and precise signal distribution to multiple antenna elements. However, the frequency-dependent nature of their design restricts the effectiveness of the conventional Butler matrix to a specific frequency band only, thus leading to the narrow band operation. This paper presents the analysis of the frequency-dependency behaviour through a 4-by-4 BM based on its first-stage operation. Through this analysis, a mathematical correlation was developed between the BM parameters, specifically the electrical length and phase components, by utilizing the phase–to–frequency gradient. This correlation serves as a foundation for subsequent design stages. The 4x4 BM is developed for a sub-6 GHz 5G operation at 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a Circularly Polarized Spiral Antenna using a Circular EBG Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the bandwidth enhancement of a circularly polarized (CP) spiral antenna using a circular electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) reflector for satellite communications and other wireless applications. The spiral antenna is placed at the front, and at the bottom is a circular EBG reflector with high-impedance surface properties. For comparison, circular EBG reflector was studied in comparison with circular PEC reflector. The antenna height from the bottom of the circular EBG reflector to the spiral antenna is small: 0.1 wavelengths at the lowest design frequency of 1.3 GHz. The circular EBG reflector contributes to a constant input impedance and small axial ratio (AR) throughout the design frequency range of 1.5–9.0 GHz (143%). The results of the analysis were verified by the measured results of the prototype antenna.

articleTitle: Compact Full Flexible Vivaldi Antenna for 3.5 GHz Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact wearable Vivaldi antenna resonating at 3.5 GHz is proposed for 5G n77, and n78 bands. It is designed upon a flexible polyester substrate having dielectric constant (ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of 1.34 and loss tangent (tan δ) of 0.005. The antenna parameters were optimized via parametric analyses using CST software with a size of 45 × 45 × 0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (length × width × height). The antenna is evaluated in terms of reflection coefficient, gain, efficiency, radiation pattern, and surface current density. This antenna attained a maximum simulated gain of 4.7 dBi, and an efficiency of 98 % in the resonating band.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Microstrip Antenna Loading Parasitic Element and Horn-Shaped Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study proposes a high-gain microstrip antenna loading a parasitic element and horn-shaped reflector. The parasitic element is placed above the microstrip antenna, and the reflector is loaded around it. The effects of the parasitic element and reflector are numerically investigated. The gain of a prototype antenna is around 12 dBi, and 6-dB gain improvement is experimentally confirmed. A high-gain microstrip antenna is successfully achieved by loading a parasitic element and reflector.

articleTitle: Node Positioning Error Optimization for Collaborative Beamforming in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Collaborative Beamforming (CB) technique is an effective technique to increase communication reliability and efficiency between sensor nodes and base station (BS) in Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). However, CB suffers from high sidelobe level (SLL) due to the random deployment of sensor nodes in WSN. Thus, this paper proposes an optimization of node positioning for linear array construction using proposed Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (ICA). The performance of ICA in optimizing 12 linear array is simulated in terms of peak sidelobe level (PSL) reduction, control the size of main lobe and power gain mitigation in unintended directions by placing null. The results show that ICA gives superior results in terms of PSL reduction (up to 31%) and placing deep nulls more than -60dB.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Ethanol-Aqueous Solution with Modified Jerusalem Resonator for Disinfectants Against COVID-19 Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a liquid-mixture sensor based on a mushroom-shaped zeroth-order resonator (ZOR). The Jerusalem-shaped mushroom-like structure is designed to reduce the dimensions of a resonator and provide a high Q-factor with an operating frequency of 5.90 GHz. Using perturbation theory, every dielectric property of the liquid-mixture influences the resonance frequency. The structure of the sensor is composed of the modified Jerusalem resonator and 3D-printed case for locking the liquid under test (LUT) to reduce the problematic error from position measurement. Five Ethanol-aqueous concentrations, e.g., 60%, 65%, 70%, 75% and 80%, are chosen to investigate the responsibility of the modified Jerusalem resonator. By detecting the change in resonant frequency of the reflection coefficient, S11, the measured results can classify five conditions of the LUT. Other benefits of the zeroth-order resonator sensor include a nondestructive method, real-time monitoring, and no life-cycle limitation.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Detection Reflectometry Technique Using Millimeter-wave Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work introduces a methodology for the early detection of skin cancer. The approach utilizes a dual-band antipodal vivaldi antenna (AVA) with circular polarization and a low-profile design for reflectometry in the millimeter-wave frequency range. The AVA distinguishes between normal skin tissue and malignant tumors by analyzing the change in return loss (RL). Planar and cylindrical tissue models have been developed to simulate skin conditions, including wet and dry skin. The tissue models incorporate irregular hexagon, pentagon, and rectangle as shapes associated with skin cancer. The analysis involves the examination of frequency shift and RL magnitude in the presence and absence of a tumor. The results indicate that the cylindrical skin model displayed a notable frequency shift and higher RL than the planar model. The RL value is significantly impacted by alterations in the tumor’s morphology.

articleTitle: Focused Metasurface Based on Time Reversal in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a time-reversal-based transmission metasurface capable of focusing in complex multipath environments. The proposed metasurface consists of amplitude and phase independently controlled units. By integrating the time-reversal algorithm with the metasurface, this study achieves electromagnetic focusing at single-point and multi-point locations in both free space and complex multipath environments. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of electromagnetic focusing in complex environments.

articleTitle: Wideband Omnidirectional Antenna Based on Dielectric Resonant and Slot Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel exciting method of TM01δ mode of cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented. Based on the internal field distribution of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> mode, the circular magnetic current can be utilized to feed this mode. The structure of circular magnetic current is realized by slots etched on the ground, which is excited by the two-order power divider. In addition, the direct radiation of slot can be designed at another frequency to obtain wideband omnidirectional radiation. To verify the presented exciting method and wideband design, the cylindrical DRA excited by four fan-shaped slots is simulated. The impedance and gain bandwidth can cover 1.95–2.87 GHz (39%). Moreover, the radiation pattern and efficiency are both stable within the operating band.

articleTitle: Stripline and Microstrip Beamforming Networks for Twin-Beam Base-Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Stripline and microstrip beamforming networks are investigated for dual-slant twin-beam base station antenna applications. The beamforming network combining stripline hybrid coupler with directional couplers provides a return loss better than 20 dB for all ports and stable output amplitude across the 3.3−4.2 GHz band. Additionally, the stripline network has an average 0.26 dB insertion loss and 45% reduction in size compared to microstrip network.

articleTitle: Design of a 1-Bit Programmable Coding Unit Cell Beamforming Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Traditional phased array antennas rely on costly phase shifters to steer beams by manipulating the phase of induced currents in each antenna element. In this study, we introduce a 1-bit coding metasurface as an alternative to traditional phased array antennas for beam control and modulation of electromagnetic waves. The metasurface operates at 5.8 GHz and consists of digitally controlled unit cells, each incorporating a pin diode. These diodes enable binary coding states of "1" and "0" with a significant 180-degree phase difference. The unit cell, with a dimension of 0.81λ x 0.81λ, comprises two metal patches separated by the pin diode on an FR-4 substrate. Simulation results demonstrate the distinct behavior of the metasurface, with the off-state exhibiting a reflection amplitude response of 1.8dB and the on-state showing a reduced amplitude due to on-resistance. The far-field patterns obtained from the simulations clearly indicate a 90-degree change in the radiation pattern between bit "0" and bit "1." This innovative design offers a cost-effective solution for beam control and versatile electromagnetic wave modulation, making it suitable for various applications, including beamforming in radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: Estimation of Element Positions in Deformed Uniform Linear Arrays using Received Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Position estimation of the antenna elements of a deformed array using received signals is presented. The model considers a uniform linear array (ULA) with a change in the positions of the elements due to deformation of the array. Multiple sources with known direction of arrival (DOA) are used to estimate the position of each antenna element within a certain range. The proposed estimation technique is demonstrated for a deformed array with eight elements under the noiseless and noisy condition.

articleTitle: NLOS Effect on LEO Doppler Positioning: A case Study in Hong Kong
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper studies a simulation case of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) effect on low Earth orbit (LEO) Doppler positioning. LEO Doppler measurement error caused by NLOS signal is analyzed. LEO constellations are simulated with 3D mapping aided ray tracing considering the propagation of NLOS signals. Simulation results show that even for stationary users, NLOS effect can cause around 10 m horizontal error during 100 seconds in average.

articleTitle: Shared-Aperture Phased Array Antenna Based on Dual-Band Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel S-/C-band shared-aperture phased array antenna is proposed in this paper. Different from the conventional dual-band shared-aperture phased array antennas utilizing two types of antenna elements, the proposed shared-aperture phased array antenna achieves the dual-band independent operation by employing the dual-band feeding network composed of duplexers and power dividers. The calculated results show that the proposed antenna can scan up to ±60° with the active VSWRs below 2.2 within 3.3−3.8 GHz (14.1% at S-band) and 5.3−6 GHz (12.4% at C-band).

articleTitle: Design of multi-beam phased array antennas for coastal disaster preventing radar system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The proposed antenna was designed with a multilayer feeding structure that combines microstrip line and slot elements in order to control the phase characteristics of the antenna. The simulated reflection coefficients of the antenna fed by port #1 and port #2 obtained approximately -28 dB and below -35 dB at the center frequency, respectively. The isolation between two ports obtained excellent characteristics of -20 dB. The phase control method was utilized by the control of the lengths of the transmission lines connected to the ports. The phases of 4 patches fed at port #1 were appeared in the same ones. In case of port #2 feeding phase of two patches was shown in the same one while phase of the other two patches was obtained in the out-of phase.

articleTitle: A New Class of Method With TE/TM Wave Decomposition and Superposition Enabling High-Efficiency Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The first-of-its-kind TE/TM wave decomposition and superposition methods for a rotational arrangement to the polarization of the unit cell are proposed and demonstrated computationally and experimentally, which can significantly enhance the aperture efficiency of the low-profile transmitarray (TA) antenna. Phase variation on the TA aperture stemming from the unit cell arrangement method was calculated by extracting the coupling coefficient between unit cells through the reflection coefficient Floquet response using TE/TM wave decomposition and superposition methods to validate the utility of the proposed unit cell arrangement. The proposed TA antenna exhibits a low focal length to diameter (F/D) ratio of 0.33 and an aperture efficiency of 40.5% at a center frequency of 3.5 GHz with an aperture size of 5.1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> × 5.1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>.

articleTitle: A New Form of Polarization Diversity Using A Pair of Spatially-Variable-Orthogonal-Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel form of polarization diversity using a pair of spatially-variable-orthogonal-polarizations (SVOPs) obtained by mixing two orthogonal linear polarizations (LPs) of a dual-polarized cross-dipole array. This method significantly enhances the beamwidth of the array without requiring changes to its configuration or amplitude tuning, resulting in reduced operational costs compared to other pattern synthesis methods. To achieve the required polarization diversity, two SVOP arrays are designed with the same pattern shapes such that their polarizations are orthogonal to each other in all directions of interest. We theoretically derive and validate the conditions for achieving orthogonal patterns using this method. It is demonstrated that the obtained pair of SVOP arrays have better polarization orthogonality (PO) and wider beam than that of the dual-polarized antenna element employed in the array.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Pattern for Arm-Worn Smartwatch GPS Antenna Based on Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A practical method for enhancing the GPS antenna performance of arm-worn smartwatch is proposed based on N-port characteristic modes (CM). With several reactive loads implemented at the clearance, radiation patterns can be synthesized with high gain to satellites, and the antenna efficiency is guaranteed by excluding higher-order modes at the same time. The proposed method provides a promising solution for commercial wearables antennas.

articleTitle: The Performance of a Frequency Reconfigurable Wearable Antenna for 5G Health Monitoring Application Under Bending Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the performance analysis of a frequency reconfigurable wearable antenna under various bending configurations. The antenna is based on a transdermal cotton patch substrate. PIN diodes are used to switch to three different frequencies of 1.8GHz, 2.3GHz, and 3.5GHz which are the 5G frequency bands in Malaysia and Indonesia. Various bending configurations are tested for each of the operating frequencies. Results have shown that the antenna can maintain a desirable performance under extreme bending conditions hence suitable for 5G health monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Perturbed Higher Order Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Low Cross-pol for Millimeter Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A singly fed high gain, wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is designed here which can be used for millimeter wave 5G applications. The simulated gain of the aperture fed DRA is 8.33 dBi and the simulated impedance bandwidth is 3 GHz which is from 26.56 GHz to 29.56 GHz. The percentage impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 11.53 percent. A H shaped slot has been done on the ground plane over which the DRA is placed and is fed by a microstrip line below the substrate. A vertical cylindrical hole has been made in the DRA which excites it to higher order mode TE21z. The cylindrical hole has also enhanced the gain of the DRA to 8 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Polarized Single-Layer Wideband Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by Two L-probes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of a single-layer dual-polarized and wideband ring microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by two L-probes. The proposed antenna is composed of a square ring patch and two feeding L-shaped probes (L-probes) arranged on a single-layer dielectric substrate. In order to obtain wideband operation, a thick dielectric substrate with a thickness of approximately 0.13 wavelengths at the center frequency is used. The two L-probes are placed at orthogonally positions each other and excite two orthogonal modes of the ring patch. Thus, linearly dual-polarized and wideband characteristics are realized by the single-layer configuration of the proposed MSA. The design frequency of the proposed antenna is around 13 GHz. In this paper, the structural parameters of the proposed MSA are tuned by using ANSYS HFSS so that dual-polarized and wideband performance is achieved. The simulated results reveal that fractional bandwidth of below –10 dB reflection is approximately 44% and that the port-to-port isolation between the two feeding ports is more than 10.6 dB in the above bandwidth. Stable unidirectional radiation patterns are also obtained over the bandwidth by the simulation.

articleTitle: A scalable model for on-chip spiral inductors by Space-mapping neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a scalable model for on-chip spiral inductors utilizing the space-mapping neural network (SMNN), built upon an enhanced 1-π equivalent circuit model. To address the inductor drop observed at low frequencies, a series network consisting of two pairs of inductors and resistors is integrated into the 1-π equivalent circuit model. The topology of the SMNN is optimized using the global search capability of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, which determines the optimal weights and thresholds for the SMNN. Compared with traditional neural network models, the proposed SMNN reduces the number of neurons required for mapping the input-output nonlinear relationship, leading to enhanced accuracy and reduced modeling time, which takes a mere 10 to 15 seconds.

articleTitle: VO-2 Assisted Unit Cell for Designing THz Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A hybrid half-wavelength model of gold and Vanadium Oxide (VO-2) is presented in this paper operating at 1.1 THz. With the temperature variation, VO-2 changes its state from insulator to metallic which causes the phase response of the unit cell to change. The phase shift of 198° is obtained based on the switching mechanism of VO-2. This provides a hint at the capacity of VO-2 being used as the switching mechanism at the terahertz band for designing the reconfigurable reflectarray antenna.

articleTitle: A Single-Feed Array Antenna With Sum- and Difference-Patterns Using Planar Magic-Ts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a single-feed microstrip array antenna for dual beam switching functionality. The proposed antenna consists of four linearly polarized microstrip antennas, two planar magic-Ts, and one single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch. The magic-Ts distribute in- or anti-phase signals to the antenna arrays to generate sum or difference radiation patterns on the y-z plane. The switching between the radiation patterns is achieved by using the SPDT switch. The concept is experimentally verified using a 5.8-GHz prototype. The measured 10-dB impedance bandwidth is around 2.8% with better than 10.9-dBi gain at 5.75 GHz. The cross-polarization suppression is better than 20 dB for both radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Inter-mode Interference Suppression Method for OAM Multiplexing in the Presence of Ground Reflection and Beam Axis Misalignment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Inter-mode interference (IMI) in orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing exhibits different mode ranges and dependences according to factors such as beam axis misalignment and ground reflection, which require countermeasures that consider their properties. In this study, we propose an IMI suppression method to improve the transmission performance of OAM multiplexing using mode limitation and an efficient IMI canceler at the transmitter and receiver, respectively, when both beam axis misalignment and ground reflection are present. Considering that the IMI caused by ground reflection becomes more severe at higher OAM modes, the proposed method focuses on transmitting the OAM during lower modes (which are less affected by such IMI). Later, the residual IMI is eliminated using an efficient IMI canceler at the receiver. The proposed method has demonstrated its superiority over the traditional one (which solely uses an efficient IMI canceler) via computer simulations.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO Antenna Scalability of A Simple Rectangular Truncated Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Massive MIMO Antennas were developed to meet the demand for 5G's high speed. Their large size poses design challenges due to software limitations. Designing Massive MIMO Antennas with multiple elements becomes complex due to modeling constraints. To forecast the specification outcomes produced by a Massive MIMO Antenna array with a certain configuration based on a Simple MIMO Antenna array with a 2x2, 4x4, 8x8, 16x16 MIMO element configuration scheme, etc. exponential increments, a scalability technique is applied. In order to forecast the specifications of a Massive MIMO Antenna array, this research will focus on the scaling process. The designed MIMO antenna arrangement is based on the design of a rectangular antenna with a truncated corner for further design with various types of configurations that operate at a frequency of 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Leaky-wave Wires Antenna for Future D- Band 6G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Future communication generation such as 6G and beyond will be utilizing the terahertz band, as this range promises potential benefits such as a high data rate. However, designing different electronic components for 6G is complicated and has low fabrication precision due to its small wavelength. Additionally, the cost is also very high as compared to 5G components. These antennas feature high data rates, small size, and high bandwidth and are a critical component for the communication system. Therefore, in this study, an antenna design is proposed for the future sub-THz communication system that operates at D- band which is proposed for the 6G communication system. The simulation analysis shows that the proposed antenna has a high gain of 9.9 dBi at 120 GHz operating frequency and good performance characteristics for the complete D-band. The design of the proposed antenna is simple, low-cost, and does not require any complex fabrication, and can be the potential leaky-wave antenna for future 6G if properly excited.

articleTitle: Using FWCW Radar Sensor to Distinguish Audio Arabic Numerals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar, as a non-contact high-precision detection technology, can realize very fine object detection and tracking in complex environments within a specific frequency range. It is of great significance to apply it to sound detection. In this paper, the application of millimeter-wave radar in sound detection will be discussed in depth from the following aspects: First, this paper reviews various current sound detection technologies and solutions, and then summarizes the characteristics, advantages, and limitations of millimeter-wave radar sound detection. Secondly, the challenges and problems faced by the application of millimeter-wave radar technology in sound detection are explored, and specific solutions are proposed. Finally, the experimental results are evaluated and summarized The experimental results are summarized, and the research results and suggestions for future development are given.

articleTitle: Array Factor, Retrodirective, and E-MIMO Beamforming Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: E-MIMO is a method developed by our laboratory to calculate the maximum efficiency of MIMO systems [1], and it has already been reported that the optimal excitation voltage of the transmission elements obtained from the method applies to beamforming [2][3]. In this paper, for a three-element dipole antenna array, we compare the excitation voltages and radiation patterns obtained by the array factor(AF) method, the retrodirective control method, and E-MIMO method, respectively, and clarify the differences between them. All analysis uses the electromagnetic field analysis software Feko.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Millimeter Wave MIMO Antenna Design and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the development of a compact ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for millimeter wave MIMO application. The main advantage of the proposed antenna lies in its utilization of a straightforward design consisting of an oval shape with rectangular slots, which leads to a bandwidth of 13 GHz spanning from 24.5 GHz to 37.5 GHz with peak gain of 6.57 dBi. The antenna is developed on Rogers RT5880 substrate with partial ground, and the total size of 30 × 35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. To test the performance of the antenna, a six-port UWB MIMO antenna system is applied. This system incorporates six antennas positioned orthogonally to ensure high isolation throughout the entire operating frequency range. From the results, the system shows mutual coupling between the ports at lower than −13.5 dB. The performance of the antenna is discussed in terms of its envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), diversity gain (DG), and its total active reflection coefficient (TARC), where all the simulated result shows values within the appropriate range of MIMO antennas.

articleTitle: Novel Partially-Reflective-Surface (PRS) Design Using Compact Microstrip Resonant Cells (CMRCs) for Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a new design of a partially reflective surface (PRS) made of compact microstrip resonant cells (CMRC) is investigated to improve the antenna gain. The gain of the antenna integrated by PRS is strongly affected by the reflection properties of the PRS. A positive phase gradient of the reflection coefficient is required to increase the gain over a wide frequency range. In this work, double layers of CMRC unit cells are used to achieve the positive phase gradient in the frequency band of interest. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed PRS design.

articleTitle: Compact Beamforming Antennas for Directional Modulation in IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper discuss a PHY-layer security technique known as Directional Modulation (DM) and its implementations with compact beamforming antennas. The motivation is to allow DM to operate from small and low-complexity IoT devices. While classical DM required large antenna arrays and complex hardware, recent work proposed an alternative algorithm that requires single RF chain. The technique was demonstrated with circular arrays of diameter of 0.6 wavelength, with only one antenna transmitting at each given time. This work revisits the concept and demonstrate its feasibility with multimodal compact beamforming antennas. Unlike circular arrays, for multimodal antennas the directional performance is directly dependent on the number of modes involved and not antenna size – albeit inclusion of higher order modes within limited volume will inevitably lead to the decrease in operational bandwidth and efficiency.

articleTitle: The Design Evolution of Trio-Band Vivaldi Antenna With Meander-Line-Fed Shape for Ground Penetrating Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is proposed based on considerable reviewed design techniques. It works at 200MHz, 800MHz and 1,200MHz named as "Trio-Band" with the fixed size of 300mm×300mm×1.6mm of the FR4 substrate. The antenna application is for Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) with targeted depth range is from 10cm to 1,000cm. The combination of slotted shapes which is Half-circle, Staircase, Quarter-eclipse and Circular-Ring are applied to achieve the Trio-Band with the parametric analysis to determine the appropriate size. The final Vivaldi antenna achieves the reflective coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) with -30.05dB (200MHz), -12.05dB (800MHz) and -15.35dB (1,200MHz) as well as 50Ω of impedance matching.

articleTitle: Stochastic Geometric Energy Coverage Analysis in Millimeter Wave Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical model of energy harvesting (EH) performance for user equipment (UE) in mm-wave cellular networks, addressing the challenges of limited battery life and high energy consumption. The effects of base stations (BSs) density, BS antenna elements and the channel path-loss on the energy coverage probability (ECP) of the UE are investigated. Results obtained from the analytical model perfectly match the Monte Carlo simulations and show significant enhancements in ECP when BSs density and antenna elements increase. Moreover, this analytical model offers researchers valuable insights into the network’s performance regarding EH capabilities. This facilitates informed decisions for network planning and development.

articleTitle: New active and reconfigurable butler matrix for 5G application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a new system for steering antenna beams using a 4x4 Butler matrix and Varactor diodes. The Butler matrix allows for four beams to be generated, each pointing in a specific direction depending on which input port is excited. The Varactor diodes are used to adjust the phase shift of the signals going through the matrix, which allows the beams to be steered to different angles. The fabricated prototype of the system and tested it at a frequency of 3.5 GHz. The system performed well, with a reflection and isolation coefficient better than -15 dB over the entire desired frequency band, and an amplitude imbalance lower than ±1.5 db. They were able to steer the radiating beam to different angles depending on the bias applied to the Varactor diodes, with the beam being oriented from ±6° to ±18° when port 1 or 4 are excited and from ±32° to ±43° for ports 2 and 3. Overall, this system could be useful in applications where it’s important to be able to steer antenna beams to different angles, such as in radar or communication systems.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Characterization of a High-Gain Antenna at 300-GHz Band Based on a Cylindrical Electrooptic Near-Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We developed a measurement system to improve the long-term stability of electrooptic phase measurements and measured a cylindrical near-field of a high-gain antenna using this system. The far-field distribution calculated from the measured cylindrical near-field distribution agreed well with the far-field obtained by direct measurements. This measurement system will be useful for characterizing antennas used in Beyond 5G/6G.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement for Wearable 5G Antenna on PVA thin film substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a 5G wearable antenna design using Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) thin film. The antenna is designed on PVA thin film as substrate with the dielectric and tangent loss of 1.853 and 0.04 respectively. Since the material has high tangent loss, the gain of the antenna will be very low. Hence, impedance matching on the transmission line has been chosen to increase the antenna gain. By this technique the gain has been improved from 1.57 dBi to 2.20 dBi around 40.13% improvement. The S11 also improved from -17.05 dB -41.25 dB with the impedance matching of 55.5 Ω to 50 Ω respectively.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Design Metasurface for Arbitrary Beam Generation and Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The development of machine learning has brought great changes to the information age. In this paper, a kind of beam generations and beam regulations using machine learning design metasurface is proposed. Experiments show that this method can arbitrarily generate and regulate beams according to the purpose, and has high efficiency, high universality, and greatly simplifies the design of beam generators.

articleTitle: C/X-Band Shared-Aperture Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel dual-band shared-aperture phased array antenna is proposed in this paper. Patch antennas are employed operating in the X band, and above them a dipole antenna operating in the C band is employed. The dipole is elaborately designed to a disconnected form, reducing the coupling from the X-band antennas. The patches are also reflecting ground of the C-band antennas in addition to the X-band radiators. The calculated results show that the C-band antenna can scan up to ±45° with the active VSWRs below 3 within 4.68−5.26 GHz (11.7% in the C band) and the X-band antenna can scan up to ±60° with the active VSWRs below 3 within 8.7−10.1 GHz (14.9% in the X band). It is a good alternative for satellite communications.

articleTitle: A 60-GHz On-chip Slot Antenna on Integrated Passive Device (IPD) Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip slot antenna fabricated on the integrated passive device (IPD) process and operated at the 60-GHz band. The carrier substrate is Gallium Arsenic (GaAs). The proposed antenna consists of a CPWG-to-SIW (Grounded CPW-to-substrate integrated waveguide) transition, a section of SIW, and a quarter-wavelength slot radiator slightly offset from the centerline of the SIW. Bond wires are attached to the GSG pads for measuring purpose. Fair agreement between the simulation and measurement is achieved. A 3-GHz frequency shift is observed in the reflection coefficient. The measured peak gain is located at θ = -30 degree with a value of 1.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Binary-Coded Genetic Algorithm Optimization for UHF RFID Tag Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a fragmented Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag antenna design. A fragmented design is portrayed to enhance the conjugate matching between chip impedance and antenna impedance utilizing the Binary Genetic Algorithm (BGA) method. The substrate used is Rogers 5880 with a thickness of 1.57mm and a relative permittivity of 2.2. The chip used is NXP Ucode 8 with a chip impedance of 13-j191 Ω. The framework is implemented in MATLAB and verified by CST simulation software. In the proposed design, the resonant frequency is at 909MHz without a chip footprint, whereas with the inclusion of a chip footprint, the resonant frequency shifts to 917MHz. Profound results are obtained utilizing the BGA method with the chip footprint where the reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) is -21.11dB, maximum power transfer of 0.99, and antenna impedance of 11.08+j191.91 Ω.

articleTitle: Study on Measurement Technique of Complex Permittivity Using Free-Space Method at Millimeterwave Frequencies in Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The free-space method is suitable for wide-band measurement in mobile communication systems. In this paper, we propose extending the free-space method based on transmitted characteristics with a horn antenna by 1) setting the material at far-field distances and the Fresnel zone, and 2) by applying a gating function to the S21 characteristics except in the range of ±0.005 ns from the first peak.

articleTitle: Investigation of Self-Resonant Equation in Meander Line Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The meander line antennas (MLAs) are used for small-sized antennas in the self-resonant condition where capacitive reactance (X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>) and inductive (X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>) reactance are equal. In the previous study, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> and X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> are not explicitly shown in the structural equation of self-resonance. In this paper, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>, and X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> are derived from the self-inductance of the crank part and the stored charge at the edge area of the MLA. By equalizing X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> and X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>, the self-resonant equation is obtained. The self-resonant structures by the equation and results of electromagnetic simulations agree very well. The usefulness of the equation is ensured.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Isolation Positive-and-Negative-45-Degree Dual-Polarization 5G mmWave Micro Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a slot-coupled dual-polarization micro base station antenna based on a vertical feed structure is proposed. The structural design of the double-layer patch allows the antenna to have two resonance points. When the resonance points are close to each other, the bandwidth of the antenna is increased. Four circular metal through-holes (or via holes) are used to improve the impedance matching of the antenna, resulting in an operating bandwidth of 24.14-29.08 GHz with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of less than 1.5. The antenna also has a high isolation of less than -30 dB. In addition, the cross-polarization performance of the antenna exceeds 15 dB, which meets the standards of base station antennas. At the same time, the antenna has a low profile feature, with a thickness of 1.3 mm (about 0.11λ at 26 GHz) and a compact size of 6 mm × 6 mm ( about 0.52λ × 0.52λ at 26 GHz ). This antenna has the potential for large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) applications.

articleTitle: Construction of Simplified Smartphone Model for Specific Absorption Rate Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, the smartphone structure has become more complicated owing to functionality improvements and miniaturization. To evaluate human exposure to electromagnetic waves, we have modeled and simulated smartphones in detail. In an era where various smartphones are being developed, simplification of smartphone models is necessary to evaluate them quickly. It takes time to model the antenna of smartphone terminals. Therefore, we propose a method for constructing a simple smartphone model that generates the same distribution as that of a real terminal using the specific absorption rate, which is an index for evaluating electromagnetic wave exposure, and confirm its validity.

articleTitle: Radar Target Recognition Method Based on Variable-Length E-Pulse
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Target features such as polarization and distance image are often related to many factors, and their values vary with the external circumstances, which greatly increases the complexity and data amount of target recognition. In this paper, a target recognition method based on poles is proposed. Poles are only related to the nature of the target itself, and have nothing to do with factors such as orientation and polarization. However, the real-time extraction of poles is often affected by noise. By extracting poles in an ideal environment, the effect of noise can be reduced and led to a better E-pulse waveform, which greatly reduces the amount of data and complexity required for target recognition. Simulation carried out in Section- III verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Study of 1D Arrayed MACKEY with a Modified Power Supply Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The metasurface-inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), a compact, thin antenna that can operate on metal, has been further thinned to a single-point power supply, the unbalanced MACKEY II. This paper presents the analytical results of a 1D arrayed model of an unbalanced MACKEY II with a modified feeding method.

articleTitle: A 2 × 2 Ka-Band Wideband Circularly Polarized Sub-Array Antenna Based on U-shaped Slots and Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel 2 × 2 U-shaped sub-array antenna with circular polarization, specifically designed for Ka-band satellite communication terminals. The sub-array is composed of a gap waveguide feed layer, a cavity layer and a radiating layer. U-shaped radiating slots are placed on the top plate. In the second layer, a coupling slot and circular polarization-generating ridges are placed in a gap waveguide cavity and the cavity layer is fed by a ridge gap waveguide feeding. The simulation of the proposed array antenna exhibits good performance, including a low axial ratio (below 3 dB) over a bandwidth of 28-34.6 GHz, high gain (12.3 dBi at the center frequency of 31.5 GHz) in the broadside direction, low relative sidelobe level (SLL), and also low-profile and planar design. All these characteristics make the proposed antenna a very promising solution for next-generation satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: An Improved Jonscher Model for Broadband Dielectric Characterization of Cement Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Here we propose an improved Jonscher model for the characterization of complex permittivity of the ultra-lightweight cement composite (ULCC). The conventional Jonscher model has inherent disadvantages in its upper frequency limit, particularly, the minimum loss factor cannot be located from its imaginary-part $\left( {\varepsilon _{\text{r}}^{''}} \right)$ model. The proposed model has fixed this problem and can handle a broadband frequency range from 100 MHz to 20 GHz for different cement-based composites. Cross validations are given for both the models using published data and new ULCC data to certify the effectiveness of the new model.

articleTitle: System Configuration of Sub-terahertz MassiveMIMO Channel Sounder for 6G
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 6G will require extremely high-speed communication data rates exceeding 100 Gbps using sub-terahertz (THz) bands. Sub-THz bands have extremely short wavelengths and are affected by objects and people surrounding mobile stations. This can result in sparser sub-THz channel properties due to weak diffraction and time non-stationarity. Therefore, we have developed a sub-THz Massive MIMO channel sounder that implements a beamforming technique using 896 antenna elements to measure channel properties in sub-THz bands. This channel sounder offers a high resolution of the time-spatial channel and can analyze the number of arriving paths with lower power in real time. In this paper, we clarify the system configuration and present the verification results of its performance in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Wideband Dielectric Patch Antenna Using Higher-Order Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dielectric patch antenna (DPA) based on air regions is designed for the enhancement of the impedance bandwidth. In virtue of the difference between E-field distribution of the fundamental TM101 mode and that of the higher-order TM121 mode, a pair of air regions are introduced into the DPA along the y-axis direction, where the radiation region of the TM101 mode is stronger than that of the TM121 mode. As a result, the resonant frequency of the TM101 mode is moved in proximity to that of the TM121 mode, resulting in a wide impedance bandwidth. For demonstration, a DPA with air regions is designed and simulated. The results show that the impedance bandwidth of the DPA is broadened to 26.9% with stable radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Design of a Superdirective Small and Wideband Yagi-like Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents the design of a three-element compact Yagi-like antenna using superdirectivity principle. The length of this Yagi-like antenna is 60 % shorter than that of a classical one, while keeping the same performances of directivity and impedance bandwidth. To validate the design, a prototype is manufactured and measured. The measurements results show that the antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 22.6% and a peak directivity of and 8.1 dBi. Also, the antenna presents a directivity bandwidth of 10.86 % and a total efficiency > 80%.

articleTitle: Suppression of the Slot-Mode in a Slitted Waveguide using Dielectric-Filling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to suppress the slot-mode in uniform rectangular waveguide based leaky-wave antennas (LWAs). In the method, the use of a dielectric-filled waveguide is shown to completely suppress the propagation of the slot-mode thereby eliminating the influence of this mode in the radiated electric field from the LWA. The characteristics of the slot mode and fundamental leaky mode are first studied using the transverse equivalent network of the LWA structure using both air-filled and dielectric-filled waveguide models and the suppression effect is confirmed by full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Wideband Dual-Slant Aperture-Coupled Metasurface Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Aperture-coupled microstrip patch antennas are studied for dual-slant base-station applications with conventional and metasurface patches. The proposed metasurface patch antenna can achieve a 14 dB impedance bandwidth of 30.3% in frequency range of 3.14–4.26 GHz. For 5G applications in the frequency range of 3.3–4.2 GHz, the isolation is better than 24 dB and the stable radiation patterns have an average boresight gain of 9.14 dBi. articleTitle: Interference-Induced Voltage Estimation for EMI Characteristics Evaluation of Implantable Medical Devices Exposed to 5G Frequency Radio Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to assess the interference effects in the micro/millimeter wave bands of the 5G, which is rapidly becoming popular in recent years, we have a newly developed monitoring tool for interference voltage induced in the pacemaker connector that can be used for a validation study of numerical simulations. We evaluated interference voltages under near-field exposure in 5G FR1 frequency bands.

articleTitle: Classification of Shaped Sub-reflector Design for Spherical Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium On Antennas And Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The spherical reflector antenna is requested for multibeam radiation performance for 5G mobile and satellite communications. This classification of sub-reflector design for a spherical reflector antenna configuration is presented in this paper. The classification is using the constant path length principle as derived and developed in [1] using the parallel incident rays, concentrated at the feed horn position. From the principle, the possible antenna configurations of a spherical reflector antenna with three types of shaped sub-reflector are identified. The shaped sub-reflector is designed and analyzed in MATLAB simulation at 12.5GHz for satellite communications.
